   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2024/3101 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 27 November 2024 amending Directive 2005/35/EC as regards ship-source pollution and on the introduction of administrative penalties for infringements», the European Union directive on penalties for ships that discharge pollution at sea. Its stated purpose: «The purpose of this Directive is to incorporate into Union law international standards on pollution from ships and to ensure that any company or other legal or natural person liable for illegal discharges of polluting substances is subject to effective, proportionate and dissuasive administrative penalties in order to improve maritime safety and to enhance protection of the marine environment from pollution from ships.» Its reach: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» What the Directive requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive changes an earlier directive: «Directive 2005/35/EC is amended as follows:». It sets what counts as a breach: «Member States shall ensure that discharges of polluting substances into any of the areas set out in Article 3(1) are regarded as infringements, unless:». It widens the list of substances to include residue from exhaust gas cleaning systems: «“polluting substances” means substances subject to regulation by Annex I (oil), Annex II (noxious liquid substances in bulk), Annex III (harmful substances carried by sea in packaged form), Annex IV (sewage from ships) and Annex V (garbage from ships) to Marpol 73/78 and Exhaust Gas Cleaning System residue». It names who is fined: «“company” means the shipowner or any other organisation or person, such as the manager or the bareboat charterer, which has assumed the responsibility for the operation of the ship from the shipowner.» The Directive enters into force as its final articles state: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* the Directive binds Member States, which must put the penalty system into national law; it names no duty on a forwarder or a shipper. A freight business meets it through the company that operates the ship carrying its cargo, because the fines are imposed on that company (Article 8(2), quoted in section 8).

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight business within the next 30 days. The date that matters is the national deadline: «Member States shall adopt and publish, by 6 July 2027, the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.» That duty is the Member States', not the freight business's.

- A carrier-contract lead adds a question to the next ocean carrier rate-agreement review, and in any case before 6 July 2027: does the carrier's contract say who bears an administrative fine imposed on the ship's operating company for an illegal discharge, and can it be charged to the cargo party?
- A compliance lead lists, when each Member State's national law is published after 6 July 2027, the penalty rules of the Member States whose ports the business's ocean carriers call at.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on Article 8(2), under which fines are «imposed on the company held liable for the infringement» (section 8), and on the national deadline above. The Directive states no fine amount, no surcharge and no pass-through of a fine to a customer. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a fine on a ship's operating company can be charged to a cargo owner or forwarder under the business's contracts and under national law.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive names the Member States, their competent authorities and the flag State, the Commission with the European Maritime Safety Agency, and the company that operates the ship. On inspection the text says: «The competent authorities of that Member State and of the flag State shall be informed.» On liability it says: «Each Member State shall take all necessary measures to ensure that any company, or other legal or natural person having committed an infringement within the meaning of paragraph 1 is held liable.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder, a shipper and a cargo owner are not named. Their position in the chain is indirect: the duty sits with the ship's operating company and with Member States. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any party other than the shipowner, the manager or the bareboat charterer can be held liable under the national law that carries out Article 4.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Directive. Section 6 notes the one kind of Commission act the text allows.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Commission may set reporting detail: «the Commission may, by means of implementing acts, lay down detailed rules on the procedure for reporting the information referred to in paragraph 2, including specifying the type of information to be reported.» The text gives that act no date. It sets a target for Member States' use of satellite alerts: «by 6 July 2030, ensure that competent authorities digitally analyse all high-confidence alerts and indicate whether or not they verify those high-confidence alerts sent by CleanSeaNet every year, striving to verify at least 25 % of those high-confidence alerts». A review follows: «By 6 July 2032, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of this Directive.» and, as part of it, «the Commission shall assess the possibility of modifying the scope of this Directive, if appropriate, in view of new or updated international standards for the prevention of pollution from ships subject to present and future provisions in Marpol 73/78, such as marine plastic litter, container loss and loss of plastic pellets.»

*Analytical inference:* the 2030 date is a target for authorities, not a deadline for a company, and the 2032 evaluation is the point where the scope could change, with container loss named as one subject to assess; the text states no outcome. A forwarder that books container space would watch that evaluation.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Two definitions decide who and what is caught. A ship is wide: «“ship” means a seagoing vessel, irrespective of its flag, of any type whatsoever operating in the marine environment». The liable party is the company defined in section 2, and the text adds that the shipowner may hand responsibility on: «which has assumed the responsibility for the operation of the ship from the shipowner».

*Analytical inference:* the definition reaches a ship of any flag and type, and it reaches a manager or bareboat charterer that has taken over operation of the ship. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a party that only books cargo space falls inside the word company, which the text does not say.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Infringements (Article 4). «Member States shall ensure that discharges of polluting substances into any of the areas set out in Article 3(1) are regarded as infringements, unless:» the discharge meets the listed conditions. «Each Member State shall take all necessary measures to ensure that any company, or other legal or natural person having committed an infringement within the meaning of paragraph 1 is held liable.»

Inspection (Article 6). «If irregularities or information give rise to a suspicion that a ship which is voluntarily within a port or at an off-shore terminal of a Member State has been engaged in or is engaging in a discharge of polluting substances into any of the areas referred to in Article 3(1), that Member State shall ensure that an appropriate inspection or other appropriate action, taking into account the relevant guidelines adopted by the IMO, is undertaken in accordance with its national law.»

Penalties (Articles 8 and 8d). «Member States shall lay down a system of administrative penalties within the meaning of their national legal system for the breach of national provisions implementing Article 4 of this Directive and shall ensure that they are applied. The administrative penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.» «Member States shall ensure that administrative penalties introduced in transposition of this Directive include fines which are imposed on the company held liable for the infringement.» Authorities weigh circumstances, among them «(d) the financial capacity of the company or other legal or natural person liable» and «(h) any previous ship-source pollution infringement by the company or other legal or natural person liable.» The floor: «Member States shall not set or apply administrative penalties for infringements under this Directive at a level that is too low to ensure the effectiveness, proportionality and dissuasive nature of those penalties.»

*Analytical inference:* each duty above sits on a Member State; the cost to a company is a fine set by national law, and the text states no amount, no rate, and no pass-through to cargo. No phase-in is stated in Articles 4, 6, 8 and 8d. No exceptions are stated in Articles 8 and 8d. No scope limits are stated in Articles 8 and 8d.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether, and in which Member States, a fine on a ship's operating company can be passed to a forwarder or its client.

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 9.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Directive sets penalty rules for ship pollution, not rules for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reporting runs from Member States to the Commission. «The Commission shall establish an electronic reporting tool, for the purposes of collection and exchange of information between Member States and the Commission on the implementation of the enforcement system provided for by this Directive.» Penalties are reported yearly: «information relating to penalties imposed in accordance with this Directive, once the administrative and, where applicable, legal proceedings are concluded, without undue delay and in any case by 30 June each year for penalties imposed during the previous calendar year.» The Commission publishes the result: «the Commission shall make publicly available a regularly updated Union-wide overview on the implementation and enforcement of this Directive, upon the conclusion of the administrative and legal proceedings, when applicable.» For each confirmed incident the overview carries «(b) identification of the ship involved in the incident;» and «(i) details of the administrative penalty imposed.»

*Analytical inference:* the overview is a public place where a confirmed incident, the ship and the penalty can be read together; the registration and reporting duties fall on Member States and the Commission, and none on a forwarder is stated.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Directive asks authorities to build the systems, and states no system for a freight business to build. It also asks Member States to inform communities: «Member States shall ensure that information on major ship-source pollution incidents is disseminated to the fishing and coastal communities concerned in a timely manner.»

- A carrier-selection lead records, at each ocean carrier onboarding or contract renewal after 6 July 2027, whether the carrier's terms address fines under the national law that carries out Article 8.
- A reporting lead checks, each time the Commission updates the Union-wide overview, whether a ship the business's carriers use appears with a confirmed incident.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the overview described in section 10 and on the fines on the operating company in section 8. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client contract allows a carrier's penalty record to be used in carrier selection.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

A discharge is not an infringement where it meets the conditions of the international rules, for example for oil: «for polluting substances subject to regulation by Annex I to Marpol 73/78, those discharges satisfy the conditions set out in Annex I Regulations 15, 34, 4.1, 4.2 or 4.3 to Marpol 73/78 and section 1.1.1 of part II-A of the International Code for Ships Operating in Polar Waters (“Polar Code”)». A Member State with no coast is excused part of the duty: «Member States without direct access to the sea or without seaports shall not be obliged to transpose and implement Article 6 and Article 7(2) of this Directive.» Stricter national rules stay possible: «This Directive does not prevent Member States from taking more stringent measures in conformity with Union and international law, by providing for administrative or criminal penalties in accordance with their national law.»

*Analytical inference:* the same discharge can therefore be treated differently by a Member State that applies stricter measures. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular discharge on a client's route meets the listed conditions.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no adjacent industry research or alternative is held for this Directive.*

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 27 November 2024: Directive adopted at Strasbourg
- 6 July 2027: Member States adopt and publish the national laws that carry out the Directive, and notify the Commission of the provisions adopted for the court route to penalties
- 6 July 2030: target year for authorities to analyse high-confidence satellite alerts and strive to verify at least 25 % of them
- 6 July 2032: Commission evaluation of the Directive, including the scope question

The Directive enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal; the text states no calendar date for that day.

## 15. Sources

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «The New Heavy Duty Vehicles (Carbon Dioxide Emission Performance Standards) (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2020», a United Kingdom Statutory Instrument. Its jurisdiction is the United Kingdom: «From 1 January 2021, the Secretary of State must monitor the data specified in Part A of Annex 1 relating to new heavy-duty vehicles registered for the first time in the United Kingdom.» The explanatory note says what it amends: «These Regulations amend Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 of the European Parliament and of the Council» and the rules «which sets emission performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles». What the Regulations say is taken from their own text. What it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulations move a European Union rule on truck carbon dioxide into United Kingdom law. The explanatory note gives the reason: «in order to address failures of retained EU law to operate effectively and other deficiencies» and the cause is «arising from the withdrawal of the UK from the European Union». The changes replace the Commission with the Secretary of State: «For “Commission” substitute “Secretary of State”.» They also replace the Union with the United Kingdom: «For “Union fleet” substitute “UK fleet”.» The objective is restated as a national one: «In order to contribute to the United Kingdom’s target of achieving net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050». Manufacturers are given duties of their own: «By 30 September each year, starting in 2021, manufacturers must report to the Secretary of State those data of the previous reporting period of 1 July to 30 June.» The captured text gives a commencement rule: «This regulation and regulations 19 to 24 come into force on the day after the day on which these Regulations are made.» and «The remainder of these Regulations come into force on IP completion day.»

*Analytical inference:* the duties sit on manufacturers of heavy-duty vehicles and on the Secretary of State; a freight business that runs such vehicles is not named. The text states no cost to a vehicle buyer.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in the Regulations falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days, and the text states no cost, fee or penalty for one. The recurring dated step that touches a vehicle buyer is the yearly publication: «By 30 April 2022 and in each subsequent year, the Secretary of State must publish a list indicating:» (the replaced Article 11 is headed publication of data and manufacturer performance).

- A fleet-procurement lead reads the list the Secretary of State publishes under Article 11 each year after 30 April, before the next order for new heavy-duty vehicles is placed, and files it with the purchase record.
- A pricing lead records, at the next road rate review, that these Regulations state no surcharge or pass-through, and that the only sums in them are the Article 8 amounts of £3,830 and £6,130, whose unit and trigger the captured text does not give.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the yearly publication and on the Article 8 substitution. The Regulations require neither of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* what the Article 8 amounts are charged for and on whom, under Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 as it now stands in United Kingdom law.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulations name the Secretary of State, manufacturers of heavy-duty vehicles, Parliament, and the Department for Transport. Manufacturers hold the reporting duty: «Each manufacturer must appoint a contact point for the purpose of reporting data in accordance with this Regulation.» Other public bodies appear: «In paragraph 2, for “national authorities” substitute “other agencies of the Secretary of State”.» The monitoring of registrations is the Secretary of State's own duty (Section 1). A forwarder is not named.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits outside the compliance chain; it meets the rules in the vehicles it buys. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any vehicle purchase contract of the business passes a manufacturer's reporting or target duty to the business.

*Analytical inference:* the 31 December 2027 date is a latest date for the Secretary of State to make regulations if the power is used, not a duty on a freight business. ## 8. Substantive Requirements

Monitoring by the Secretary of State. «From 1 January 2021, the Secretary of State must monitor the data specified in Part A of Annex 1 relating to new heavy-duty vehicles registered for the first time in the United Kingdom.»

Reporting by manufacturers. «By 30 September each year, starting in 2021, manufacturers must report to the Secretary of State those data of the previous reporting period of 1 July to 30 June.» «From the starting years set out in point 1 of Part B of Annex I, manufacturers of heavy-duty vehicles must monitor the data specified in point 2 of Part B of Annex 1, for each new heavy-duty vehicle.» «Each manufacturer must appoint a contact point for the purpose of reporting data in accordance with this Regulation.»

Determination and targets. «For the reporting period beginning with 1 July 2021, and for each subsequent reporting period, the Secretary of State must determine» the average emissions of a manufacturer. The Article 8 amounts change: «(b) in point (a) for “4 250 EUR” substitute “£3,830”( 2 ); (c) in point (b) for “6 800 EUR” substitute “£6,130”.» «(4) In paragraph 4, for “shall be considered as revenue for the general budget of the European Union” substitute “must be paid into the Consolidated Fund”.» The captured text states neither the unit nor the trigger of the two amounts.

Scope and conditions. «Article 2 (scope) is amended as follows.» «In paragraph 2, for “Union”, each time it occurs, substitute “United Kingdom”.» «A statutory instrument containing regulations under this Regulation is subject to annulment in pursuance of a resolution of either House of Parliament.» The date for reports in the data processing rule: «30 April each year, starting from 2022».

*Analytical inference:* each duty above falls on manufacturers or on the Secretary of State, as the text names; the Regulations state no duty and no cost for a freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* what the Article 8 amounts are charged for and on whom, and whether any manufacturer duty is passed to a buyer by contract.

*Analytical inference:* the registration and reporting duties fall on manufacturers and the Secretary of State; the text states none on a freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a manufacturer asks a buyer of its vehicles for registration data.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulations ask a freight business to build no system and state no cost or penalty. The monitoring and reporting systems are the manufacturer's: «The date of simulation must be the date reported in accordance with data entry 71 in point 2 of Part B of Annex 1.» A fleet-procurement lead can add the manufacturer's reporting under Article 4 and Article 5 as a line in the tender checklist for new heavy-duty vehicles, at the next tender, so the purchase record notes that the vehicle is covered by those manufacturer duties.

*Analytical inference:* the checklist line rests on the manufacturer reporting duties in Section 8, not on a duty of the buyer. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business may be asked for vehicle data under Part A or Part B of Annex 1.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

One edge case decides which vehicles the monitoring counts: «Data relating to new heavy-duty vehicles that were registered previously outside the United Kingdom shall not be monitored and reported, unless that registration was made less than three months before registration in the United Kingdom.» Powers to make rules are checked by Parliament: «A statutory instrument containing regulations under this Regulation is subject to annulment in pursuance of a resolution of either House of Parliament.»

*Analytical inference:* a vehicle first registered abroad and then registered in the United Kingdom more than three months later falls outside the monitoring on this wording. *Legal Confirmation Required:* how the three-month rule is applied to a vehicle a client brings into the United Kingdom.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «The Greenhouse Gas Emissions Trading Scheme (Amendment) Order 2026 Made 10th March 2026 Coming into force in accordance with article 2», a United Kingdom statutory instrument. Its jurisdiction: «This Order extends to England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.» The source states its legal basis: «This Order is made in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 44, 54 and 90(3) of, and Schedule 2 and paragraph 9 of Schedule 3 to, the Climate Change Act 2008». The text appears on legislation.gov.uk as «You are here: UK Statutory Instruments 2026 No. 278». What the Order says is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Order changes how the UK emissions trading scheme gives free allowances to industrial plants. The explanatory note sets the background: «Operators of certain industrial installations are required to monitor, submit verified reports on, and surrender “allowances” equivalent to, their greenhouse gas emissions each scheme year.» The first of three main changes: «The first main change arises as a result of the introduction of the United Kingdom Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (“UK CBAM”) from 2027. Industrial installations that operate in one of the five sectors covered by UK CBAM (cement, fertilisers, iron and steel, aluminium and hydrogen) will have their annual free allocation reduced by a set amount over the 2027-2030 allocation period». The second: «The second main change is to enable operators of incumbent installations to have their 2020, or 2020 and 2021, scheme year data excluded from the calculation of their “ historical activity levels ” (the arithmetic mean of their activity levels in the 2019-2023 scheme years) upon which their free allocation entitlement is calculated.»

It also amends two retained regulations: «Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/331 is amended in accordance with this Part.» and «Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/1842 is amended in accordance with this Part.»

The Order enters into force as its text states: «This Order comes into force on the day after the day on which it is made.» It was made on «Made 10th March 2026»

*Analytical inference:* the Order changes allowance allocation for plants in five industrial sectors; it sets no duty, fee or charge on a freight business and states no pass-through of any cost to cargo owners. Freight is touched only as the carrier of goods from those sectors (section 7).

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The nearest dated step in the text binds the UK ETS authority: «Where article 34A(1A) applies, the UK ETS authority must publish— (a) the allocation table referred to in article 34A(1A)(a) as soon as reasonably practicable after it is compiled and in any event before 1st January 2027; and (b) the updated allocation table referred to in article 34A(1A)(b) as soon as reasonably practicable after it is compiled and in any event before 1st January 2028.» The sectors covered by the UK carbon border rules are: «Five tables are provided below and are split by sector covering the following sectors: cement, fertilisers, iron and steel, aluminium and hydrogen.»

- When a contract for cement, fertiliser, iron and steel, aluminium or hydrogen cargo is next renewed in 2027, a pricing lead asks the shipper whether any UK CBAM cost is expected to be added to the cargo price.

*Analytical inference:* the question rests on the five covered sectors and on the cut to free allowances for plants in those sectors; the Order itself states no pass-through to customers. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a UK CBAM cost can reach a freight customer under its contract is not stated in this Order and needs counsel.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The duty holders named are operators of installations, the regulator and the UK ETS authority. The scheme's background duty: «Operators of certain industrial installations are required to monitor, submit verified reports on, and surrender “allowances” equivalent to, their greenhouse gas emissions each scheme year.» The monitoring plan duty: «Where the operator has any relevant product benchmark sub-installation, relevant heat benchmark sub-installation, relevant fuel benchmark sub-installation or any relevant process emissions sub-installation within the meaning of Article 4(9), the operator must modify the monitoring methodology plan to reflect the boundaries of the sub-installation that apply as a result of the requirement in Article 10(4a).» The authority's table duty: «as soon as reasonably practicable after approval under Article 16b of the Free Allocation Regulation of the final annual number of allowances to be allocated in 2027, compile an allocation table for the 2027-2030 allocation period which contains entries for the 2027 scheme year only»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder, carrier or shipper is not named; a freight business meets the Order only as a seller or mover of goods from the covered sectors. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that holds a producer's goods in transit takes on any role under the free allocation rules.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text sets dated steps for the UK ETS authority and the regulator. Table publication: «in any event before 1st January 2027» and «in any event before 1st January 2028». The factor orders: «for scheme year 2027, unless otherwise provided for on or before 31 December 2026 by way of an order under Part 3 of the Climate Change Act 2008, 0.975»; «for scheme year 2028, unless otherwise provided for on or before 31 December 2027 by way of an order under Part 3 of the Climate Change Act 2008, 0.95»; «for scheme year 2029, unless otherwise provided for on or before 31 December 2028 by way of an order under Part 3 of the Climate Change Act 2008, 0.9»; «for scheme year 2030, unless otherwise provided for on or before 31 December 2029 by way of an order under Part 3 of the Climate Change Act 2008, 0.775». If benchmarks are not adopted: «no earlier than 1 October 2027», and the correction factor step «the calculation referred to in paragraphs 2 to 4 must occur on or after 1 November 2027». The explanatory note puts it differently: «Where the UK ETS Authority does not adopt updated benchmarks for the 2028, 2029 and 2030 scheme years by 30 September 2027, the existing Annex 8 benchmarks will apply». A past step on another regulation: «the reporting requirement in Article 3(1a) (which will come into force on 1st January 2026)».

*Analytical inference:* the explanatory note speaks of 30 September 2027 while the operative articles use 30 September 2026 as the cut-off and 1 October 2027 as the earliest calculation date, so the operative articles are the better guide to timing. The next dated step for the UK ETS authority is the table publication before the end of 2026.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Whether a plant's process counts as serving UK CBAM goods turns on Annex 9: «Five tables are provided below and are split by sector covering the following sectors: cement, fertilisers, iron and steel, aluminium and hydrogen.» The operator must tell them apart: «the operator must, after following the relevant steps in paragraphs 3 and 4, clearly distinguish on the basis of the product benchmarks and PRODCOM codes listed in Annex 9 whether or not the relevant process serves the production of a UK CBAM good.» A threshold removes the duty: «Where at least 95 % of the activity level of the product benchmark sub-installations, of the heat benchmark sub-installations, of the fuel benchmark sub-installations or of the process emissions sub-installations, serve the production of a UK CBAM good or where at least 95 % of the activity level of the product benchmark sub-installations, of the heat benchmark sub-installations, of the fuel benchmark sub-installations or of the process emissions sub-installations do not serve the production of a UK CBAM good, the operator is exempted from providing data allowing for the distinction in terms of UK CBAM status.»

*Analytical inference:* only plants in the five sectors are caught, so a freight business is affected, if at all, through shipments from those plants. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular shipped good falls within the Annex 9 lists.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Monitoring plan. «Where the operator has any relevant product benchmark sub-installation, relevant heat benchmark sub-installation, relevant fuel benchmark sub-installation or any relevant process emissions sub-installation within the meaning of Article 4(9), the operator must modify the monitoring methodology plan to reflect the boundaries of the sub-installation that apply as a result of the requirement in Article 10(4a).» The timing: «the operator must notify the regulator of the modification of the monitoring methodology plan on or before 30th September 2026; (b) the modification of the monitoring methodology plan is subject to approval by the regulator; (c) once approved, the modification will take effect on 1st January 2027.»

Second stage of the application. «the second stage is that in the period beginning with 1 April 2026 and ending with 30 June 2026, the operator must: (i) notify the regulator in writing that the operator wishes the application to proceed;»

UK CBAM split. «the operator must, after following the relevant steps in paragraphs 3 and 4, clearly distinguish on the basis of the product benchmarks and PRODCOM codes listed in Annex 9 whether or not the relevant process serves the production of a UK CBAM good.»

Reduction factors for UK CBAM sub-installations. «The factor to be applied in the 2027-2030 allocation period is: (a) for scheme year 2027, unless otherwise provided for on or before 31 December 2026 by way of an order under Part 3 of the Climate Change Act 2008, 0.975; (b) for scheme year 2028, unless otherwise provided for on or before 31 December 2027 by way of an order under Part 3 of the Climate Change Act 2008, 0.95; (c) for scheme year 2029, unless otherwise provided for on or before 31 December 2028 by way of an order under Part 3 of the Climate Change Act 2008, 0.9; (d) for scheme year 2030, unless otherwise provided for on or before 31 December 2029 by way of an order under Part 3 of the Climate Change Act 2008, 0.775.»

Benchmarks. «for incumbent installations applying for free allocation in the 2027-2030 allocation period: (i) in respect of the calculation of the preliminary annual number of allowances for the 2027 scheme year, the benchmarks set out in Annex 8» A fallback: «but if no benchmarks for the 2028, 2029 and 2030 scheme years are adopted by way of an order under Part 3 of the Climate Change Act 2008 ( 3 ) before the regulator is required to calculate the preliminary annual number of allowances to be allocated for the 2028, 2029 and 2030 scheme years, the benchmarks for the 2027 scheme year are to be used for the calculation.»

Timing if benchmarks are late. «Where the benchmarks for the 2028, 2029 and 2030 scheme years have not been adopted under paragraph 13(b)(ii) on or before 30 September 2026, the regulator must: (a) calculate the preliminary annual number of allowances to be allocated in respect of the installation for the 2027 scheme year; and (b) no earlier than 1 October 2027, calculate the preliminary annual number of allowances to be allocated in respect of the installation for the 2028, 2029 and 2030 scheme years.» The correction factor calculation: «the calculation referred to in paragraphs 2 to 4 must occur on or after 1 November 2027»

New entrants. «but Article 16(15) to (17) does not apply to this calculation»

Allocation tables. «Where article 34A(1A) applies, the UK ETS authority must publish— (a) the allocation table referred to in article 34A(1A)(a) as soon as reasonably practicable after it is compiled and in any event before 1st January 2027; and (b) the updated allocation table referred to in article 34A(1A)(b) as soon as reasonably practicable after it is compiled and in any event before 1st January 2028.»

*Analytical inference:* each requirement above falls on an installation operator, the regulator or the UK ETS authority; the text names no obligation on a business that ships the goods. This rests on the duty holders named in the quoted articles. No price pass-through of allowance cost is stated.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any UK CBAM or free allocation rule creates a charge or reporting request that reaches a forwarder; the Order is silent on it.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Operators notify the regulator in writing: «the second stage is that in the period beginning with 1 April 2026 and ending with 30 June 2026, the operator must: (i) notify the regulator in writing that the operator wishes the application to proceed;» Monitoring plan changes are notified: «the operator must notify the regulator of the modification of the monitoring methodology plan on or before 30th September 2026; (b) the modification of the monitoring methodology plan is subject to approval by the regulator; (c) once approved, the modification will take effect on 1st January 2027.» The UK ETS authority publishes tables: «Where article 34A(1A) applies, the UK ETS authority must publish— (a) the allocation table referred to in article 34A(1A)(a) as soon as reasonably practicable after it is compiled and in any event before 1st January 2027; and (b) the updated allocation table referred to in article 34A(1A)(b) as soon as reasonably practicable after it is compiled and in any event before 1st January 2028.»

*Analytical inference:* these notifications and publications fall on operators, the regulator and the authority; the text states none on a freight business.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Order requires no system from a freight business. The system work sits with installation operators: «Where the operator has any relevant product benchmark sub-installation, relevant heat benchmark sub-installation, relevant fuel benchmark sub-installation or any relevant process emissions sub-installation within the meaning of Article 4(9), the operator must modify the monitoring methodology plan to reflect the boundaries of the sub-installation that apply as a result of the requirement in Article 10(4a).» with the timing «the operator must notify the regulator of the modification of the monitoring methodology plan on or before 30th September 2026; (b) the modification of the monitoring methodology plan is subject to approval by the regulator; (c) once approved, the modification will take effect on 1st January 2027.»

*Analytical inference:* the 30th September 2026 notification date has passed, so a plant in the covered sectors has already had to notify its monitoring plan change; the text states no data request to businesses outside the plant.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

An operator escapes the split when almost all activity falls one way: «Where at least 95 % of the activity level of the product benchmark sub-installations, of the heat benchmark sub-installations, of the fuel benchmark sub-installations or of the process emissions sub-installations, serve the production of a UK CBAM good or where at least 95 % of the activity level of the product benchmark sub-installations, of the heat benchmark sub-installations, of the fuel benchmark sub-installations or of the process emissions sub-installations do not serve the production of a UK CBAM good, the operator is exempted from providing data allowing for the distinction in terms of UK CBAM status.» An operator may drop pandemic-affected years: «The second main change is to enable operators of incumbent installations to have their 2020, or 2020 and 2021, scheme year data excluded from the calculation of their “ historical activity levels ” (the arithmetic mean of their activity levels in the 2019-2023 scheme years) upon which their free allocation entitlement is calculated.» The hydrogen table has an exception: «Except the production of hydrogen within a refinery or organic chemical installation and where this hydrogen is exclusively used within that refinery or installation»

*Analytical inference:* the 95 % rule and the hydrogen exception narrow who must split sub-installations; they do not reach freight handling of the goods.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COMMISSION IMPLEMENTING DECISION (EU) 2022/197 of 17 January 2022 establishing a common fiscal marker for gas oils and kerosene», an act of the European Commission for the European Union. Its jurisdictional scope is the Union through its Member States: «This Decision is addressed to the Member States.» The recitals in Section 2 give its purpose. What the Decision says is taken from its own text. What it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Decision picks the substance that Member States use to mark these fuels. The recitals give the reason: «For the proper functioning of the internal market, and in particular to prevent tax evasion, Directive 95/60/EC provides for a common marking system to identify gas oils, falling within code 2710 00 69 of the Combined Nomenclature (CN), and kerosene, falling within CN code 2710 00 55, which have been released for consumption exempt from excise duty, or subject to a reduced excise duty rate.» The substance chosen is: «The common fiscal marker provided for by Directive 95/60/EC, for the marking of all gas oils falling within CN codes 2710 19 43, 2710 19 46, 2710 19 47, 2710 19 48, 2710 20 11, 2710 20 16 and 2710 20 19 as well as of kerosene falling within CN code 2710 19 25, shall be ACCUTRACE™ PLUS, as specified in the Annex to this Decision.» The old marker is replaced because the evaluation found shortcomings in it: «the Commission’s evaluation confirmed the usefulness of common rules for the marking of fuels that are subject to reduced excise duty rates but identified the shortcomings of Solvent Yellow 124 in terms of its lack of resilience to common removal methods.» The Decision names no freight activity and is addressed to the Member States.

*Analytical inference:* the Decision sets the marker that Member States use on gas oil and kerosene of the listed CN codes, not a duty on a transport service; if it reaches a freight business at all, it is through the fuel the business buys. The text names no forwarder or carrier.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Decision is addressed to the Member States and states no cost, fee or penalty for a freight business, so no step in it falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The nearest dated step ahead is the review of the Decision: «This Decision shall be reviewed by 31 December 2028 at the latest, taking into account technical developments in the field of marking systems and the need to counteract fraudulent use of energy products exempt from excise duty or subject to a reduced excise duty rate.»

- A fuel-procurement lead asks, at the next renewal of each contract for gas oil or kerosene, which fiscal marker the fuel carries and at what marking level, and compares the answer with the marker and levels in Article 1.
- A compliance lead sets a reminder to read the outcome of the Commission's review before the end of 2028, because that review can change the marker.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on Article 1 (the marker and its level) and Article 3 (the review). The Decision requires neither of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the fuel the business buys falls in the CN codes of Article 1 and which national rules of the Member State of supply apply to its marking.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Decision names the Member States, the Commission and the Committee on Excise Duty: «The measures provided for in this Decision are in accordance with the opinion of the Committee on Excise Duty». Marker suppliers appear in the recitals: «For all candidate markers, the Commission requested and received, form the suppliers, the maximum selling price for the markers and their yearly indexation methods.» The Decision itself fixes the marker; the duty to set the marking level falls on the Member States (Section 8). A forwarder or carrier is not named.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits outside the compliance chain of this Decision; if it meets the marker at all, it is in fuel it buys under the national rules of a Member State. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any customer or carrier contract of the business passes a marking duty or a marker cost to the business.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Decision sets its own follow-up steps. The scheduled review: «This Decision shall be reviewed by 31 December 2028 at the latest, taking into account technical developments in the field of marking systems and the need to counteract fraudulent use of energy products exempt from excise duty or subject to a reduced excise duty rate.» An earlier review can be triggered: «An earlier review shall be undertaken if it is found that ACCUTRACE™ PLUS gives rise to tax evasion or causes health or environmental damage.»

*Analytical inference:* the review is the point at which the marker could be changed again, as it was here. The text states no content for the review beyond what it takes into account. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Commission has since opened a review.

## 7. Threshold Questions

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Marker and level. «The common fiscal marker provided for by Directive 95/60/EC, for the marking of all gas oils falling within CN codes 2710 19 43, 2710 19 46, 2710 19 47, 2710 19 48, 2710 20 11, 2710 20 16 and 2710 20 19 as well as of kerosene falling within CN code 2710 19 25, shall be ACCUTRACE™ PLUS, as specified in the Annex to this Decision.» «Member States shall set a marking level of ACCUTRACE™ PLUS at least 12,5 milligram per litre and not more than 18,75 milligram per litre of energy product.» The recitals tie the marker to the Directive: «ACCUTRACE™ PLUS should be established instead of Solvent Yellow 124 as the common fiscal marker within the meaning of Directive 95/60/EC subject to the conditions set out in that Directive.»

Transition. «Member States may use either Solvent Yellow 124 or ACCUTRACE™ PLUS as the common fiscal marker within the meaning of Directive 95/60/EC during a transitional period ending on 18 January 2024.» «If they use Solvent Yellow 124 as the common fiscal marker in that transitional period, Member States shall set a marking level of at least 6 mg and not more than 9 mg of Solvent Yellow 124 per litre of energy product.» That period has passed.

Review and repeal. Article 3 sets the review by 31 December 2028 (Section 6). «Implementing Decision (EU) 2017/74 is repealed.»

*Analytical inference:* the marker is fixed by the Decision and the duty to set the marking level falls on the Member States; the Decision states no duty, cost or price effect for a freight business. No phase-in is stated in Articles 1 and 3. No scope limits are stated in Articles 2 to 5.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which national rules set the marking of gas oil and kerosene in each Member State where the business buys fuel, and whether any of them reaches the business or its suppliers.

Obligations surveyed: 4; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 6.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: the Decision sets a fuel marker for Member States, not a product a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Decision sets no registration or reporting obligation on a freight business. The one reporting step is the Commission's own: the review in Article 3. The recitals add that the marker can be supplied under licence: «The availability of ACCUTRACE™ PLUS, despite it being under patent cover in the Union, should be secured, where appropriate, by licensing agreements.»

*Analytical inference:* the licence recital concerns the supply of the marker to Member States, not a registration by a freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any national rule in a Member State of supply asks a purchaser of marked fuel to keep records.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Decision asks a freight business to build no system, and states no cost or penalty. A fuel-procurement lead can keep a contract-by-contract list of the fuel marker named for each purchase of gas oil or kerosene, updated at each contract renewal, so that the 2028 review can be read against the marker actually in use. A pricing lead can note, at the next fuel cost review, that the Decision states no marker cost and no price effect, so none is built into a rate on its authority.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the absence of a stated cost in the Decision and on Article 1. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a contract of the business for gas oil or kerosene carries any term on fiscal marking.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Decision makes one allowance for a period that has passed: «Member States may use either Solvent Yellow 124 or ACCUTRACE™ PLUS as the common fiscal marker within the meaning of Directive 95/60/EC during a transitional period ending on 18 January 2024.» The recitals give the reason: «to allow Member States to exhaust existing stocks of the current marker Solvent Yellow 124, a transitional period of 24 months should be allowed.» The Decision also states: «This Decision does not release any undertaking from its obligations under Article 102 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.»

*Analytical inference:* the transitional allowance is for Member States, not a freight business, and it has ended. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether fuel marked with the old marker is still still carried by fuel the business buys in a Member State.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

The recitals record how the new marker was chosen: «The candidate markers proposed by suppliers were thoroughly investigated from a technical standpoint with the assistance of the Joint Research Centre to check their resilience to the most common illegal removal techniques.» Another body supports the finding: «fuel laundering also resulted in serious environmental pollution due to the use of chemicals such as sulfuric acid, chloric acid and bleaching earth and the illegal dumping of waste products and oil sludge in nature, agricultural land or public roads.»

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

The captured text states no separate date on which the Decision enters into force; it is dated by its closing line: «Done at Brussels, 17 January 2022.»

- 17 January 2022: Decision adopted
- 18 January 2024: transitional period ends, after which the Decision lets Member States use that marker alone (date passed)
- 31 December 2028: latest date for the review of the Decision

*Analytical inference:* the transitional period has passed; the review is the dated step still ahead, and it runs on the Commission, not on a freight business.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2022/2400 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 23 November 2022 amending Annexes IV and V to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 on persistent organic pollutants», a regulation of the European Union. Its jurisdictional scope is every Member State: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» It sets concentration limits for chemicals in waste. What the Regulation says is taken from its own text. What it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation adds new chemicals to the Union's waste limits for persistent organic pollutants and changes some existing ones. The recital gives the reason: «In view of those amendments to the Convention and to ensure that waste containing those substances is managed in accordance with the provisions of the Convention, it is necessary also to amend Annexes IV and V to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 by including pentachlorophenol, dicofol and PFOA, its salts and PFOA-related compounds, as well as PFHxS, its salts and PFHxS-related compounds in the Annexes and indicating their corresponding concentration limits.» Existing limits are changed too: «it is appropriate to amend the concentration limits in Annex IV for those substances to adapt their limit values to scientific and technical progress.» The amending step is: «Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 is amended as follows:». The dates of coming into effect: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . This Regulation shall apply from 10 June 2023.»

*Analytical inference:* the Regulation sets limits that apply to waste containing the named chemicals; the goods that reach a freight business are consignments of such waste, and the text does not name a forwarder or carrier.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in the Regulation falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days and the text states no cost or penalty. The nearest dated step ahead is on 30 December 2027: «(c) from 30 December 2027, 200 mg/kg or, if higher, the sum of the concentration of those substances where they are present in mixtures or articles», and the Commission review of several limits is set for the same date: «The Commission shall review that concentration limit and shall, where appropriate, adopt a legislative proposal to lower that value, where such lowering is feasible in accordance with scientific and technical progress, no later than 30 December 2027.»

- A customer-compliance lead asks each client that consigns waste, at the booking of each such consignment, whether the waste contains pentachlorophenol, dicofol, PFOA, PFHxS or the other substances in Annex IV, and records the client's answer with the booking.
- A compliance lead checks, before 30 December 2027, whether the Commission has adopted a legislative proposal to lower the limits it was to review by that date, because the lower values would change the answer a client gives.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the Annex IV limits for waste and on the 2027 review date. The Regulation requires neither of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular consignment of waste is within Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 and which limit in Annex IV or Annex V applies to it.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the Commission, the Member States, and companies and competent authorities. Member States gather data: «In order to enable Member States to collect data on the actual amount of PCDD/PCDF and of dioxin-like polychlorinated biphenyls (dl-PCBs) in ashes and soot from private households, as well as in fly ashes from biomass units for heat and power production». Companies get time: «It is appropriate to provide for a sufficient period of time to allow companies and competent authorities to adapt to the new requirements.» The Commission has a task: «The Commission shall assess whether it would be appropriate to amend Directive 2008/98/EC or Decision 2000/532/EC, or both, to recognise that waste containing any persistent organic pollutants exceeding the concentration limits specified in Annex IV to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 is to be classified as hazardous». A forwarder is not named.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits outside the named compliance chain; it meets the limits in the waste its clients consign. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any contract of the business with a waste client or with the receiving site passes a limit-value duty to the business.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Regulation sets its own follow-up steps. The Commission assessment on hazardous classification has a relative date: «not later than 36 months after entry into force of this Regulation, shall put forward a legislative proposal to amend Directive 2008/98/EC or a proposal to amend Decision 2000/532/EC, or both, accordingly.» The review of limit values has a calendar date: «no later than 30 December 2027». The recitals say of information on ashes and soot: «That information should be made available no later than 1 July 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* the 1 July 2026 date has passed; the review in 2027 is ahead and could lower limits, as the textile recital states for PFOA. The captured text states no calendar date for the 36 month step because it runs from entry into force, which the text sets as the twentieth day after publication. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Commission has since put forward the hazardous classification proposal.

## 7. Threshold Questions

One calculation decides which figure a result is compared with for dioxin-like compounds: «The limit is calculated as the sum of PCDD, PCDF and dl-PCBs according to the toxic equivalency factors (TEFs) set out in Part 2, in the third paragraph, in the table, of Annex V.» The recital explains the grouping: «it is appropriate to include dl-PCBs within the existing group entry for PCDD/PCDF in Annexes IV and V to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021.»

*Analytical inference:* a measured result for these compounds is compared with the limit as a weighted sum, not as single substances. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party must obtain the result for a consignment of waste.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Limits in Annex IV. New rows: «Pentachlorophenol, its salts and esters 87-86-5 and others 201-778-6 and others 100 mg/kg». «Dicofol 115-32-2 204-082-0 50 mg/kg». «Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), its salts and PFOA-related compounds, as set out in Annex I 335-67-1 and others 206-397-9 and others 1 mg/kg (PFOA and its salts), 40 mg/kg (sum of PFOA-related compounds)». «Perfluorohexane sulfonic acid (PFHxS), its salts and PFHxS-related compounds 355-46-4 and others 355-46-4 and others 1 mg/kg (PFHxS and its salts), 40 mg/kg (sum of PFHxS-related compounds)». Replaced rows: «Alkanes C 10 -C 13 , chloro (short-chain chlorinated paraffins) (SCCPs) 85535-84-8 287-476-5 1 500 mg/kg». «Polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/PCDF) and dioxin-like polychlorinated biphenyls (dl-PCBs) 5 μg/kg». «Hexabromocyclododecane ( 2 ) 25637-99-4, 3194-55-6, 134237-50-6, 134237-51-7, 134237-52-8 247-148-4 221-695-9 500 mg/kg».

Stepped limit for brominated diphenyl ethers. «Sum of the concentrations of tetrabromodiphenyl ether C 12 H 6 Br 4 O, pentabromodiphenyl ether C 12 H 5 Br 5 O, hexabromodiphenyl ether C 12 H 4 Br 6 O, heptabromodiphenyl ether C 12 H 3 Br 7 O and decabromodiphenyl ether C 12 Br 10 O: (a) until 29 December 2027, 500 mg/kg; (b) from 30 December 2025 until 28 December 2027, 350 mg/kg, or, if higher, the sum of the concentration of those substances where they are present in mixtures or articles, as set out in the fourth column, point 2, of Annex I for the substances tetrabromodiphenyl ether, pentabromodiphenyl ether, hexabromodiphenyl ether, heptabromodiphenyl ether and decabromodiphenyl ether; (c) from 30 December 2027, 200 mg/kg or, if higher, the sum of the concentration of those substances where they are present in mixtures or articles, as set out in the fourth column, point 2, of Annex I for the substances tetrabromodiphenyl ether, pentabromodiphenyl ether, hexabromodiphenyl ether, heptabromodiphenyl ether and decabromodiphenyl ether.».

Transitional provision for ashes. «A value of 10 μg/kg shall apply to fly ashes from biomass units for heat and power production containing or contaminated by polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/PCDF) and dioxin-like polychlorinated biphenyl (dl-PCBs) as listed in Annex IV until 30 December 2023. The value of 5 μg/kg provided for in Annex IV shall apply to fly ashes from biomass units for heat and power production from 31 December 2023.»

Limits in Annex V. «Pentachlorophenol, its salts and esters: 1 000 mg/kg; Dicofol: 5 000 mg/kg; Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), its salts and PFOA-related compounds: 50 mg/kg (PFOA and its salts), 2 000 mg/kg (PFOA-related compounds); Perfluorohexane sulfonic acid (PFHxS), its salts and PFHxS-related compounds: 50 mg/kg (PFHxS and its salts), 2 000 mg/kg (PFHxS-related compounds).» The waste codes list is widened: «the following text is inserted after ‘10.01 Wastes from power stations and other combustion plants (except 19)’: ‘10 01 03: fly ash from peat and untreated wood’».

*Analytical inference:* each limit above is a concentration limit that Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 attaches to waste; the Regulation states no duty, cost or price effect for a freight business. No phase-in is stated outside the stepped limits above. No scope limits are stated in Articles 2 and 3.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* what Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 requires once waste exceeds a limit in Annex IV or Annex V, and who carries that duty for a consignment.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Regulation sets no registration obligation on a freight business. The recitals speak of data on ashes and soot: «That information should be made available no later than 1 July 2026.» The Commission reviews values: «The Commission shall review that concentration limit and shall, where appropriate, adopt a legislative proposal to lower that value to not higher than 200 mg/kg no later than 30 December 2027.» The recital behind the data step reads: «Members States should collect information on the presence of PCDD/PCDF and dl-PCBs in ashes and soot from private households and fly ashes from biomass units for heat and power production.»

*Analytical inference:* the data step is a recital statement about Member States and the review is the Commission's own; the text states no reporting step on a freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a Member State asks a consignor of waste to report concentration results.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks a freight business to build no system and states no cost or penalty. A customer-compliance lead can add a line to the intake form for waste consignments, at the next form revision, asking the client to state whether the waste holds a substance listed in Annex IV and the concentration the client has measured, so the answer sits with the booking before the 30 December 2027 step. A pricing lead can note, at the next rate review for waste consignments, that the Regulation states no surcharge or pass-through.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the Annex IV limits; the Regulation requires neither of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether holding a client's concentration statement is enough for the business, or whether a Member State asks for a measured result from a named method.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Regulation holds transitional values in a new article: «A value of 15 μg/kg shall continue to apply for ashes and soot from private households containing or contaminated by polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/PCDF) as listed in Annex IV until 31 December 2024.» From the next year the lower value applies: «the value of 5 μg/kg provided for in Annex IV shall apply from 1 January 2025.» The recital gives the reason for the later start: «to afford Member States sufficient time to take measures necessary to give effect to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021, the amended concentration limit for the sum of PCDD/PCDF and dl-PCBs should, with regard to ashes and soot from private households and for fly ashes from biomass units, apply at a later stage after the entry into force of this Regulation.»

*Analytical inference:* both transitional dates have passed, so the lower values of 5 μg/kg now apply on this wording. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which value applies to a consignment of ashes or soot that left a household before the date.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

The recitals link the limits to wider policy. On textiles: «To ensure that recycled textiles are free of hazardous chemicals such as PFOA from the onset, it is necessary to strengthen limit values for PFOA, its salts and PFOA-related compounds in waste since their presence could have an impact on the collection and treatment of textile waste.» On method: «The proposed concentration limits should be underpinned by the precautionary principle as laid down in the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union».

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

The Regulation is dated by its closing line: «Done at Strasbourg, 23 November 2022.» It enters into force as Article 3 states and applies from a fixed date: «This Regulation shall apply from 10 June 2023.»

- 23 November 2022: Regulation adopted
- 10 June 2023: Regulation applies (date passed)
- 31 December 2023: value of 5 μg/kg applies to fly ashes from biomass units (date passed)
- 31 December 2024: last day of the 15 μg/kg value for ashes and soot from private households (date passed)
- 1 January 2025: value of 5 μg/kg applies to ashes and soot from private households (date passed)
- 1 July 2026: date by which, the recital says, the ash information should be made available (date passed)
- 30 December 2027: Commission review of limit values for several substances, and the lower sum limit for brominated diphenyl ethers (200 mg/kg or, if higher, the Annex I mixture and article sum)

*Analytical inference:* the dated steps to 2026 have passed; the 2027 step is the one ahead and runs on the Commission, with the lower limit applying to waste from that date.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2024/1747 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 June 2024 amending Regulations (EU) 2019/942 and (EU) 2019/943 as regards improving the Union’s electricity market design (Text with EEA relevance)», the European Union rule that changes how wholesale electricity markets work. It is a wholesale electricity market rule: its duties fall on Member States, regulators, grid operators, market operators and the Commission, not on freight companies. Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation amends two earlier electricity regulations. Its stated aim for electricity markets: «set fundamental principles for well-functioning, integrated electricity markets, which allow all resource providers and electricity customers non-discriminatory market access, enable the development of forward electricity markets to allow suppliers and consumers to hedge or protect themselves against the risk of future volatility in electricity prices». Its recitals name electric vehicles as new demand: «to be able to address new demand such as electric vehicles and heat pumps». The Regulation enters into force as its last article states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business meets this Regulation only as an electricity customer, for example at depots, warehouses or charging sites, and through whatever price effects the market changes have on its supply contracts; the text states no freight rate or surcharge. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business with its own electricity supply contracts counts as a final customer under Articles 19a and 19d.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight business within the next 30 days. The nearest dated step that reaches electricity customers is the start of contracts for difference: «The first subparagraph shall apply to contracts under direct price support schemes for investment in new generation concluded on or after 17 July 2027, or, in the case of offshore hybrid asset projects connected to two or more bidding zones, 17 July 2029.» That duty is the Member States'.

- An energy-procurement lead checks, after 17 July 2027, how each Member State where the business holds electricity supply contracts distributes the revenues of two-way contracts for difference to final customers, and records whether they reach the business's tariff.
- A facilities lead lists, at the next electricity supply contract renewal, the depots and charging sites that buy electricity directly, so that a power purchase agreement can be assessed where the Member State has set up the guarantee instruments described in Article 19a.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on Article 19a and Article 19d (section 8). The Regulation states no electricity price, no freight rate and no surcharge. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any revenue distribution under Article 19d(5) is owed to the business as a final customer under national law.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names Member States, regulatory authorities, transmission system operators, nominated electricity market operators (NEMOs), ACER, the ENTSO for Electricity, the EU DSO entity, the Commission and final customers. It assigns national tasks to the Member State: «each Member State shall define, on the basis of that report, an indicative national objective for non-fossil flexibility, including the respective specific contributions of both demand response and energy storage to that objective.» It assigns reports to regulators: «the regulatory authority or another authority or entity designated by a Member State, shall adopt a report on the estimated flexibility needs for a period of at least the next 5 to 10 years at national level». Revenues go to customers: «Any revenues, or the equivalent in financial value of those revenues, arising from direct price support schemes in the form of two-way contracts for difference and equivalent schemes with the same effects referred to in paragraph 1 shall be distributed to final customers.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder, a carrier and a shipper are not named. Final customers is the only term that can reach a freight business, as a buyer of electricity. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that charges its own vehicles or runs refrigerated storage is a final customer under the Regulation.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Regulation. Section 6 notes the Commission and ACER steps the text sets.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Many dated steps are for the Commission and ACER, and most have passed. ACER was to look at templates: «By 17 October 2024, ACER shall assess, in close coordination with the relevant institutions and stakeholders, the need to develop and issue voluntary templates for PPAs». The Commission was to report on capacity mechanisms: «By 17 January 2025, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a detailed report assessing possibilities of streamlining and simplifying the process of applying a capacity mechanism under Chapter IV». It was to follow with proposals: «By 17 April 2025, the Commission shall, after consultation with Member States, submit proposals with a view to simplifying the process of assessing capacity mechanisms as appropriate.» ACER was to assess peak-shaving: «By 30 June 2025, ACER shall, after consulting stakeholders, assess the impact of developing peak-shaving products on the Union electricity market under normal market circumstances.» The Commission was to assess forward markets: «By 17 January 2026, the Commission shall, after consulting relevant stakeholders, carry out an assessment of the impact of possible measures to achieve the objective referred to in paragraph 3.» and to act on it: «the Commission shall, by 17 July 2026, adopt an implementing act to further specify measures and tools to achieve the objectives referred to in in paragraph 3 of this Article». It was to check power purchase markets: «By 31 January 2026 and every two years thereafter, the Commission shall assess whether barriers persist, and whether there is sufficient transparency, in the PPA markets.» And to review the Regulation: «By 30 June 2026, the Commission shall review this Regulation and shall submit a comprehensive report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the basis of that review, accompanied by a legislative proposal where appropriate.» Those dates have passed, and the captured text does not say whether each step was completed. Ahead: «By 1 December 2027, the Commission shall, after consulting NEMOs, ENTSO for Electricity, ACER and relevant stakeholders, submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council». Transmission operators with a derogation file again: «The transmission system operator concerned shall submit the request to the regulatory authority concerned, to the ENTSO for Electricity and to ACER by 30 June 2028.»

*Analytical inference:* the review report of 30 June 2026 and the report of 1 December 2027 are the points where the market rules may be changed again; the text states no outcome. The next PPA barrier assessment falls two years after the 31 January 2026 date. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the passed Commission and ACER steps were completed, which the captured text cannot show.

## 7. Threshold Questions

One question decides when a price support scheme must take the two-way form: the date of the contract and the kind of plant. The scheme applies to new generation «from the following sources: (a) wind energy; (b) solar energy; (c) geothermal energy; (d) hydropower without reservoir; (e) nuclear energy.» Another question is when peak-shaving can be used: «Where a regional or Union-wide electricity price crisis is declared in accordance with Article 66a of Directive (EU) 2019/944, Member States may request system operators to propose the procurement of peak-shaving products in order to achieve a reduction of electricity demand during peak hours.»

*Analytical inference:* the two-way contract rule covers new wind, solar, geothermal, hydropower without reservoir and nuclear plants under contracts concluded from 17 July 2027, and peak-shaving is open only while a crisis is declared. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given Member State scheme falls inside the Article 19d rule.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Power purchase agreements (Article 19a). «Member States shall promote the uptake of PPAs, including by removing unjustified barriers and disproportionate or discriminatory procedures or charges, with a view to providing price predictability». «Member States shall ensure, in a coordinated manner, that instruments, such as guarantee schemes at market prices, to reduce the financial risks associated to offtaker payment default in the framework of PPAs are in place and accessible to customers that face entry barriers to the PPA market and that are not in financial difficulty.»

Two-way contracts for difference (Article 19d). «Direct price support schemes for investment in new power-generating facilities for the generation of electricity from the sources listed in paragraph 4 shall take the form of two-way contracts for difference or equivalent schemes with the same effects.» Revenues: «shall be distributed to final customers». Design: «include penalty clauses applicable in the case of undue unilateral early termination of the contract».

Flexibility (Articles 19e and 19f). «each Member State shall define, on the basis of that report, an indicative national objective for non-fossil flexibility, including the respective specific contributions of both demand response and energy storage to that objective.»

Forward markets (Article 9). «The design of the Union’s forward markets shall comprise the necessary tools to improve the ability of market participants to hedge price risks in the internal electricity market.»

Trading (Article 8). «From 1 January 2026, the intraday cross-zonal gate closure time shall not be more than 30 minutes ahead of real time.»

*Analytical inference:* each duty above sits on a Member State, a regulator, a grid or market operator or the Commission; the text states no electricity price, no freight rate, no amount of fine and no pass-through of any cost to a freight customer. No phase-in is stated in Articles 19a, 19e and 19f beyond the dates in section 14. No exceptions are stated in Articles 19a and 19f. No scope limits are stated in Articles 19a and 19f.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these market changes alters the price a freight business pays for electricity under its contracts.

Obligations surveyed: 7; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 9.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets electricity market rules, not rules for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Reporting runs between operators, regulators, ACER and the Commission. The grid operators propose data formats: «By 17 April 2025, the ENTSO for Electricity and the EU DSO entity shall jointly submit to ACER a proposal regarding the type of data and format to be submitted to a regulatory authority or another authority or entity designated pursuant to paragraph 1, and the methodology for the analysis of the flexibility needs referred to in paragraph 4.» The Commission reports on power purchase markets every two years, as quoted in section 6. The text names no registration duty on a freight business.

*Analytical inference:* the registration and reporting duties fall on regulators, operators and the Commission; none on a forwarder is stated.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks grid operators and regulators to build data and market systems, and states no system for a freight business to build.

- A facilities lead keeps a register of each depot and charging site that buys electricity directly, with its supply contract end date, and reviews it each time a Member State announces a power purchase agreement guarantee instrument under Article 19a.
- A pricing lead records, at the next annual tariff review, whether electricity cost changes at depots and charging sites are passed to clients, and notes that the Regulation itself states no freight rate or surcharge.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on Article 19a and on the absence of a freight cost in the text. The recitals say revenues may be used for «investment in distribution grid development, renewable energy sources and electric vehicle charging infrastructure». *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client contract lets the business pass electricity cost changes through.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Grid operators may be excused from the 30-minute gate closure for a time: «grant a derogation from the requirement laid down in paragraph 1 until 1 January 2029». A further derogation needs a new request: «The transmission system operator concerned shall submit the request to the regulatory authority concerned, to the ENTSO for Electricity and to ACER by 30 June 2028.» Small installations may be exempted from the two-way contract rule: «Member States may exempt small-scale renewables installations».

*Analytical inference:* the gate closure rule can differ between transmission areas until the derogations end, and the CfD rule can differ for small installations. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the transmission operator derogation request duty can reach a counterparty of the business, such as a grid operator serving a depot, and whether a derogation changes the supply terms it offers.
