## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 13 June 2024: Regulation adopted at Brussels
- 17 October 2024: ACER assessment of voluntary PPA templates (passed)
- 17 January 2025: Commission report on capacity mechanisms (passed)
- 17 April 2025: Commission proposals on capacity mechanisms, and ENTSO and EU DSO entity data proposal to ACER (passed)
- 30 June 2025: ACER assessment of peak-shaving products (passed)
- 1 January 2026: intraday cross-zonal gate closure not more than 30 minutes ahead of real time (passed)
- 17 January 2026: Commission assessment of forward market measures (passed)
- 31 January 2026: Commission assessment of PPA market barriers, then every two years (passed)
- 30 June 2026: Commission review of the Regulation (passed)
- 17 July 2026: Commission implementing act on forward market measures (passed)
- 17 July 2027: two-way contracts for difference apply to new contracts under direct price support schemes
- 1 December 2027: Commission report on intraday gate closure
- 30 June 2028: date for a transmission operator to submit a request for a further derogation
- 1 January 2029: end of the first derogation period and target for 30-minute gate closure
- 17 July 2029: the two-way contract date for offshore hybrid asset projects

The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal; the text states no calendar date for that day.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2024/1244 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 24 April 2024 on reporting of environmental data from industrial installations, establishing an Industrial Emissions Portal and repealing Regulation (EC) No 166/2006», the European Union rule on public reporting of pollution from industrial sites. Its subject: «This Regulation lays down rules on the collection and reporting of environmental data on industrial installations and establishes an Industrial Emissions Portal (the ‘Portal’) at Union level in the form of an online database giving public access to such data.» Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation makes operators of listed industrial sites report their releases of pollutants and their waste transfers each year, and puts the results on a public website. The duty sits with operators: «Each operator of an installation that undertakes one or more of the activities listed in Annex I which meet or exceed the applicable capacity thresholds specified in that Annex and either releases any of the pollutants listed in Annex II in a quantity above the applicable thresholds, or exceeds the waste thresholds set out in point (b) of this paragraph, shall report annually to its competent authority». The public can search by facility: «facility, including the facility’s parent company where applicable, and its geographical location». Two listed activities are close to freight supply chains: «Installations for the building and/or dismantling of ships, and for the painting or removal of paint from ships» and «Electrolysis of water for production of hydrogen». The Regulation enters into force as its last article states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.» It applies later: «It shall apply from 1 January 2028.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder, a carrier or a shipper is not an operator of an Annex I installation, so the reporting duty is not theirs; the Regulation matters to them as a public source on the sites of suppliers, ship yards and hydrogen producers they deal with.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight business within the next 30 days. The Regulation applies from «1 January 2028», and the Commission acts that prepare it were due earlier: «The Commission shall, by 31 December 2025, adopt by means of implementing acts a list of relevant raw materials to be reported». That date has passed; the captured text does not say whether the acts were adopted.

- A supplier-data lead marks in the supplier file, before 1 January 2028, each contracted supplier or ship yard that runs an installation in the Annex I list, so its Portal entry can be matched once reporting under this Regulation starts.
- A contracts lead asks, at the next supplier contract review, whether a supplier that operates an Annex I installation reports under Article 6 and will share the data it files, so the business can answer a client who asks about a supplier's releases.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the operator duty in Article 6 and the public Portal in Articles 4 and 5, quoted in section 2 and section 8. The Regulation states no cost, fee or rate for a freight business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a supplier contract can oblige a supplier to share the report it files, and whether any data is confidential under Article 11.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the operator, the competent authority, the Member States, the Commission and the European Environment Agency (the Agency). The text defines the authority: «‘competent authority’ means the national authority or authorities, or any other competent body or bodies, designated by Member States». The chain runs operator to competent authority, then Member State to Commission: «On an annual basis, no later than 11 months from the end of the reporting year, Member States shall submit to the Commission, by electronic means, a report including all the data referred to in Article 6, in a format to be established by the Commission by means of implementing acts.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder, a carrier and a shipper are not named; their position is outside the chain, as readers of public data. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that operates a warehouse or port terminal with an Annex I activity on site could be an operator under the Directive definition the Regulation uses.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Regulation. Section 6 notes the guidance the text calls for.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Commission must draw up guidance: «The guidelines concerning points (a) to (g) of the first paragraph, shall be drawn up for the first time by 1 January 2026. The guidelines concerning point (h) of the first paragraph, shall be drawn up for the first time by 1 January 2025, after consulting the Member States.» Both dates have passed, and the captured text does not say whether the guidance was published. The Commission was also to review the list of pollutants: «The Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with paragraph 2 by 31 December 2025.» The recital says the review should include «an assessment of the need to reduce the reporting thresholds for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and other relevant substances». The delegated powers have a term: «shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 22 May 2024». The Regulation is reviewed: «The Commission shall carry out a review of the implementation of this Regulation and its Annexes, at least every five years from its date of application.»

*Analytical inference:* the delegated act on pollutants and thresholds decides how many substances and sites are reported; the text states no outcome. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the guidance and acts due by 31 December 2025 have been adopted, which the captured text cannot show.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Two thresholds decide whether a site reports. A capacity threshold sits in Annex I, for example «Installations for the building and/or dismantling of ships, and for the painting or removal of paint from ships With a capacity for ships 100 m long». A waste threshold sits in Article 6: «data on off-site transfers of hazardous waste exceeding 2 tonnes per year per facility or of non-hazardous waste exceeding 2 000 tonnes per year per facility». For hydrogen: «Electrolysis of water for production of hydrogen Industrial scale production».

*Analytical inference:* a site below the thresholds still has a duty to say so, as Article 6(2) quoted in section 12 states. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular ship yard or hydrogen plant used by a client meets these thresholds.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Annual reporting (Article 6). «Each operator of an installation that undertakes one or more of the activities listed in Annex I which meet or exceed the applicable capacity thresholds specified in that Annex and either releases any of the pollutants listed in Annex II in a quantity above the applicable thresholds, or exceeds the waste thresholds set out in point (b) of this paragraph, shall report annually to its competent authority at least the following information and data, unless such information or data are already available to the competent authority». The data cover releases, waste transfers, «data on the use of water, energy and relevant raw materials as determined in the implementing act referred to in the second subparagraph» and «information allowing contextualisation of the data reported under points (a) to (d), including production volume and number of operating hours».

Method (Article 6(3)). «Operators shall obtain the data by means of measurement.» Quality (Article 9). «The operators of an installation that are subject to the reporting requirements set out in Article 6 shall ensure that the data they report are of high quality.»

Public access (Article 10). «The Commission, assisted by the Agency, shall make the data included in the Portal publicly accessible and free of charge on the internet within one month of the submission of the reports by Member States in accordance with Article 7(1).»

Penalties (Article 18). «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.» «The penalties referred to in paragraph 1 shall include fines.»

*Analytical inference:* the duties above sit on operators and Member States; the Regulation states no amount of fine, no charge to customers and no pass-through to freight. No phase-in is stated in Articles 6, 9, 10 and 18 beyond the application date of 1 January 2028. No scope limits are stated in Articles 9, 10 and 18.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which national penalty rules apply in each Member State where a supplier operates.

Obligations surveyed: 5; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 9.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets reporting rules for industrial installations, not for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Operators report to their competent authority each year (Article 6, quoted in section 8). Member States then report to the Commission, which publishes: «The Commission services, assisted by the European Environment Agency (the ‘Agency’), shall incorporate the data reported by Member States into the Portal within one month of the completion of reporting by Member States in accordance with paragraph 1.» The transition keeps the older rule for one more year: «Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 shall continue to apply as regards reporting for the year 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* reporting under this Regulation therefore begins with the year after 2026, since the older Regulation continues for the year 2026; the text states no other start date. The registration and reporting duties fall on operators and Member States, and none on a forwarder is stated.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks operators and authorities to build data and reporting systems, and states no system for a freight business to build.

- A sustainability data lead checks the Portal each time the Commission adds a reporting year after the 2028 application, for entries on the suppliers listed in the supplier file.
- A sales lead prepares, before the first published entries, a short plain note for clients that explains what a Portal entry on a supplier shows and what it does not.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the public access rule in Article 10 and on the search by facility and parent company in Article 5. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client contract limits what the business may say about a supplier's Portal entry.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

A site below the thresholds files a short statement: «the operator of the installation concerned shall declare, in its report, that the release of pollutants or off-site transfers of pollutants or waste are below those thresholds.» Confidential data are marked, not dropped: «shall indicate separately for each installation which data cannot be made public and provide the reasons for that.» Some activities are listed only where another law does not already cover them: «Underground mining and related operations, including the extraction of crude oil or gas either onshore or offshore (where not covered by Annex I to Directive 2010/75/EU)». The transition: «shall continue to apply as regards reporting for the year 2026».

*Analytical inference:* the data a client asks about can therefore be missing from the Portal either because the site is below the thresholds or because a Member State treats the data as confidential. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a supplier's missing entry means no duty or confidential data.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 24 April 2024: Regulation adopted at Strasbourg
- 22 May 2024: delegated-act power conferred on the Commission for five years
- 1 January 2025: date by which the Commission draws up the first guidelines on how to apply the definitions of sites, facilities and installations (passed)
- 31 December 2025: date by which the Commission adopts the list of raw materials and the delegated act on the pollutant list (passed)
- 1 January 2026: date by which the Commission draws up the first guidelines on reporting procedures, data, quality, confidentiality, methods, parent company names and calculation methods (passed)
- 1 January 2028: the Regulation applies and Regulation (EC) No 166/2006 is repealed

The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal; the text states no calendar date for that day.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) 2024/1834 of 3 July 2024 implementing Directive 2009/125/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council with regard to ecodesign requirements for fans driven by motors with an electric input power between 125 W and 500 kW and repealing Commission Regulation (EU) No 327/2011», the Union ecodesign rule for fans, the machines that move air or gas, used in buildings, industry and equipment. Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation states is quoted from its text; what it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation sets what a fan must meet before it is sold: «This Regulation lays down ecodesign requirements for the placing on the market or putting into service of fans with an electric input power between 125 W and 500 kW (≥ 125 W and ≤ 500 kW) at their best efficiency point, including where they are integrated into other products.» The requirements sit in an annex and have their own start dates: «The ecodesign requirements for fans are set out in Annex II and shall apply from the dates indicated therein.» It replaces an older rule: «Regulation (EU) No 327/2011 is repealed with effect from 24 July 2026.»

The Regulation enters into force as its Article 10 states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». Its start dates: «It shall apply from 24 July 2026. However, Article 6 and Article 9(2) shall apply from 24 July 2024.»

*Analytical inference:* the rules bind the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative that places a fan on the market, not the carrier that moves it. A forwarder or shipper is not named. A freight business meets it as an importer if it places fans on the Union market, as a carrier of fans or fan spare parts, or as a buyer of equipment that has a fan built in.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Regulation sets no step on a freight operator within the next 30 days. Its main date has passed: «It shall apply from 24 July 2026.» The next live date is 24 July 2027: «With effect from 24 July 2027, the following requirements shall apply:» Spare parts have a delivery time: «During the period mentioned in point (c), the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative shall ensure the delivery of the spare parts with the following timeframe: (1) as specified in a contract, where a contract exists between the manufacturer and the end user of the fan; (2) if not, as specified in the product information of the fan and made available on free access websites; (3) if not, then no later than 6 weeks after having received the order.»

- A logistics lead at a business that ships fan spare parts for a manufacturer or importer asks, at the next service-level review, which delivery time the contract or the published product information states for those parts, because the Regulation falls back to no later than 6 weeks after the order when neither does.

- A procurement lead at a business that buys equipment with a built-in fan asks, at the next purchase, for the free access website address of the fan's manufacturer, authorised representative or importer, because the product information must be kept there for at least 20 years after the last unit is placed on the market.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the delivery-time and information-website rules quoted here; the Regulation requires neither step of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an importer within the Regulation when it brings fans or equipment with fans into the Union.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the manufacturer, the importer, the authorised representative, professional repairers, Member State authorities and the end user. The duty not to rig test results: «Manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall not place on the market or put into service products designed to alter their behaviour or properties when being tested so as to achieve a more favourable result for any declared value of the parameters regulated in this Regulation.» Market surveillance: «Member State authorities shall apply the verification procedure laid down in Annex IV to this Regulation when performing the market surveillance checks referred to in Article 3(2) of Directive 2009/125/EC.» Spare parts duty holders: «manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives of fans, other than safety critical fans, shall make available to professional repairers at least the following spare parts»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder or shipper is not named. The parties the Regulation puts the duties on are the manufacturer, importer and authorised representative, and a carrier that only moves fans does not hold their role. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that brings fans into the Union under its own name is an importer in the Regulation's sense.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance on this Regulation is held.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Later steps are set by the text. Spare parts availability starts: «Availability of spare parts referred to in points (a) and (b) shall be ensured for a minimum period starting at the latest 24 July 2028 or two years after the placing on the market of the first unit of the model, whichever is the later date, and ending at least 10 years after placing on the market the last unit of the model concerned.» The Commission reviews the rules: «The Commission shall review this Regulation in the light of technological progress and shall present the results of that assessment, including, if appropriate, a draft revision proposal, to the Consultation Forum by 27 July 2030 at the latest.» The older rule runs on for some fans: «However, Annexes I, II and III to that Regulation, shall continue to apply until 24 July 2037, in relation to fans integrated into other products and in relation to spare part fans.»

*Analytical inference:* the 2027 date adds information on partial-load performance; the 2030 review is where the exemptions, the circumvention rules and the case for an energy label are reassessed. The text does not say what the review will change.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether a product is caught is whether it is a fan in scope. The text sets it: «This Regulation lays down ecodesign requirements for the placing on the market or putting into service of fans with an electric input power between 125 W and 500 kW (≥ 125 W and ≤ 500 kW) at their best efficiency point, including where they are integrated into other products.» It lists exclusions, for example: «This Regulation shall not apply to: (a) fan impellers mounted on the shaft of electric motors with the sole purpose of cooling the motor itself;» And fans specified to operate exclusively in listed settings: «This Regulation shall not apply to fans that are specified to operate exclusively as follows and are specifically designed and marketed as such:» Another example: «(l) for handling gases with a compressibility factor, rounded to the nearest second decimal, in the designated pressure and temperature range of the scope that is not equal to 1,00;»

*Analytical inference:* a fan outside the 125 W to 500 kW range at its best efficiency point, or one specified to operate exclusively in a listed setting, is outside the rules. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a fan the business handles is inside the 125 W to 500 kW range at its best efficiency point.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Minimum efficiency. «With effect from 24 July 2026, the following rules shall apply: 1. Fans, except jet fans, cross flow fans and fans referred to in point 7, shall have a fan efficiency ( η ) equal to or larger than the minimum fan efficiency ( η min )» «Cross flow fans shall have a minimum total fan efficiency (B,D) of at least 0,21 (21 %) over the entire power range.»

Who it applies to. «Fans shall comply with the ecodesign requirements set out in points 1 to 5 of this Annex, except for fans that meet all the following criteria:»

Information. «free access websites of the manufacturer of the fan, its authorised representative or the importer for a period of at least 20 years after the placing on the market of the last unit of the model concerned.»

Spare parts. «For all models, units of which are placed on the market as from 24 July 2026, manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives of fans, other than safety critical fans, shall make available to professional repairers at least the following spare parts, if part of the fan, as individual elements or in an assembly when integrated as originally supplied:» «(3) if not, then no later than 6 weeks after having received the order.»

Conformity assessment. «The conformity assessment procedure referred to in Article 8 of Directive 2009/125/EC shall be the internal design control system set out in Annex IV to that Directive or the management system for assessing conformity set out in Annex V to that Directive.»

*No penalty: the source states no penalty, fine or sanction; it sets a verification procedure for market surveillance checks by Member State authorities.*

*Analytical inference:* each duty falls on the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative; the Regulation states no fine, cost or freight rate effect, so the cost of non-compliance or of spare part deliveries to a freight business is a gap. No phase-in is stated in Articles 3 and 4 beyond the dates in Annex II. No scope limits are stated in Articles 3, 4, 5 and 6.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a spare part shipment the business carries for a manufacturer or importer gives the business any duty under the delivery-time rule.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Regulation asks for documents, not registrations. Technical file: «For the purposes of the conformity assessment pursuant to Article 8 of Directive 2009/125/EC, the technical documentation shall contain a copy of the declared values of parameters in point 2.2 of Annex II» Product information: «With effect from 24 July 2026, the information on fans set out in points 2(a) to (o) shall be visibly displayed in:» A change that needs no new assessment: «A fan to which a VSD is added shall not be considered a new fan model requiring a new conformity assessment if:»

*Analytical inference:* these are duties of the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative; the text states no registration or report by a forwarder.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks the parties it names to keep a public spare parts list and an ordering route, and to meet a delivery time. The spare parts rule reads: «the list of spare parts, the procedure for ordering them shall be publicly available on the free access website of the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative» The delivery time is set in Section 3.

- A customer-service lead at a business that orders fan spare parts through a freight service asks the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative, at the next order, for the published ordering procedure, because the Regulation requires the list and the procedure to be publicly available for the parts period.

- A transport planner at a business that moves fan spare parts records the order date for each shipment, so a delivery measured from the order, as in the 6 week fallback, can be checked later.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the public ordering procedure and the delivery-time fallback; the Regulation states no data a forwarder must keep as a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is a manufacturer, importer or authorised representative of any fan.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Some fans and units are treated apart. Transitional units: «Units of models placed on the market between 24 July 2024 and 24 July 2026 which comply with the provisions of this Regulation shall be considered to comply with the requirements of Regulation (EU) No 327/2011.» Spare part fans: «However, until 24 July 2037, spare part fans replacing fans placed on the market before 24 July 2026, or until the date of the last placing on the market of the last unit of the model for fans that meet the criteria (a) to (d) above, and integrated into a product, are exempt from the requirements set out in points 1 to 5»

*Analytical inference:* the transitional rule treats units placed on the market between the two dates as compliant with the older Regulation if they comply with this one; spare part fans for older fans can stay on the older rules until the stated date, with the conditions the Annex sets.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2026/261 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 26 January 2026 on phasing out Russian natural gas imports and preparing the phase-out of Russian oil imports, improving monitoring of potential energy dependencies and amending Regulation (EU) 2017/1938», the Union regulation that bans imports of Russian natural gas in steps and prepares the end of Russian oil imports. Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation states is quoted from its text; what it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation states its aim: «This Regulation provides a framework for eliminating the Union’s remaining exposure to the significant risks for trade and security of supply resulting from trade in natural gas with the Russian Federation and for preparing the effective and timely phase-out of oil imports from the Russian Federation by laying down: (a) a stepwise prohibition on imports of natural gas from the Russian Federation;» It covers liquefied natural gas: «‘LNG’ means liquefied natural gas as referred to in CN code 2711 11 00;» Its definition of the person who bears the import duties reaches the party that files the customs declaration: «‘importer’ means the natural or legal person that is the declarant as defined in Article 5, point (15), of the Union Customs Code in the relevant customs declaration, or a natural or legal person, including affiliated undertakings, that brings goods into the customs territory of the Union or otherwise places goods on the Union market;»

The Regulation enters into force as its Article 14 states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union». Its start dates, both of which have passed: «Article 3 shall apply from 18 March 2026, except where otherwise specified in Article 4. Article 5 shall apply from 18 February 2026.»

*Analytical inference:* the bans bite on imports of natural gas and LNG, and the importer is defined to include the declarant named in the customs declaration. A freight business that files customs declarations for natural gas or LNG, or that brings such goods into the Union, may therefore be an importer within the Regulation. A forwarder or shipper is not named. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an importer as the definition reads when it acts as declarant or carries such goods.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

WINDOW CLOSING: the temporary exemption for LNG under long-term contracts ends on 1 January 2027, about 60 days away; no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days, and whether the Regulation puts any duty on a forwarder is the question for counsel below. The ban date: «The prohibition pursuant to Article 3(2) shall apply as of 1 January 2027, where it can be demonstrated to the authorising authorities that the relevant imports are carried out under a long-term supply contract concluded before 17 June 2025, and not amended thereafter, unless the amendment is covered by paragraph 5 of this Article.» The customs side is already live: «shall be provided with all information necessary to establish the country of production of that natural gas, no later than 5 working days before its entry into the customs territory of the Union.» If proof is not conclusive: «Where the information provided is not conclusive, the customs authorities shall refuse the release for free circulation of the relevant goods.» Gas moved through the Union in transit also needs advance information: «Where natural gas is transported through the Union from third country to third country under a transit procedure in accordance with the Union Customs Code, including for the purpose of storage under customs warehousing rules, authorising authorities and, where applicable, customs authorities shall be informed no later than 5 working days before the planned transit about:»

- A customs lead at a business that files declarations for natural gas or LNG asks each importer client, at each new consignment, for the evidence that shows the country of production, because the information must reach the authorising authorities no later than 5 working days before entry.

- A customs lead, before 1 January 2027, asks each importer client of LNG whether its supply is under a long-term contract concluded before 17 June 2025 and not amended since, because the Article 3(2) ban applies from 1 January 2027 for those contracts only where that is demonstrated.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the declarant definition, the proof-of-origin deadline and the exemption conditions quoted above; the Regulation does not name a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business bears any penalty exposure as an importer when it acts as declarant for a client, and which authority is the authorising authority in each Member State where it files.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the importer, the customs authority, the authorising authority, competent and regulatory authorities, ACER, OLAF, EPPO, the Commission and Member States. The authorising authority is set: «The authorising authority is the customs authority, unless a Member State designates another authority for that purpose.» Monitoring is shared: «Customs authorities, and, where relevant, competent authorities and regulatory authorities, the European Anti-Fraud Office (OLAF), the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) and the European Union Agency for the Cooperation of Energy Regulators (ACER) shall ensure the effective monitoring of the provisions in Chapter II» Parties to a gas supply contract are identified by number: «(d) the identity of the parties to the gas supply contract, including, for parties registered in the Union, the Economic Operator Registration and Identification (EORI) number;»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder or shipper is not named. The importer is the person who carries the customs declaration or brings the goods in, and the customs authority is the default authorising authority and the body that refuses release; the contract parties' EORI numbers are asked for in the authorisation file. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which party in a gas supply chain is the importer when a declarant acts for another person.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance on this Regulation is held; Section 6 states that the Commission is to publish guidance.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Later steps are set by the text. Guidance: «The Commission shall, in close cooperation with authorising authorities and, where applicable, customs authorities, publish guidance on further details concerning the prior authorisation procedure and adequate types of documents and evidence to be submitted.» Storage filling: «it shall confirm that risk by way of an implementing decision no later than 15 September 2027.» and then «the prohibition pursuant to Article 3(1) of this Regulation shall apply only as of 1 November 2027 in that Member State» Reports on contracts, with the first date passed: «By 1 July 2026 and 1 July 2027, ACER shall, based on the data received under this Regulation and on information in its possession, publish a report providing an overview of contracts for the supply of natural gas that originates in or is exported, directly or indirectly, from the Russian Federation, and assessing the impact of diversification on energy markets.» Commission report: «By 4 February 2028, the Commission shall submit a report on the implementation of this Regulation to the European Parliament and the Council.» Oil: «A Member State that receives imports of oil that originates in or is exported, directly or indirectly, from the Russian Federation, shall establish a plan describing measures for, milestones in and potential barriers to diversifying their oil supplies, (a ‘national diversification plan for oil’), in order to discontinue, all imports of oil that originates in or is exported, directly or indirectly, from the Russian Federation by the end of 2027.»

*Analytical inference:* the 15 September 2027 decision decides whether the pipeline gas ban date moves to 1 November 2027 in a Member State at risk on storage filling; the text sets no date for the guidance, so the evidence forms for authorisation are open. The oil end date is addressed to Member States' plans; the text held states no import ban on oil with a date and no duty on a freight operator for oil.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether a consignment is caught is where the gas comes from. Gas entering by named routes is presumed Russian: «Natural gas to be imported into the Union via borders or interconnectors or interconnection points between the Union and the Russian Federation or Belarus, or via pipelines which connect the Russian Federation with the Union and are running through third countries without having entry points between the Russian Federation and the Union, shall be presumed to be exported, directly or indirectly, from the Russian Federation.» The country of production is not always the country of extraction: «where natural gas extracted in countries other than the Russian Federation is liquified or regasified in the Russian Federation, the Russian Federation shall be considered to be the country of production.» A producing country can be exempt from prior authorisation: «An exemption from the prior authorisation set out in paragraph 3 shall apply where natural gas is imported from a country which produces natural gas and has exported more than 5 bcm of natural gas to the Union in 2024, and:»

*Analytical inference:* a consignment that enters by the named routes is treated as Russian gas by the presumption, and a consignment from a producing country outside the exemption needs the proof of production in the authorisation file. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which of these tests applies to a consignment the business declares.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Prohibition on pipeline gas. «The import of natural gas in gaseous state via pipelines (‘pipeline gas’) that originates in or is exported, directly or indirectly, from the Russian Federation shall be prohibited, unless one of the temporary exemptions provided for in Article 4 applies.»

Prohibition on LNG. «The import of LNG that originates in or is exported, directly or indirectly, from the Russian Federation, or that is obtained from natural gas in gaseous state extracted in the Russian Federation, shall be prohibited, unless one of the temporary exemptions provided for in Article 4 applies. This prohibition shall also apply to LNG that originates in or is exported, directly or indirectly, from the Russian Federation or that is obtained from natural gas in gaseous state extracted in the Russian Federation contained in mixtures.»

Short-term contracts. «The prohibition pursuant to Article 3(1) shall apply as of 17 June 2026 and the prohibition pursuant to Article 3(2) shall apply as of 25 April 2026, where it can be demonstrated to the authorising authorities that the relevant imports are carried out under a short-term supply contract concluded before 17 June 2025, and not amended thereafter, unless the amendment is covered by paragraph 5 of this Article.» Both dates have passed.

Long-term contracts, pipeline gas. «The prohibition pursuant to Article 3(1) of this Regulation shall apply as of 30 September 2027, where it can be demonstrated to the authorising authorities that the relevant imports are carried out under a long-term supply contract concluded before 17 June 2025, and not amended thereafter, unless the amendment is covered by paragraph 5 of this Article.»

Long-term contracts, LNG. «The prohibition pursuant to Article 3(2) shall apply as of 1 January 2027, where it can be demonstrated to the authorising authorities that the relevant imports are carried out under a long-term supply contract concluded before 17 June 2025, and not amended thereafter, unless the amendment is covered by paragraph 5 of this Article.» «The quantities of imports made in accordance with paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 4 shall not exceed the contracted quantities.»

Prior authorisation. «Where a temporary exemption pursuant to Article 4 is requested, imports shall be subject to prior authorisation.» «The information referred to in paragraph 1 shall be submitted to the authorising authority no later than one month before the entry of the natural gas into the customs territory of the Union.» «Imports of natural gas, the country of production of which is not the Russian Federation, shall be subject to prior authorisation, except where those imports fall under paragraph 4.» «Where the information provided is not conclusive, the customs authorities shall refuse the release for free circulation of the relevant goods.»

Oil. «to discontinue, all imports of oil that originates in or is exported, directly or indirectly, from the Russian Federation by the end of 2027.»

Emergency suspension. «The suspension shall be limited to a duration which is strictly necessary to bridge the time until there are sufficient supplies from countries other than the Russian Federation to meet Union demand. It shall not be granted for more than 4 weeks at a time»

Penalties. «Member States shall provide for effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties for failure to comply with Articles 3, 4 or 5. 2. The maximum penalty for legal persons shall be at least: (a) 3,5 % of the undertaking’s total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, (b) EUR 40 million, or (c) 300 % of the estimated transaction turnover, which shall be calculated on the basis of the volume of the natural gas involved and the ‘day-ahead’ contract prices on the TTF market. The maximum penalty for natural persons shall be at least EUR 2,5 million.»

Relation to other rules. «This Regulation is without prejudice to the application of the prohibition related to LNG established in Regulation (EU) No 833/2014 which shall apply and be complied with regardless of the provisions of this Regulation.»

*Analytical inference:* the bans and the proof-of-origin deadlines fall on the importer and are applied by the customs and authorising authorities; the penalties are for Member States to set at the stated minimum maxima. The Regulation states no freight rate or surcharge effect, so the effect on cargo costs is a gap. No phase-in is stated in Article 8 beyond the notification date.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business would be treated as an importer for the penalties when it acts as declarant, and how a Member State has set the penalty above the stated minimum.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation covers imports of natural gas and oil, not products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reporting duties fall mainly on Member States and authorities. Plans: «By 1 March 2026, Member States shall submit to the Commission their national diversification plans for natural gas, using the template set out in Annex I.» «By 1 March 2026, Member States shall submit to the Commission their national diversification plans for oil, using the template set out in Annex II.» Contract information to the Commission: «The information referred to in point (c) of the first subparagraph shall be provided no later than 4 March 2026 and for each contract in a disaggregated format, including the relevant text parts in full, excluding price information» Authority reporting: «authorising authorities and, where applicable, customs authorities shall inform regulatory authorities, competent authorities, ACER and the Commission, on a monthly basis, on the key elements concerning the developments on imports of natural gas» Penalty rules: «Member States shall, by 4 February 2028, notify the Commission of the national provisions in force ensuring the implementation of this Article»

*Analytical inference:* these are duties of Member State authorities and of those who supply contract information; the text does not state a registration or report by a forwarder, but the authorisation file asks for the contract parties' EORI numbers, as Section 4 quotes.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

WINDOW CLOSING: with the LNG long-term exemption ending on 1 January 2027, the authorisation file needs facts that sit with the importer and its supplier. Authorities verify the origin evidence: «Authorising authorities and customs authorities shall verify the evidence submitted to establish the country of production, and, where appropriate, request further information» The file includes: «(e) for LNG imports, the place of liquefaction and the port of first loading;» «(c) the contracted quantities, including all upward or downward flexibility rights;» For mixtures: «(f) in the case of mixtures, documentation proving the quantities of natural gas that originates in or is exported, directly or indirectly, from the Russian Federation and the quantities of natural gas from other countries of origin contained in the mixture and information establishing the mixing process;»

- A customs lead keeps, per LNG consignment, the place of liquefaction and the port of first loading, and the contract quantities, on the file the business holds for the importer client, because the authorisation information asks for them one month before entry.

- A booking desk, when an LNG consignment is a mixture, asks the importer for the documents that prove the quantity from each country of origin, because the Regulation asks for that proof for mixtures.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the file contents quoted above; the Regulation requires these facts of the importer in its file to the authorising authority, not of a forwarder as such. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is the party that must submit the file.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The temporary exemptions are the heart of the text. Amended contracts keep their exemption for some changes: «The temporary exemptions provided for in paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 4 shall also apply with regard to existing supply contracts that are amended as follows: (a) lowering contracted quantities; (b) lowering prices and fees; (c) amending confidentiality clauses;» A landlocked country: «(7) ‘landlocked country’ means a country that is entirely surrounded by land and has no direct access to the sea;» and a short-term contract that supports a long-term one: «that the relevant imports are carried out under a short-term supply contract with delivery to a landlocked country which is necessary to fulfil the long-term supply contract»

*Analytical inference:* the exemptions are tied to contracts concluded before 17 June 2025 and to the contracted quantities; they do not cover a new contract or a price rise that the list does not allow. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a contract amendment a client reports is on the list of permitted amendments.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2021/1153 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 7 July 2021 establishing the Connecting Europe Facility and repealing Regulations (EU) No 1316/2013 and (EU) No 283/2014», an EU regulation published in the «Official Journal of the European Union». Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» Its subject matter: «This Regulation establishes the Connecting Europe Facility (the ‘CEF’) for the period of the Multiannual Financial Framework (the “MFF”) 2021-2027. This Regulation lays down the objectives of the CEF, its budget for the period 2021-2027, the forms of Union funding and the rules for providing such funding.» What the Regulation says is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Connecting Europe Facility is an EU grant fund for transport, energy and digital networks. Its aims: «The general objectives of the CEF are to build, develop, modernise and complete the trans-European networks in the transport, energy and digital sectors and to facilitate cross-border cooperation in the field of renewable energy». Its size: «The financial envelope for the implementation of the CEF for the period from 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2027 shall be EUR 33 710 000 000». A share goes to climate: «the CEF shall contribute, through its actions, 60 % of its overall financial envelope to climate objectives». The transport share: «(a) EUR 25 807 000 000 for the specific objectives referred to in Article 3(2), point (a)». It was adopted at Strasbourg: «Done at Strasbourg, 7 July 2021.»

The Regulation enters into force as its text states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 1 January 2021.»

*Analytical inference:* the Regulation sets no duty, fee or surcharge on a freight business; it is a funding rulebook. Freight is touched because the fund pays for ports, terminals, rail freight, inland waterway and alternative fuel infrastructure (section 8).

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The funding period has a stated end: «The financial envelope for the implementation of the CEF for the period from 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2027 shall be EUR 33 710 000 000». Who may apply: «To be eligible, proposals shall be submitted: (a) by one or more Member States; or (b) with the agreement of the Member States concerned, by international organisations, joint undertakings, or by public or private undertakings or bodies, including regional or local authorities.» Later spending is allowed: «If necessary, appropriations may be entered in the Union budget beyond 2027 to cover the expenses provided for in Article 4(5), to enable the management of actions not completed by 31 December 2027, in accordance with this Regulation.» A project is judged also on freight disruption: «The assessment shall also consider whether the implementation of actions financed by the CEF risks causing disruption to freight and passenger flows on the section of the line concerned by the project and whether those risks have been mitigated.»

- When a Commission call for proposals under the CEF work programme opens before the funding period ends on 31 December 2027, a business development lead at a port, terminal or logistics-platform operator checks the planned project against the eligible transport actions in section 8 and asks the Member State concerned to agree to the submission.

*Analytical inference:* the action rests on the rule that an undertaking's proposal needs the agreement of the Member States concerned, unless the Member State decides otherwise for a work programme; the Regulation requires no such step of a business that does not apply. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular project qualifies and which Member State must agree is for counsel and the call documents.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The roles named are the Commission, Member States and beneficiaries. Member States may submit: «To be eligible, proposals shall be submitted: (a) by one or more Member States; or (b) with the agreement of the Member States concerned, by international organisations, joint undertakings, or by public or private undertakings or bodies, including regional or local authorities.» Eligible legal entities: «2. The following entities shall be eligible: (a) legal entities established in: (i) a Member State, including joint ventures;» The Commission decides grants: «Following every call for proposals based on the work programmes referred to in Article 20, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act setting the amount of financial support to be granted to the projects selected or to parts thereof» Beneficiaries report: «The beneficiaries shall submit reports as defined in the respective grant agreements without prior approval of the Member States.» The Regulation is «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder, carrier or shipper is not named as a duty holder; a freight business meets the Regulation as an applicant, a beneficiary or a user of funded infrastructure. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that operates a terminal or logistics platform counts as an eligible undertaking in a given call.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Regulation; the stored text holds the Regulation and its Annex only.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Dated steps in the text. Later spending: «If necessary, appropriations may be entered in the Union budget beyond 2027 to cover the expenses provided for in Article 4(5), to enable the management of actions not completed by 31 December 2027, in accordance with this Regulation.» Delegated acts power: «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 22(2) and Article 25 shall be conferred on the Commission until 31 December 2028.» Evaluations: «An interim evaluation of the CEF shall be carried out once there is sufficient information available about the implementation of the CEF, but no later than four years after the start of implementation of the CEF.» «At the end of the implementation of the CEF, but no later than four years after the end of the period specified in Article 1, the Commission shall carry out a final evaluation of the CEF.» Steps already passed: first work programmes «In order to provide transparency and predictability and to enhance the quality of the projects, the Commission shall adopt by 15 October 2021 the first multiannual work programmes.»; delegated acts for renewable energy projects «By 31 December 2021, the Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 26»; and the Cohesion Fund change «As of 1 January 2024, resources transferred to the CEF which have not been committed to a transport infrastructure project shall be made available to all Member States eligible for funding from the Cohesion Fund to finance transport infrastructure projects in accordance with this Regulation.» Targets cited: «the achievement of the interconnection target of at least 10 % by 2020 and 15 % by 2030»; and «uninterrupted 5G wireless broadband coverage to all urban areas by 2025» A later renewable energy step: «from 2024, may also be used to co-fund the Union renewable energy financing mechanism established under Regulation (EU) 2018/1999»

*Analytical inference:* the end of the funding period on 31 December 2027 and the delegation to 31 December 2028 are the next dated steps, so new calls under this Regulation fall inside the 2027 window; the text states no successor programme.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Whether a business can apply turns on eligible entities: «2. The following entities shall be eligible: (a) legal entities established in: (i) a Member State, including joint ventures;» «Natural persons shall not be eligible.» The route for proposals: «To be eligible, proposals shall be submitted: (a) by one or more Member States; or (b) with the agreement of the Member States concerned, by international organisations, joint undertakings, or by public or private undertakings or bodies, including regional or local authorities.» An exception for non-associated third countries: «Legal entities established in a third country which is not associated to the CEF shall exceptionally be eligible to receive Union financial support under the CEF where this is indispensable for the achievement of the objectives of a given project of common interest in the transport, energy and digital sectors or of a cross-border project in the field of renewable energy.»

*Analytical inference:* an undertaking established in a Member State can be eligible as a legal entity, but its proposal goes through a Member State or with that state's agreement. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a joint venture or a subsidiary of a non-EU group is eligible in a particular call.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Eligible transport actions. «2. In the transport sector, only the following actions shall be eligible to receive Union financial support under this Regulation», including «efficient, interconnected, interoperable and multimodal networks for the development of railway, road, inland waterway and maritime infrastructure». Ports and terminals: «actions implementing the core network in accordance with Chapter III of Regulation (EU) No 1315/2013, including actions relating to cross-border links and missing links, such as those listed in Part III of the Annex to this Regulation, as well as urban nodes, multimodal logistics platforms, maritime ports, inland ports, rail-road terminals and connections to airports of the core network». Short-sea: «actions supporting motorways of the sea as provided for in Article 21 of Regulation (EU) No 1315/2013 with a focus on cross-border short-sea shipping». Freight services: «actions supporting sustainable freight transport services in accordance with Article 32 of Regulation (EU) No 1315/2013 and actions to reduce rail freight noise». Fuels: «actions supporting new technologies and innovation, including automation, enhanced transport services, modal integration and alternative fuels infrastructure for all modes of transport in accordance with Article 33 of Regulation (EU) No 1315/2013». Rail freight: «actions promoting an increase in rail freight traffic and automatic gauge-change facilities». Digital freight systems: «including single-window services such as the maritime single window, port community systems and relevant customs information systems».

Award criteria. «Transparent award criteria shall be laid down in the work programmes referred to in Article 20 and in the calls for proposals, taking into account, to the extent applicable, only the following elements:» Freight disruption: «The assessment shall also consider whether the implementation of actions financed by the CEF risks causing disruption to freight and passenger flows on the section of the line concerned by the project and whether those risks have been mitigated.»

Rates. «(a) for works relating to the specific objectives referred to in Article 3(2), point (a)(i), the amount of Union financial support shall not exceed 30 % of the total eligible cost; however, the co-financing rates may be increased to a maximum of 50 % for the actions:» Next: «(b) for works relating to the specific objectives referred to in Article 3(2), point (a)(ii), the amount of Union financial support shall not exceed 50 % of the total eligible cost; however, the co-financing rates may be increased to a maximum of 85 % if the necessary resources are transferred to the CEF pursuant to Article 4(13)» Studies: «For studies, the amount of Union financial support shall not exceed 50 % of the total eligible cost.» Outermost regions: «a specific maximum co-funding rate of 70 % shall apply»

Blending. «The Union contribution to blending operations in the transport sector shall not exceed 10 % of the budgetary amount indicated in Article 4(2), point (a)(i), of this Regulation.»

Cost rules. «eligible costs shall not include value added tax.» and «expenditure related to the purchase of land is not an eligible cost, except for funds transferred from the Cohesion Fund in the transport sector».

Scope limit stated in a recital. «Individual digital services and applications, such as those involving various distributed ledger technologies or applying artificial intelligence, should therefore be outside the scope of the CEF»

Consequence of delay. «In addition to the grounds specified in Article 131(4) of the Financial Regulation, the amount of the grant may, except in duly justified cases, be reduced on the following grounds: (a) for studies, the action has not started within one year following the starting date indicated in the grant agreement; (b) for works, the action has not started within two years following the starting date indicated in the grant agreement; (c) following a review of the progress of the action, it is established that the implementation of the action has suffered such major delays that the objectives of the action are unlikely to be achieved;» «The grant agreement may be amended or terminated on the basis of the grounds specified in paragraph 1.» Before a decision: «Before any decision regarding the reduction or termination of a grant is taken, the case shall be examined comprehensively and the beneficiaries concerned shall be given the possibility to submit their observations within a reasonable time-frame.»

*Analytical inference:* the eligibility and rate rules fall on applicants and the Commission; the text names no obligation on a business that does not seek funding. This rests on the eligible entities and grant articles quoted. No price or surcharge effect on freight is stated.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular freight infrastructure project fits one of the eligible transport actions and the rates above.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Reports: «The beneficiaries shall submit reports as defined in the respective grant agreements without prior approval of the Member States.» Information to Member States: «During the implementation of the grant agreements the beneficiaries and the Member States concerned shall be informed by the Commission regarding changes to the grant amounts and the final amounts paid.» Decisions: «Following every call for proposals based on the work programmes referred to in Article 20, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act setting the amount of financial support to be granted to the projects selected or to parts thereof» Work programme timetable: «Those first multiannual work programmes shall include the timetable of the calls for proposals for the first three years of the CEF, their topics and indicative budget, as well as a prospective framework covering the entire programming period.»

*Analytical inference:* the reporting rests on beneficiaries under a grant agreement; a business that holds no grant has none.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation requires no system from a freight business that is not a beneficiary. A beneficiary reports under its grant agreement: «The beneficiaries shall submit reports as defined in the respective grant agreements without prior approval of the Member States.» Funded telematic systems include: «including single-window services such as the maritime single window, port community systems and relevant customs information systems»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business may meet the funded port and customs systems as a user; the text states no duty on users and no data request to them.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Costs can be eligible early: «costs incurred in respect of actions supported under this Regulation may be considered eligible as of 1 January 2021, even if they were incurred before the grant application was submitted» A Cohesion Fund allocation rule has ended: «Until 31 December 2023, the selection of projects eligible for financing shall respect the national allocations under the Cohesion Fund with regard to 70 % of the resources transferred.» and a guarantee: «shall be guaranteed until 31 December 2024» A cap ended: «Until 31 December 2025, the total amount allocated from the amount referred to in paragraph 2, point (a)(ii), to actions in a Member State eligible for funding from the Cohesion Fund shall not exceed 170 % of the share of that Member State in the total amount transferred from the Cohesion Fund.» Old actions carry on: «this Regulation shall not affect the continuation or modification of actions initiated pursuant to Regulation (EU) No 1316/2013, which shall continue to apply to those actions until their closure» The old regulations are gone: «Regulations (EU) No 1316/2013 and (EU) No 283/2014 are repealed.» Spending outside the EU is allowed in narrow cases: «only expenditure incurred in Member States is eligible, except where the project of common interest or cross-border projects in the field of renewable energy involves the territory of one or more third countries as referred to in Article 5 or Article 11(4) of this Regulation or international waters, and where the action is indispensable to the achievement of the objectives of the project concerned» Third countries: «Legal entities established in a third country which is not associated to the CEF shall exceptionally be eligible to receive Union financial support under the CEF where this is indispensable for the achievement of the objectives of a given project of common interest in the transport, energy and digital sectors or of a cross-border project in the field of renewable energy.»

*Analytical inference:* the 31 December 2023, 31 December 2024 and 31 December 2025 limits have passed, so they no longer shape new calls; this rests on the dates quoted.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2018/842 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 30 May 2018 on binding annual greenhouse gas emission reductions by Member States from 2021 to 2030», the European Union rule that gives each Member State a yearly greenhouse gas limit. Its subject: «This Regulation lays down obligations on Member States with respect to their minimum contributions for the period from 2021 to 2030 to fulfilling the Union’s target of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by 30 % below 2005 levels in 2030 in the sectors covered by Article 2 of this Regulation». Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation sets a national budget, not a company rule. Each Member State has a limit for 2030: «Each Member State shall, in 2030, limit its greenhouse gas emissions at least by the percentage set for that Member State in Annex I in relation to its greenhouse gas emissions in 2005», and a yearly path to it: «each Member State shall ensure that its greenhouse gas emissions in each year between 2021 and 2029 do not exceed the limit defined by a linear trajectory». Transport is named in the recitals: «The transport sector represents almost a quarter of the Union’s greenhouse gas emissions.» The Regulation enters into force as its last article states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .»

*Analytical inference:* the Regulation binds Member States and names no duty on a forwarder, a carrier or a shipper; a freight business meets it through national policies that governments choose to hold their yearly limit. The recitals list one such Union measure: «CO 2 -reductions from road vehicles». *Legal Confirmation Required:* which freight activities fall inside the source categories in Article 2, quoted in section 8.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight business within the next 30 days. The nearest dated steps are the Member State compliance checks: «In 2027 and 2032, if the reviewed greenhouse gas emissions of a Member State exceed its annual emission allocation for any specific year of the period, taking into account paragraph 2 of this Article and the flexibilities used pursuant to Articles 5, 6 and 7, the following measures shall apply». Those duties are the Member States'.

- A regulatory-affairs lead lists, before the 2027 compliance check, the national transport and fuel measures announced in each Member State where the business runs road or rail operations, and re-checks the list when that Member State submits a corrective action plan.
- A pricing lead adds a line to the next annual tariff review asking each national haulage or fuel supplier contract whether a new national measure justifies a clause on cost changes.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the Member State limit in Article 4 and on the corrective action plan duty in Article 8 (section 8). The Regulation sets no fee, surcharge or rate on freight. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which of a Member State's later measures bind freight operators; the Regulation itself does not say.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the Member States, the Commission, the European Environment Agency and the Central Administrator. The Commission assesses: «If the Commission finds, in its annual assessment under Article 21 of Regulation (EU) No 525/2013 and taking into account the intended use of the flexibilities referred to in Articles 5, 6 and 7 of this Regulation, that a Member State is not making sufficient progress towards meeting its obligations under Article 4 of this Regulation, that Member State shall, within three months, submit to the Commission a corrective action plan». The Central Administrator runs the registry step: «The Central Administrator shall implement the prohibition referred to in point (b) of the first subparagraph in the Union Registry.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder, a carrier and a shipper are not named; the duty runs from the Regulation to the Member State, and from the Member State to its own national measures. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any national measure carrying out Article 4 reaches a freight operator in a Member State where the business operates.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Regulation. Section 6 notes the acts the text calls for.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Implementing acts fix each Member State's yearly figures: «The Commission shall adopt implementing acts setting out the annual emission allocations for the years from 2021 to 2030 in terms of tonnes of CO 2 equivalent as specified in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article.» The power to adopt delegated acts runs «for a period of five years from 9 July 2018». Member States listed in Annex II had to say whether they would use allowance cancellation: «The Member States listed in Annex II shall notify the Commission by 31 December 2019 of any intention to make use of the limited cancellation of EU ETS allowances referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article». That date has passed. They may revise the notified use later: «The Member States listed in Annex II may decide to revise the notified percentage downwards once in 2024 and once in 2027. In such case, the Member State concerned shall notify the Commission thereof by 31 December 2024 or by 31 December 2027, respectively.» The 31 December 2024 date has passed; 31 December 2027 is ahead. The Regulation is kept under review: «The Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council, within six months of each global stocktake agreed under Article 14 of the Paris Agreement, on the operation of this Regulation».

*Analytical inference:* the 2027 and 2032 compliance checks, the December 2027 notification and the stocktake reports are the steps where Member State positions can change; the text states no outcome for any of them.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides what counts is the scope. «This Regulation applies to the greenhouse gas emissions from IPCC source categories of energy, industrial processes and product use, agriculture and waste as determined pursuant to Regulation (EU) No 525/2013, excluding greenhouse gas emissions from the activities listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC.» Aviation is handled separately: «For the purposes of this Regulation, CO 2 emissions from IPCC source category ‘1.A.3.A civil aviation’ shall be treated as zero.»

*Analytical inference:* emissions of activities listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC are outside this Regulation, and carbon dioxide from civil aviation counts as zero in it. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether road, rail or sea freight emissions of a given Member State fall in the listed source categories; the text names no transport mode in Article 2.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Targets and path (Article 4). «Each Member State shall, in 2030, limit its greenhouse gas emissions at least by the percentage set for that Member State in Annex I in relation to its greenhouse gas emissions in 2005, determined pursuant to paragraph 3 of this Article.» Annex I sets the percentage for each Member State. Scope (Article 2). «This Regulation applies to the greenhouse gas emissions from IPCC source categories of energy, industrial processes and product use, agriculture and waste as determined pursuant to Regulation (EU) No 525/2013, excluding greenhouse gas emissions from the activities listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC.»

Flexibilities (Articles 5 to 7). «In respect of the years 2021 to 2025, a Member State may borrow a quantity of up to 10 % from its annual emission allocation for the following year.» «A Member State may transfer up to 5 % of its annual emission allocation for a given year to other Member States in respect of the years 2021 to 2025, and up to 10 % in respect of the years 2026 to 2030.»

Corrective action (Article 8). «that Member State shall, within three months, submit to the Commission a corrective action plan that includes: (a) additional actions that the Member State shall implement in order to meet its specific obligations under Article 4 of this Regulation, through domestic policies and measures and the implementation of Union action».

Compliance check (Article 9). «an addition to the Member State’s greenhouse gas emission figure of the following year equal to the amount in tonnes of CO 2 equivalent of the excess greenhouse gas emissions, multiplied by a factor of 1,08» and «the Member State shall be temporarily prohibited from transferring any part of its annual emission allocation to another Member State until it is in compliance with Article 4».

Safety reserve (Article 11). «A safety reserve corresponding to a quantity of up to 105 million tonnes of CO 2 equivalent shall be established in the Union Registry, subject to the fulfilment of the Union target referred to in Article 1.»

*Analytical inference:* each duty above sits on a Member State, and the consequence for a missed limit is an addition to its next-year figure and a bar on transfers; the text states no fine, fee or rate on a company and no pass-through to freight customers. No phase-in is stated in Article 4(1). The phased borrowing and transfer shares in Article 5 are the only step series in the text.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which national measures a Member State adopts to hold its limit and whether any of them applies to a freight operator.

Obligations surveyed: 6; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 9.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets national emission limits, not rules for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Regulation keeps its accounts in the Union Registry. «The Central Administrator shall conduct an automated check on each transaction in the Union Registry that results from this Regulation and shall, where necessary, block transactions to ensure that there are no irregularities.» The records are public: «The information referred to in points (a) to (e) of paragraph 1 and in paragraph 2 shall be accessible to the public.» The Commission's yearly figures draw on inventories that Member States report: «the Commission shall carry out a comprehensive review of the most recent national inventory data for the years 2005 and 2016 to 2018 submitted by Member States pursuant to Article 7 of Regulation (EU) No 525/2013.»

*Analytical inference:* the reporting and registry duties sit on Member States, the Commission and the Central Administrator; none on a forwarder is stated.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation builds budgets and registry steps for governments and states no system for a freight business to build.

- A data lead records, at the start of each financial year, which Member State's annual emission allocation (published by the Commission as implementing acts under Article 4) covers each national operation of the business, so that a later national measure can be matched to its source.
- A regulatory-affairs lead reviews the list again on 31 December 2027, the date by which a listed Member State may notify a downward revision of its allowance cancellation.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the implementing acts in Article 4(3) and the notification in Article 6(3). *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a national measure creates a data duty for freight operators; the Regulation states none.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Some Member States may count land-use removals: «To the extent that a Member State’s greenhouse gas emissions exceed its annual emission allocations for a given year, including any annual emission allocations banked pursuant to Article 5(3) of this Regulation, a quantity up to the sum of total net removals and total net emissions from the combined land accounting categories of afforested land, deforested land, managed cropland, managed grassland and, subject to the delegated acts adopted pursuant to paragraph 2 of this Article, managed forest land and managed wetland, as referred to in points (a) and (b) of Article 2(1) of Regulation (EU) 2018/841, may be taken into account for its compliance under Article 9 of this Regulation for that year». Some may count allowance cancellation: «The Member States listed in Annex II to this Regulation may have a limited cancellation of up to a maximum of 100 million EU ETS allowances collectively taken into account for their compliance under this Regulation.» The safety reserve is limited to States with «its GDP per capita at market prices in 2013, as published by Eurostat in April 2016, was below the Union average».

*Analytical inference:* these routes let a Member State meet its limit with credits from land or from cancelled allowances; the text states no effect of them on freight. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these routes affects a company, which the text does not say.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives
