## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 30 May 2018: Regulation adopted at Strasbourg
- 9 July 2018: delegated-act power conferred on the Commission for five years
- 31 December 2019: deadline for listed Member States to notify any intended use of allowance cancellation (passed)
- 2021: first year of the 2021 to 2030 period of annual emission allocations
- 31 December 2024: last date for a listed Member State to revise its notified percentage in 2024 (passed)
- 2026: lower borrowing share and higher transfer share begin for 2026 to 2029 and 2026 to 2030
- 2027: first Member State compliance check
- 31 December 2027: last date for a listed Member State to revise its notified percentage in 2027
- 2030: Member State limit set in Annex I applies
- 2032: second Member State compliance check

The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal; the text states no calendar date for that day.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2023/2869 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 December 2023 amending certain Regulations as regards the establishment and functioning of the European single access point», a Union regulation that changes many regulations in the field of financial services and capital markets so that the information they already require to be published also goes to a collection body and appears on one Union website. Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation states is quoted from its text; what it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation supports the European single access point (ESAP) set up by Regulation (EU) 2023/2859. Its recitals give the aim: «public access to financial, non-financial and environmental-, social- and governance-related information about natural or legal persons (‘entities’) that are themselves required to make such information public, or that publicly disclose such information to a collection body on a voluntary basis, needs to be improved.» The roll-out is staged: «sufficient time should be allocated for the technical implementation of ESAP and for the collection of information to be put in place in Member States.»

The Regulation enters into force as its Article 20 states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* this is filing plumbing for the participants it names, not a freight rule. A forwarder or shipper is not named. A freight business meets it directly, because a regulation applies in the Member States without national law, only if it is itself a filer of the kinds the Regulation names (an issuer, an offeror, a person asking for admission to trading, an emission allowance market participant, an institution), or when it reads a counterparty's filings.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Regulation sets no step on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The first filing date has passed and applies now: «From 10 July 2026, when making public any information referred to in Article 1(4) points (f) and (g), Article 1(5) first subparagraph, points (e) and (f), Articles 8(5), 9(4), 10(2), 17(2), 21(1), 21(9) and 23(1) of this Regulation, the issuer, the offeror or the person asking for admission to trading on a regulated market, where relevant, shall submit that information at the same time to the relevant collection body». The next dated step falls on 10 January 2028: «From 10 January 2028, when making public any information referred to in Article 17(1) and (2) and Article 19(3) of this Regulation, the issuer or the emission allowance market participant shall submit that information at the same time to the relevant collection body». Legal persons among them need an identifier: «issuers and emission allowance market participants that are legal persons shall obtain a legal entity identifier.»

- A finance lead at a business that issues securities or offers them to the public checks, before 10 January 2028 and at each announcement of information named in Articles 17(1) and (2) and 19(3), that the announcement is also sent to the national collection body in a data extractable format with its metadata.

- A trading lead at a business that buys or sells emission allowances asks counsel, before 10 January 2028, whether the business is an emission allowance market participant under Regulation (EU) No 596/2014, because the text names that participant as a filer from that date.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the filing duties quoted above; the Regulation requires neither step of a forwarder as such. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an issuer, offeror, person asking for admission to trading or emission allowance market participant under the amended Regulations.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the issuer, the offeror, the person asking for admission to trading on a regulated market, the emission allowance market participant, credit rating agencies, PRIIPs manufacturers, institutions, the collection body, the competent authority, ESMA and Member States. The duty on market participants reads: «the issuer or the emission allowance market participant shall submit that information at the same time to the relevant collection body referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article for the purpose of making it accessible on the European single access point (ESAP)» The body that receives it varies: «the collection body as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 shall be the competent authority.» In one case: «the collection body as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 shall be ESMA.» And one conditional case: «where national law provides that a competent authority is itself permitted to make public the information referred to in Article 19(3) of this Regulation for the purpose of making that information accessible on ESAP, the collection body as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 shall be the competent authority.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder or shipper is not named. A freight business sits in the chain only as one of the named filers; the Regulation puts the filing duty on that participant and the receiving duty on the collection body. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is one of the named filers, and which collection body receives its filing.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Later steps are set by the text. For the 2028 filings: «By 9 January 2028, for the purpose of making the information referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article accessible on ESAP, Member States shall designate at least one collection body as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 and notify ESMA thereof.» For the 2030 filings: «By 9 January 2030, for the purpose of making the information referred to in paragraph 1, first subparagraph, point (b), of this Article accessible on ESAP, Member States shall designate at least one collection body as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 and notify ESMA thereof.» The technical detail comes from ESMA: «ESMA shall develop draft implementing technical standards to specify: (a) any other metadata to accompany the information; (b) the structuring of data in the information; (c) for which information a machine-readable format is required and, in such cases, which machine-readable format is to be used.»

*Analytical inference:* the 2028 date matters to issuers and emission allowance market participants; the 2030 date matters to institutions and issuers of the bonds the 2030 article names. The text sets no date for ESMA's technical standards, so the machine-readable format is open.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Filing by market participants, in the order of their dates. 10 July 2026: «From 10 July 2026, when making public any information referred to in Article 6(1) of this Regulation, the natural or legal person shall submit that information at the same time to the collection body referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article for the purpose of making it accessible on the European single access point (ESAP)» 10 January 2028 for credit rating agencies: «From 10 January 2028, when making public any information referred to in Article 8(1), Article 8(6) and (7), Article 8a(1) and (3), Article 10(1) and (4), Article 11(1) and Article 12 of this Regulation, credit rating agencies shall submit that information at the same time to the collection body referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article for the purpose of making it accessible on ESAP.» 10 January 2028 for the key information document: «From 10 January 2028, when making public the key information document referred to in Article 5(1) of this Regulation, the PRIIPs manufacturer shall submit that key information document at the same time to the relevant collection body» 10 January 2030 for institutions: «From 10 January 2030, when making public any information referred to in Part Eight of this Regulation, the institutions shall submit that information at the same time to the relevant collection body referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article for the purpose of making it accessible on the European single access point (ESAP)» 10 January 2030 for issuers of the bonds the article names: «From 10 January 2030, when making public any of the following: (a) the factsheet, the pre-issuance review related to the factsheet, annual allocation reports, the post-issuance review related to one or several annual allocation reports, the impact report, the impact report review referred to in Article 15; (b) the pre-issuance disclosures referred to in Article 20, and the periodic post-issuance disclosures referred to in Article 21; the issuer shall submit that information at the same time to the relevant collection body»

Form of the filing. It is «be submitted in a data extractable format as defined in Article 2, point (3), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 or, where required by Union law, in a machine-readable format, as defined in Article 2, point (4), of that Regulation;» It carries metadata: «(iv) the type of information, as classified pursuant to Article 7(4), point (c), of that Regulation; (v) an indication of whether the information contains personal data.»

*No penalty: the source states no penalty, fine or enforcement consequence for a filer.*

*Analytical inference:* each duty falls on the named filer, who must send the information at the same time as it makes it public; the Regulation states no fine, charge or freight rate effect, so any cost to a freight business is a gap. No exceptions are stated in Articles 11a, 21a, 13a, 29a, 434b and 15a as inserted. No scope limits are stated in Articles 11a, 21a, 13a, 29a, 434b and 15a as inserted.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which of the named filing duties, if any, applies to the business and from which date.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Filers register an identifier and Member States name receiving bodies. Identifier: «For the purposes of paragraph 1, point (b)(ii), issuers, offerors, or persons asking for admission to trading on a regulated market that are legal persons shall obtain a legal entity identifier.» Bodies: see Section 6 for the dates by which Member States designate a collection body and notify ESMA. Guidelines: «Where necessary, ESMA shall adopt guidelines for entities to ensure that the metadata submitted in accordance with paragraph 5, first subparagraph, point (a), are correct.»

*Analytical inference:* a legal entity identifier is needed by a filer before its first filing; the registration step for any act sits in that act, and the text states no registration of a forwarder as such.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks filers to submit at the same time as they publish, in a data extractable format with metadata (Section 8). No step is due from a freight operator that is not one of the named filers.

- A finance lead at a business that already publishes regulated announcements asks, at the next announcement, the person who prepares it whether the same file can go to the collection body in a data extractable format with the metadata listed, and whether the business holds a legal entity identifier.

- A data lead, ahead of 10 January 2028, confirms with the national competent authority which body is the collection body for the business's announcements, because the Regulation names the competent authority in some cases and ESMA in others.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the same-time filing, format and receiving-body rules above; the text states no data a forwarder must keep as a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is one of the named filers.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «The Environmental Targets (Fine Particulate Matter) (England) Regulations 2023 Made 30th January 2023 Coming into force in accordance with regulation 1», a United Kingdom statutory instrument. Its jurisdiction is England: «These Regulations extend to England and Wales but apply in relation to England only.» The source states the legal basis: «The Secretary of State makes these Regulations in exercise of the powers conferred by sections 1, 2, 6(1) and 143(1) of the Environment Act 2021». What the Regulations say is stated from their own text; what that means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. The text appears on legislation.gov.uk as: «You are here: UK Statutory Instruments 2023 No. 96».

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulations set two air quality targets for fine particles (PM 2.5), which are very small particles in outdoor air. The explanatory note says what they do: «These Regulations, which apply to England, set— a target in respect of the annual mean concentration of PM 2.5 (fine particulate matter) in ambient air under section 2 of the Environment Act 2021 (c.30) (“the annual mean concentration target”), and a long-term target to reduce population exposure to PM 2.5 (fine particulate matter), within the priority area of air quality under section 1 of that Act (“the population exposure reduction target”)». The first target: «The annual mean concentration target is that by the end of 31st December 2040 the annual mean level of PM 2.5 in ambient air must be equal to or less than 10 µg/m³ (“the target level”)». The second target: «The population exposure reduction target is that there is at least a 35% reduction in population exposure by the end of 31st December 2040 (“the target date”), as compared with the average population exposure in the three-year period from 1st January 2016 to 31st December 2018 (“the baseline period”)».

The instrument enters into force as its text states: «(2) Subject to paragraph (3), these Regulations come into force on the day after the day on which they are made. (3) Paragraph 3(1)(b) of Schedule 2 comes into force on 1st January 2024.» The commencement note reads «Reg. 1 in force at 31.1.2023, see reg. 1(2)».

*Analytical inference:* the Regulations set targets and monitoring rules for the Secretary of State and state no duty, fee or charge on a freight business. This rests on the targets above and on the duties in section 4, which all name the Secretary of State. The text names road traffic only in describing where some monitoring stations are sited (section 8).

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The nearest dated step in the text is the one for the number of monitoring stations: «From 1st January 2028— (a) the total number of monitoring stations in each zone, and (b) the number of those monitoring stations which are— (i) at urban background or suburban background sites; (ii) at near-source sites, must be not less than the minimum numbers specified in the following table.». That step binds the Secretary of State, and 1st January 2028 is more than a year away.

- Before 1st January 2028, a regulatory-affairs lead at a road or port operator in England reads the published station locations and checks which stations sit near the sites the business runs, so the business knows which local readings feed the national targets.

*Analytical inference:* the action rests on the publication duty in section 4 (the zone and location of each station is published) and carries no legal duty for the business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any local air quality measure that later relies on these targets would apply to the business is not stated in these Regulations and needs counsel when such a measure appears.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The only duty holder named is the Secretary of State. The monitoring duty: «(1) The Secretary of State must ensure that the requirements in Schedule 2 (relating to the location and number of monitoring stations and position of monitoring equipment) are met.». The publication duty: «(1) The Secretary of State must publish on a website the information specified in Schedule 3.». The source states no role for a forwarder, carrier, shipper or port operator. The explanatory note records that an impact assessment exists: «A full impact assessment of the effect that this instrument will have on the costs of business, the voluntary sector and the public sector is available from the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs».

*Analytical inference:* a freight business has no place in the compliance chain of these Regulations; it is affected, if at all, by separate measures that a later instrument would have to set. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business is ever named as a duty holder in separate air quality rules that use these targets.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for these Regulations; the stored text holds the Regulations, their Schedules and the explanatory note only.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text sets dated steps, some still ahead. The monitoring network steps up: «Until 31st December 2027— (a) the total number of monitoring stations in each zone must be not less than the number of AQSR monitoring stations in that zone immediately before the coming into force of these Regulations; (b) at least one monitoring station in each zone must be at an urban background or suburban background site.» and then «From 1st January 2028— (a) the total number of monitoring stations in each zone, and (b) the number of those monitoring stations which are— (i) at urban background or suburban background sites; (ii) at near-source sites, must be not less than the minimum numbers specified in the following table.» The table of minimum numbers by zone population reads «Population of zone (thousands) Minimum total number of monitoring stations Minimum number of monitoring stations at urban background or suburban background sites Minimum number of monitoring stations at near-source sites ≥ 6,000 15 10 5 4,750 – 5,999 11 7 4 3,750 – 4,749 10 6 4 2,750 – 3,749 9 6 3 1,000 – 2,749 6 4 2 250 – 999 3 2 1 <250 2 1 1». The reporting dates for both targets fall in 2041: «For the purposes of section 6(1) of the 2021 Act the reporting date for the annual mean concentration target is 15th July 2041.» and «the reporting date for the population exposure reduction target is 15th July 2041.». Earlier steps have passed: «The following are to be calculated by 15th July 2023— (a) the Population Exposure Indicator for the baseline period (“PEIbase”); (b) the Population Exposure Indicator for each of the years 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022; (c) the Reference Indicator for each of the years 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022;». Annual calculation continues: «The following are to be calculated for each year from 2023 onwards (“year n”), by 15th July in the following year».

*Analytical inference:* from 1st January 2028 each zone must have at least the minimum numbers of stations in the table by zone population. The text states no content for the report beyond the reporting date.

## 7. Threshold Questions

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulations bind the Secretary of State and set no test of whether a business falls in scope.*

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Annual mean target. «The annual mean concentration target is that by the end of 31st December 2040 the annual mean level of PM 2.5 in ambient air must be equal to or less than 10 µg/m³ (“the target level”)»

Population exposure target. «The population exposure reduction target is that there is at least a 35% reduction in population exposure by the end of 31st December 2040 (“the target date”), as compared with the average population exposure in the three-year period from 1st January 2016 to 31st December 2018 (“the baseline period”)» The baseline is «the average population exposure in the three-year period from 1st January 2016 to 31st December 2018».

Measurement method. «(1) The Secretary of State must ensure that PM 2.5 levels at each monitoring station are assessed as follows.» «Fixed measurements of PM 2.5 must be taken either continuously or at hourly or other regular intervals which are not less frequent than once per day»

Data capture. «The minimum annual data capture requirement for a monitoring station is that fixed measurements of PM 2.5 levels are taken, and the data from such measurements are ratified, for at least 85% of the hours in a year»

Scope of the monitoring rules. «Scope of this Part E+W 11. This Part applies in relation to monitoring and assessment of PM 2.5 levels carried out for the purposes of the annual mean concentration target and the population exposure reduction target.»

Existing stations. «Subject to any determination under paragraph (3)(b), every AQSR monitoring station which was in operation immediately before the coming into force of this regulation is a monitoring station for the purposes of these Regulations.»

Roadside stations. «Monitoring stations at near-source sites where the main nearby source of pollution is traffic emissions from a road must be— (a) not more than 10 metres from the kerbside of the road;»

*Analytical inference:* every obligation above falls on the Secretary of State; the text names no obligation on a business. This rests on the monitoring and assessment duties quoted above. No cost, penalty or price effect for freight is stated.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any operator duty arises under separate legislation that cites these targets; none is stated here.

Obligations surveyed: 8; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 9.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulations set air quality targets and monitoring rules, not product rules.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Secretary of State publishes information: «(1) The Secretary of State must publish on a website the information specified in Schedule 3.» The timing: «The information must be published within a reasonable time after» the information is available. The list begins with: «In relation to each monitoring station— E+W (a) its zone and location;» No registration or reporting duty falls on a business.

*Analytical inference:* these publication duties fall on the Secretary of State; the text states none on a freight business.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulations require no system from a freight business. The system work sits with the Secretary of State, who has this duty: «(1) The Secretary of State must ensure that the requirements in Schedule 2 (relating to the location and number of monitoring stations and position of monitoring equipment) are met.». The source describes the sites some stations measure: «“ near-source ” means a site in a location where the PM 2.5 level is likely to be elevated above the background level due to the influence of one or more sources of pollution in close proximity to the site, such as emissions from traffic from a major road or from nearby industrial sources».

*Analytical inference:* the text describes near-source sites as places where PM 2.5 is likely to be raised by traffic from a major road or nearby industrial sources; it names no freight business and sets no duty or cost on one.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

One edge in the measurement rule: the 2040 annual mean target is judged at stations that are measured «disregarding any periods during that year in which the monitoring station is temporarily out of operation, for example for repair or maintenance». *Analytical inference:* a station out of service for repair does not drop out of the test, because the text disregards such periods.

- 15th July 2023: first calculations due under Schedule 1 (past)

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2023/2859 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 December 2023 establishing a European single access point providing centralised access to publicly available information of relevance to financial services, capital markets and sustainability», the Union regulation that sets up one website where the public can find the financial and sustainability information that companies and financial firms must already publish. Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation states is quoted from its text; what it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation names the body that builds and runs the website and what goes on it: «By 10 July 2027, ESMA shall establish and operate a European single access point (ESAP) providing centralised electronic access to the following information: (a) information made public pursuant to the Union legislative acts listed in the Annex or pursuant to any further legally binding Union acts that provide for centralised electronic access to information on ESAP; (b) information that any entity governed by the law of a Member State chooses to make accessible on ESAP on a voluntary basis». It adds no new content duty: «ESAP should not create any new disclosure requirements in terms of content». Reading the site is free for users: «ESMA shall ensure that access to information on ESAP is provided on a non-discriminatory basis and that users have direct and immediate access free of charge to the information on ESAP.»

The Regulation enters into force as its Article 15 states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* this is infrastructure, not a freight rule. A forwarder or shipper is not named. A freight business meets it only if it files information that the listed Union acts require to be made public (the filing duty sits in those acts, not here), if it chooses to submit information voluntarily, or when it reads a counterparty's filings.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Regulation sets no step on a freight operator within the next 30 days. Its next dated step falls on ESMA: «By 10 July 2027, ESMA shall establish and operate a European single access point (ESAP)». Filings do not arrive early: «The information referred to in paragraph 1, point (a), of this Article shall not be submitted to collection bodies for the purpose of being made accessible on ESAP before the date of application of the requirement to submit that information as provided for in the Union legislative acts listed in the Annex». Reading is free but heavy use is not: «ESMA shall, however, charge fees for specific services with high maintenance and support costs or that involve searches for and downloads of large volumes of information.» «ESMA shall publish and make easily accessible on the ESAP website the fee structure, the volume thresholds, if relevant, and the rates.»

- A compliance lead, from 10 July 2027, adds ESAP to the places checked at the next counterparty review for a customer's or supplier's published filings, once the counterparty's own filing date under the listed act has passed.

- A data lead who expects to download filings in bulk reads the fee structure and rates when ESMA publishes them on the ESAP website, before planning any volume download.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the free access rule and the fee rule quoted above; the Regulation requires neither step of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any act listed in the Annex makes a business of the reader's kind a filer.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names ESMA, the collection bodies, the entities that submit, the Joint Committee of the European Supervisory Authorities, the Commission and Member States. An entity is defined: «‘entity’ means any natural or legal person: (a) that is required to submit the information referred to in Article 1(1), point (a), to a collection body; or (b) that submits information to a collection body on a voluntary basis pursuant to Article 1(1), point (b), in order for that information to be made accessible on ESAP;» A collection body is defined: «‘collection body’ means a Union body, office or agency or national body, authority or register designated as such pursuant to any of the Union legislative acts under Article 1(1), point (a), or designated as such by a Member State in accordance with Article 3(2);» The entity carries the accuracy duty: «Entities shall be responsible for the completeness and accuracy of the information in the language in which it is submitted, as well as for the relevant accompanying metadata they submit to the collection bodies.» And the rework duty: «Where the information submitted by an entity pursuant to Article 1(1), point (a), is rejected or removed by a collection body, that entity shall rectify and resubmit the information without undue delay.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder or shipper is not named. A freight business sits in the chain only as an entity, that is, a person that must submit information under a listed act or that submits voluntarily; the Regulation puts the accuracy and resubmission duties on that entity. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an entity under either limb of the definition.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text sets later steps. Technical standards: «The ESAs shall submit those draft implementing technical standards to the Commission by 10 September 2024.» That date has passed. For voluntary submissions: «The ESAs shall submit the draft implementing technical standards to the Commission by 10 January 2028.» Site features: «ESMA shall ensure that ESAP provides for the functionalities referred to in paragraph 1, points (e) and (g), by 10 July 2028.» «ESMA shall ensure that ESAP provides for the functionalities referred to in paragraph 1, point (h), by 9 January 2030.» Member State bodies for voluntary filings: «By 9 January 2030, each Member State shall designate at least one collection body for the collection of information submitted on a voluntary basis and notify ESMA thereof.» Commission review: «By 10 January 2029 the Commission shall, in close cooperation with ESMA, and taking into account the annual reports referred to in Article 12, submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the implementation, functioning and effectiveness of ESAP.» The review can slow the roll-out: «The Commission shall adopt a delegated act in accordance with Article 14 amending the Union legislative acts referred to in the second subparagraph of this paragraph in order to postpone the inclusion on ESAP of information for which submission to ESAP is not yet required or permitted pursuant to Article 1(1), point (a), by a maximum of 36 months if the Commission concludes in the report referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article that there is evidence of severe and pervasive difficulties»

*Analytical inference:* the 2027 date is when ESAP must exist; the 2028 and 2030 dates add site features and voluntary filing. A postponement of up to 36 months applies only to information whose submission is not yet required or permitted and only on the evidence the Commission report finds, so the dates for a given filing are not final until that report.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides what appears on the site is which information is in scope. Two limbs are set by Article 1(1) above; historical information has its own rule: «‘historical information’ means the information referred to in Article 1(1), point (a), that was made public no earlier than five years before the date of application of the requirement to submit that information to ESAP;» For voluntary filings, scope is a condition of each submission: «ensure that the information submitted falls within the scope of Article 1(1), point (b);»

*Analytical inference:* the filing duty for any given company comes from the act listed in the Annex that applies to it, not from this Regulation. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which listed act, if any, applies to the business and from which date.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Voluntary submission. «From 10 January 2030, an entity may submit the information referred to in Article 1(1), point (b), to the collection body in the Member State where the entity has its registered office for the purpose of making that information accessible on ESAP.» Each submission carries a mark and a format: «ensure that the information is accompanied by metadata specifying that the information is made accessible on ESAP on a voluntary basis; (b) ensure that the information is accompanied by metadata specifying whether the information contains personal data;» «use a data extractable format for submitting the information; (e) ensure that the information submitted falls within the scope of Article 1(1), point (b); (f) ensure that no personal data are included in the information, except where the personal data are required by Union or national law or constitute a necessary element of the information about the entity’s economic activities.»

Consequence of a defective filing. «The collection bodies shall reject information submitted by entities where the automated validations referred to in paragraph 1, point (c), of this Article reveal that the information does not comply with the requirements laid down in that point»

Collection body and site duties. «ensure that the information referred to in Article 1(1) remains available to ESAP for at least 10 years, unless otherwise provided in the Union legislative acts under Article 1(1), point (a).» «ensure that ESAP is accessible for at least 97 % of the time per month, excluding cases of scheduled maintenance, content updates and page upgrades» «ESMA may notify the collection bodies of deficiencies identified and suspend making information accessible on ESAP.»

*Analytical inference:* the consequence the Regulation states for an entity is rejection of a defective filing and a duty to rectify and resubmit; ESMA may suspend display of information it finds deficient. The Regulation states no fine, charge or freight rate effect on an entity, so a cost to a freight business is a gap. No phase-in is stated in Article 5 beyond the dates in Section 14.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a rejected or suspended filing by the business would breach the duty in the listed act that requires the filing.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Regulation asks for lists and reports from ESMA and Member States. Lists: «ESMA shall publish a list of the collection bodies, containing the uniform resource locator of each collection body, on the web portal referred to in Article 7(1), point (a).» Reports: «shall monitor the functioning of ESAP based on at least the qualitative and quantitative indicators laid down in paragraph 2, and shall publish and submit to the European Parliament and to the Council an annual report on the functioning of ESAP.» Searches use an identifier: «(b) the legal entity identifier of the entity that submitted the information and of the legal person to which the information relates;» A Member State also names bodies for voluntary filings, as Section 6 states.

*Analytical inference:* an entity that files should hold a legal entity identifier because the site's search runs on it; the registration duty for a given act sits in that act, not here, and the text states no registration of a forwarder as such.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks filers to be able to submit once to one collection body, in a data extractable format with complete metadata: «Entities may choose to submit information only once and to one collection body only. The submission and any re-submission of information, together with the relevant accompanying metadata, shall be made to the same collection body.» The automated check is «(i) it has been submitted using a data extractable format or, where appropriate, the machine-readable format specified in any of the Union legislative acts under Article 1(1), point (a), pursuant to which the information is submitted; (ii) the metadata for the information, as specified pursuant to paragraph 10, point (e), of this Article and, where applicable, Article 3(1), point (a), is available and complete;»

- A finance lead at a business that files under a listed act asks, at the next filing preparation, the person who prepares the filing whether it is produced in a data extractable format with its metadata complete, because the collection body rejects a filing that fails the automated check.

- A data lead, when the business first submits voluntarily from 10 January 2030, sends all of one filing and any resubmission to the same collection body.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the format, metadata and single-body rules above; the text states no data a forwarder must keep as a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an entity that must file.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Some users and cases are treated apart. Free access is kept for named users, including «(h) entities providing and using information on ESAP to fulfil their regulatory obligations.» Collection bodies may refuse some filings: «The collection bodies may reject information submitted by entities where the information is manifestly inappropriate, abusive or outside the scope of the information referred to in Article 1(1).» Liability is limited: «Neither ESMA nor the collection bodies shall bear any liability for the access, use or re-use of information submitted by entities to the collection bodies and made accessible on ESAP.»

*Analytical inference:* the free access list, rejection grounds and liability limit are rules for ESMA and the collection bodies; for a freight business they matter as the conditions under which its filings are accepted and read.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COMMISSION DELEGATED REGULATION (EU) 2025/843 of 5 May 2025 amending Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards UV-328», an act of the European Commission for the European Union. Its jurisdictional scope is every Member State: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» It adds the chemical UV-328 to the Union's list of persistent organic pollutants and sets dated limits and dated exemptions for articles that contain it. What the Regulation says is taken from its own text. What it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation carries a global chemicals treaty into Union law. The recitals say what the treaty asks of its parties: «Each Party to the Convention is required to prohibit the chemicals on the list and/or take the legal and administrative measures necessary to eliminate their production, use, import and export.» The parties to that treaty agreed to list the chemical: «to amend Annex A to the Convention to include UV-328 in that Annex with specific exemptions.» The amending step is short: «Annex I to Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation.» The effect of listing is stated in a recital: «Article 3 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 prohibits the manufacturing, placing on the market and use of substances listed in Annex I to that Regulation whether on their own, in mixtures or in articles.» Import of the chemical in goods was still open before this Regulation: «In absence of an authorisation under Regulation (EU) No 1907/2006, UV-328 cannot be used in the EU, but it can still be imported in articles.» The Regulation enters into force as its Article 2 states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .»

*Analytical inference:* the goods the Regulation reaches are articles that contain UV-328, and the exemptions name land-based motor vehicles, aircraft, rail transportation vehicles, spare parts, polarisers, photographic paper and blood collection tube separators. The text names no forwarder, so any freight exposure comes through the goods a client ships.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in the Regulation falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The nearest dated step ahead is the second trace limit: «(b) 10 mg/kg (0,001 % by weight) from 4 August 2027;». The exemptions for vehicles, coatings, aircraft and several other articles run to a later date: «(a) in land-based motor vehicles, until 4 August 2030;»

- A customer-compliance lead asks each customer that ships land-based motor vehicles, aircraft, rail transportation vehicles or spare parts for them into the Union, at the booking of the next such shipment, whether the articles contain UV-328 and, if so, which point of the Annex exemption list covers them.
- A compliance lead asks the same customers, before 4 August 2027, whether their articles meet the lower trace limit of 10 mg/kg that applies from that date.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the exemption list and the trace limit in the Annex. The Regulation requires neither of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular article of a client falls under one of the exemption points of the Annex and who carries the duty for it under Regulation (EU) 2019/1021.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names the Commission, the Member States, the Parties to the Convention, the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) and airlines of the Union. The recitals record: «ECHA held a call for information». An exemption is justified by airlines: «To avoid serious consequences for EU airlines, an exemption that allows continued delivery of such aircrafts and spare parts for aircrafts should be granted.» The duty in the parent Regulation is to prohibit manufacturing, placing on the market and use (Section 2). A forwarder, carrier or importer is not named.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits outside the named compliance chain; any exposure comes through the goods of its clients. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that holds goods, or that clears them for a client, is a party to which the prohibition on placing on the market in Regulation (EU) 2019/1021 applies.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Regulation sets its dates in the Annex itself, three trace limit steps and the end of the exemptions. The steps: «(a) 100 mg/kg (0,01 % by weight) from 4 August 2025; (b) 10 mg/kg (0,001 % by weight) from 4 August 2027; (c) 1 mg/kg (0,0001 % by weight) from 4 August 2029;». Aircraft spare parts run to a later date: «(i) in spare parts for civilian and military aircrafts where UV-328 was initially used in their production, until 31 December 2030.» The last date in the Annex is for spare parts of machines and displays: «until the end of their service life or 31 December 2043, whichever comes earlier;». The text names no implementing act or guidance still to come.

*Analytical inference:* the first step has passed; the steps in 2027 and 2029 are ahead, as are the exemption end dates from 2030. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a Member State or the Commission has published guidance on the trace limit since this text.

## 7. Threshold Questions

One condition decides whether a spare part is covered: «where UV-328 was initially used in their production». It sits on the exemption points for spare parts. *Analytical inference:* a spare part that did not contain UV-328 when first made is not within that exemption point on its wording. *Legal Confirmation Required:* how a client shows that UV-328 was initially used in the production of a spare part.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Trace limit. «For the purposes of this entry, Article 4(1), point (b), shall apply to concentrations of UV-328 equal to or below: (a) 100 mg/kg (0,01 % by weight) from 4 August 2025; (b) 10 mg/kg (0,001 % by weight) from 4 August 2027; (c) 1 mg/kg (0,0001 % by weight) from 4 August 2029; where they are present in substances, mixtures or articles.» The recital explains the purpose: «a limit value should be set for UV-328 occurring as an unintentional trace contaminant in substances, mixtures or articles.»

Exemptions for articles. «By way of derogation, the placing on the market of UV-328 present in articles and the use of such articles shall be allowed for the following purposes: (a) in land-based motor vehicles, until 4 August 2030; (b) in industrial coating for land-based motor vehicles, engineering machines, rail transportation vehicles, and in heavy-duty coatings for large steel structures, until 4 August 2030; (c) in mechanical separators in blood collection tubes, until 4 August 2030; (d) in triacetyl cellulose film in polarisers, until 4 August 2030; (e) in photographic paper, until 4 August 2030; (f) in civilian and military aircrafts, until 4 August 2030;» The column of the Annex is headed «Specific exemption on intermediate use or other specification».

Spare parts. «(g) in spare parts for any of the following: (i) land-based motor vehicles; (ii) stationary industrial machines for use in agriculture, forestry and construction; (iii) liquid crystal displays in instruments for analysis, measurements, control, monitoring, testing, production and inspection, other than for medical applications; where UV-328 was initially used in their production, until the end of their service life or 31 December 2043, whichever comes earlier;» «(h) in spare parts for any of the following: (i) liquid crystal displays in devices within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2017/745, and within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2017/746 of the European Parliament and of the Council ( *1 ) ; (ii) liquid crystal displays in instruments for analysis, measurements, control, testing, production and inspection; where UV-328 was initially used in their production, until the end of their service life;» «(i) in spare parts for civilian and military aircrafts where UV-328 was initially used in their production, until 31 December 2030.»

Continued use. «Articles containing UV-328 already in use in the Union before or on the date of expiry of the relevant exemption laid down in point 2(a) to (i) may continue to be used.»

*Analytical inference:* the exemptions are written as permissions for the placing on the market of UV-328 in articles and for the use of those articles; the Annex states no duty on a freight business and no cost. No phase-in is stated outside the trace limit steps above.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which party must show that an article falls under an exemption point, and what proof a Member State accepts.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks a freight business to build no system and states no cost or penalty. A customer-compliance lead can add a UV-328 question to the booking or onboarding form for vehicles, aircraft, rail vehicles, spare parts, polarisers and photographic paper, at the next form revision, and a compliance lead can record the exemption point a customer names, so the answer is held before the 4 August 2027 step.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the Annex lists and the dated trace limit; the Regulation requires neither of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether holding a customer's UV-328 statement is enough for the business, or whether a Member State asks for more.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Regulation holds its exemptions and its continued use rule in the Annex (Section 8). The recital gives the reason for the continued use rule: «In this regard, it should be clarified that articles that contain UV-328 and that are produced or placed on the market under an exemption laid down in Annex I to that Regulation and that were already in use on the expiry date of the relevant exemption, are allowed to continue to be used after that date.» The vehicles covered are defined: «Land-based motor vehicles include cars, motorcycles, agricultural and construction motor vehicles and industrial trucks, including motor vehicles covered by Regulations (EU) 2018/858 ( 6 ) , (EU) No 167/2013 ( 7 ) and (EU) No 168/2013 ( 8 ) of the European Parliament and of the Council.»

*Analytical inference:* an industrial truck is within the recital's definition of a land-based motor vehicle; that is wording of a recital, not of the Annex. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular vehicle or machine of a client is a land-based motor vehicle for the Annex.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

The recitals record what the Commission learned before setting the exemptions. ECHA gathered comments: «The comments submitted support the need for the specific exemptions included in Decision SC-11/11 of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention, such as for land-based motor vehicles, mechanical separators in blood collection tubes, polarizers, photographic paper and for spare parts.» The public feedback mechanism brought a point on aircraft: «Information has been provided through the public feedback mechanism that many aircrafts that are to be delivered to EU airlines in the next 5 years and spare parts for such aircrafts contain UV-328.»

The Regulation enters into force as its Article 2 sets, on the twentieth day after publication in the Official Journal of the European Union; the captured text gives no other calendar date for it. It is dated by its closing line: «Done at Brussels, 5 May 2025.»

- 4 August 2030: end of the exemptions for motor vehicles, coatings, blood collection tube separators, polariser film, photographic paper and aircraft

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) 2023/1670 of 16 June 2023 laying down ecodesign requirements for smartphones, mobile phones other than smartphones, cordless phones and slate tablets pursuant to Directive 2009/125/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council and amending Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/826», an EU regulation published in the «Official Journal of the European Union». Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» Its scope: «This Regulation establishes ecodesign requirements for the placing on the market of smartphones, other mobile phones, cordless phones and slate tablets.» What the Regulation says is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation sets design rules for phones and tablets sold in the EU: how long spare parts and software updates must be available, how robust a device must be and what information must be published. It does not cover everything: «This Regulation does not apply to the following products: (a) mobile phones and tablets with a flexible main display which the user can unroll and roll up partly or fully; (b) smartphones for high security communication.» The requirements: «The ecodesign requirements set out in Annex II shall apply from the dates indicated therein.» The recital explains the lead time: «The entry into application of ecodesign requirements should be 21 months after the entry into force of this Regulation, in order to give manufacturers sufficient time to redesign their products subject to this Regulation.» It was adopted at Brussels: «Done at Brussels, 16 June 2023.»

The Regulation enters into force as its text states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 20 June 2025. Article 6 shall apply from 20 September 2023.»

*Analytical inference:* the duties sit on manufacturers, importers and authorised representatives; a freight business has no ecodesign duty of its own. Freight is touched through the goods it moves and through the service levels a client must meet, such as spare part delivery times (section 3).

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days, and the main application date has passed. The date: «It shall apply from 20 June 2025.». The delivery commitment a client carries: «(i) during the first 5 years of the period referred to in points 1(a) and (c), spare parts are delivered within 5 working days after having received the order; (ii) during the remaining 2 years of the period referred to in points 1(a) and (c), spare parts are delivered within 10 working days after having received the order» A separate rule applied earlier: «Article 6 shall apply from 20 September 2023.»

- At the next contract review with a client that places smartphones or tablets on the EU market, an account lead asks whether the client spare parts delivery commitment of 5 working days for the first 5 years and 10 working days for the remaining 2 years is built into the transport service levels.

*Analytical inference:* the action rests on the delivery times above, which bind the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative and not a carrier; the Regulation states no transport duty. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that places products on the EU market for a client counts as an importer or authorised representative under this Regulation.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The duty holders named are manufacturers, importers and authorised representatives, with Member State authorities checking. Spare parts duty: «manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall make available to professional repairers and end-users at least the following spare parts, including required fasteners, if not reusable, until at least 7 years after the date of end of placement on the market» Anti-circumvention: «Manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall not place on the market products designed to alter their behaviour or properties when tested by Member State authorities performing checks on product compliance, in order to reach a more favourable result for any of the declared values of the parameters covered by ecodesign requirements included in this Regulation applicable at the time of the placing on the market of the products.» Conformity assessment: «The conformity assessment procedure as referred to in Article 8 of Directive 2009/125/EC shall be the internal design control system set out in Annex IV to that Directive or the management system set out in Annex V to that Directive.» Market surveillance: «Member States shall apply the verification procedure laid down in Annex IV to this Regulation when performing the market surveillance checks referred to in Article 3(2) of Directive 2009/125/EC.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder, carrier or warehouse operator is not named; a freight business meets the duty only if it is also the importer or authorised representative of a product. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether such a role arises when a freight business clears or imports goods for a client.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Which products are in scope turns on the scope article: «This Regulation establishes ecodesign requirements for the placing on the market of smartphones, other mobile phones, cordless phones and slate tablets.» The exclusions: «This Regulation does not apply to the following products: (a) mobile phones and tablets with a flexible main display which the user can unroll and roll up partly or fully; (b) smartphones for high security communication.»

*Analytical inference:* only the four product groups named are covered, so other consumer electronics fall outside this Regulation. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular device on a client's range is a smartphone, mobile phone, cordless phone or slate tablet as the Annex I definitions define them.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Spare parts, smartphones. «manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall make available to professional repairers at least the following spare parts, including required fasteners, if not reusable, until at least 7 years after the date of end of placement on the market, when present:» Also: «manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall make available to professional repairers and end-users at least the following spare parts, including required fasteners, if not reusable, until at least 7 years after the date of end of placement on the market»

Delivery time. «(i) during the first 5 years of the period referred to in points 1(a) and (c), spare parts are delivered within 5 working days after having received the order; (ii) during the remaining 2 years of the period referred to in points 1(a) and (c), spare parts are delivered within 10 working days after having received the order»

Spare part prices. «manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall provide indicative pre-tax prices at least in euro for spare parts listed in points 1(a) and (c), including the pre-tax price of fasteners and tools, if supplied with the spare part, on the free access website of the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative»

Serialised parts. «provide non-discriminatory access for professional repairers to any software tools, firmware or similar auxiliary means needed to ensure the full functionality of those spare parts and of the device in which such spare parts are installed during and after the replacement» The timing: «shall provide access to the software tools, firmware or similar auxiliary means referred to in points (a) and (b) within 3 working days after having received the request»

Robustness. «Manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall ensure that the devices pass 45 falls without any protective foil or separate protective cover, except for foldable smartphones designed to be used with a protective foil on the foldable display» «the screen of the device passes the hardness level 4 on the Mohs hardness scale»; and «protected against the ingress of solid foreign objects of size bigger than 1 millimeter and splashing of water»

Battery. «Manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall ensure that the devices achieve at least 800 cycles at 80 % remaining capacity» «manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall provide a power management feature which by default ensures that once the battery is fully charged there is no further charging power supplied to the battery unless the charge level drops below 95 % of its maximum charge capacity.»

Software. «from the date of end of placement on the market to at least 5 years after that date, manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall, if they provide security updates, corrective updates or functionality updates to an operating system, make such updates available at no cost for all units of a product model with the same operating system»

Plastic marking. «plastic components heavier than 50 g shall be marked by specifying the type of polymer»

Cordless phones. «the networked standby power consumption Pn of a base station shipped with a cordless phone shall not exceed 1 W, regardless of whether a handset is on the base station»

Circumvention. «Manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall not place on the market products designed to alter their behaviour or properties when tested by Member State authorities performing checks on product compliance, in order to reach a more favourable result for any of the declared values of the parameters covered by ecodesign requirements included in this Regulation applicable at the time of the placing on the market of the products.»

Scope exclusions. «This Regulation does not apply to the following products: (a) mobile phones and tablets with a flexible main display which the user can unroll and roll up partly or fully; (b) smartphones for high security communication.»

Enforcement consequence. «Where a model is not in conformity with the requirements laid down in Article 6 of this Regulation, the model and all equivalent models shall be considered not compliant.»

*Analytical inference:* each requirement above falls on the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative; the text names no obligation on a carrier or forwarder. This rests on the duty holders named in each quoted sentence. No price effect or surcharge on freight is stated.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that places these products on the market for a client carries any of these duties; the Regulation does not say.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Information to publish: «Manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall provide in the technical documentation and make publicly available on free access websites of the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative the following information:» Technical documentation: «the technical documentation shall contain a copy of the product information provided in accordance with Annex II to this Regulation, and the details and the results of the calculations set out in Annex III to this Regulation» Dismantling information: «The information referred to in point (1) shall be available until at least 15 years after the placing on the market of the last unit of a product model.» Spare part prices: «manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall provide indicative pre-tax prices at least in euro for spare parts listed in points 1(a) and (c), including the pre-tax price of fasteners and tools, if supplied with the spare part, on the free access website of the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative»

*Analytical inference:* these publication and documentation duties fall on the manufacturer, importer or authorised representative; the text states none on a freight business.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation requires no system from a freight business. Systems sit with the product supplier: «provide non-discriminatory access for professional repairers to any software tools, firmware or similar auxiliary means needed to ensure the full functionality of those spare parts and of the device in which such spare parts are installed during and after the replacement» with the timing «shall provide access to the software tools, firmware or similar auxiliary means referred to in points (a) and (b) within 3 working days after having received the request» The technical documentation: «the technical documentation shall contain a copy of the product information provided in accordance with Annex II to this Regulation, and the details and the results of the calculations set out in Annex III to this Regulation» For a pack without a charger the instructions carry this: «For environmental reasons this package does not include a charger.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight operator that handles repair returns may see requests tied to serialised parts access, but the text states no duty or request to it.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Plastic marking has an exemption: «Plastic components shall be exempt from marking requirements provided the following conditions are fulfilled:» Foldable smartphones have a separate drop test: «Manufacturers, importers or authorised representatives shall ensure that the devices pass 45 falls without any protective foil or separate protective cover, except for foldable smartphones designed to be used with a protective foil on the foldable display» Products outside the Regulation: «This Regulation does not apply to the following products: (a) mobile phones and tablets with a flexible main display which the user can unroll and roll up partly or fully; (b) smartphones for high security communication.»

*Analytical inference:* the exemptions narrow the product design duties; they do not change the delivery times for spare parts quoted in section 3.
