   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2023/857 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 19 April 2023 amending Regulation (EU) 2018/842 on binding annual greenhouse gas emission reductions by Member States from 2021 to 2030 contributing to climate action to meet commitments under the Paris Agreement, and Regulation (EU) 2018/1999», an EU regulation published in the «Official Journal of the European Union». Its jurisdiction is the European Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» The Regulation changes two earlier laws, one on national greenhouse gas limits and one on energy and climate governance. Its subject matter, as the amended first article puts it: «This Regulation lays down obligations on Member States with respect to their minimum contributions for the period from 2021 to 2030 to fulfilling the Union’s target of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by 40 % below 2005 levels in 2030 in the sectors covered by Article 2 of this Regulation.» What the Regulation says is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

Each EU country has a national limit on greenhouse gas emissions from sectors outside the EU emissions trading scheme, and this Regulation amends those limits in line with the Union's new 2030 target. The recital explains the pace: «the sectors covered by Regulation (EU) 2018/842 will need to reduce their greenhouse gas emissions progressively until they reach – 40 % in 2030 compared to 2005 levels». It adds a long-term aim: «It contributes to the long-term target of climate neutrality in the Union at the latest by 2050, with the aim of achieving negative emissions thereafter.»

The Regulation enters into force as its text states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union» It was adopted at Strasbourg: «Done at Strasbourg, 19 April 2023.»

*Analytical inference:* the duties are on Member States, which must keep national emissions inside a yearly limit; the text sets no duty, charge or reporting step on a freight business. The recital notes that emissions trading will also apply to maritime transport, buildings and road transport, and keeps the scope of the national limits (section 7).

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The nearest dated step in the text binds Member States: «The Member States listed in Annex II may decide to revise the notified percentage once in 2024 and once in 2027. In such case, the Member State concerned shall notify the Commission thereof by 31 December 2024 or by 31 December 2027, respectively.» The first of those two dates has passed.

- When a Member State where the business runs road haulage or domestic shipping publishes a corrective action plan under Article 8, a regulatory-affairs lead reads whether the plan names transport measures. The trigger is this duty: «If the Commission finds, in its annual assessment under Article 29 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 and taking into account the intended use of the flexibilities referred to in Articles 5, 6 and 7 of this Regulation, that a Member State is not making sufficient progress towards meeting its obligations under Article 4 of this Regulation, that Member State shall, within three months, submit to the Commission a corrective action plan that includes:» The plan is public: «Each Member State shall make its corrective action plan as referred to in paragraph 1 and any justification as referred to in paragraph 3 publicly available.»

*Analytical inference:* the action rests on the Article 8 duty and the publication duty above; a plan would show which national measures a state intends to add. The text states no measure on freight. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any national transport measure that follows from a corrective action plan would apply to the business needs counsel when such a measure is adopted.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The duty holders named are Member States, the Commission and the Central Administrator. Member States: «1. Each Member State shall, in 2030, limit its greenhouse gas emissions at least by the percentage set for that Member State in column 2 of Annex I in relation to its greenhouse gas emissions in 2005» Where a state falls short: «If the Commission finds, in its annual assessment under Article 29 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 and taking into account the intended use of the flexibilities referred to in Articles 5, 6 and 7 of this Regulation, that a Member State is not making sufficient progress towards meeting its obligations under Article 4 of this Regulation, that Member State shall, within three months, submit to the Commission a corrective action plan that includes:» A deduction applies to a state with excess land-use emissions: «2. If the greenhouse gas emissions of a Member State in the period from 2021 to 2025 referred to in Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2018/841 exceeded its removals, as determined in accordance with Article 12 of that Regulation, the Central Administrator shall deduct from that Member State’s annual emission allocations an amount equal to those excess greenhouse gas emissions in tonnes of CO 2 equivalent for the relevant years.» The Regulation is «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight business is not named in the compliance chain; it may meet the Regulation only through national measures a Member State chooses to reach its limit. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business is named as a duty holder in national measures made to meet these limits.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Regulation; the stored text holds the amending Regulation and its Annex only.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Dated steps in the text: the Member States listed in Annex II may revise a notified percentage, and «The Member States listed in Annex II may decide to revise the notified percentage once in 2024 and once in 2027. In such case, the Member State concerned shall notify the Commission thereof by 31 December 2024 or by 31 December 2027, respectively.» The Commission has to report: «2. The Commission shall submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council, within six months of each global stocktake agreed under Article 14 of the Paris Agreement, on the operation of this Regulation» The data reporting step: «3. From 2023, Member States shall determine and report to the Commission final greenhouse gas inventory data by 15 March each year (year X) and preliminary greenhouse gas inventory data by 15 January each year» The Commission sets yearly limits: «The Commission shall adopt implementing acts setting out the annual emission allocations for each Member State for the years from 2021 to 2030 in tonnes of CO 2 equivalent in accordance with the linear trajectories set out in paragraph 2 of this Article.» A recital also records a past plan step: «By 30 June 2023, Member States are to submit a draft update of their integrated national energy and climate plans to the Commission.»

*Analytical inference:* the report within six months of each global stocktake is the point where national targets may be reviewed, and the text states no stocktake date. The 31 December 2027 notification is the next dated step for the listed Member States.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Which emissions count under these national limits turns on the scope article: «1. This Regulation applies to the greenhouse gas emissions from IPCC source categories of energy, industrial processes and product use, agriculture and waste as determined pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 of the European Parliament and the Council ( *2 ) , excluding greenhouse gas emissions from the activities listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC, other than the activity ‘maritime transport’ and activities only listed therein for the purposes of Articles 14 and 15 of that Directive.» The recital adds for shipping: «While emissions trading will also apply to greenhouse gas emissions from maritime transport as well as from buildings, road transport and additional sectors, the scope of Regulation (EU) 2018/842 should be maintained. Regulation (EU) 2018/842 should therefore continue to apply to the greenhouse gas emissions from domestic navigation, but not to those from international navigation.»

*Analytical inference:* the scope article names energy, industrial processes and product use, agriculture and waste, and the recital says domestic navigation stays in the national limits and international navigation does not. This rests on the scope article and the recital quoted; the text does not say which freight activities fall in the covered categories. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular road or inland movement falls within the covered sectors under national inventory rules.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Covered sectors. «1. This Regulation applies to the greenhouse gas emissions from IPCC source categories of energy, industrial processes and product use, agriculture and waste as determined pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 of the European Parliament and the Council ( *2 ) , excluding greenhouse gas emissions from the activities listed in Annex I to Directive 2003/87/EC, other than the activity ‘maritime transport’ and activities only listed therein for the purposes of Articles 14 and 15 of that Directive.»

National limit for 2030. «1. Each Member State shall, in 2030, limit its greenhouse gas emissions at least by the percentage set for that Member State in column 2 of Annex I in relation to its greenhouse gas emissions in 2005» The yearly path: «Subject to the flexibilities provided for in Articles 5, 6 and 7 of this Regulation and to the adjustment pursuant to Article 10(2) of this Regulation, and taking into account any deduction resulting from the application of Article 7 of Decision No 406/2009/EC, each Member State shall ensure that its greenhouse gas emissions: (a) do not exceed, in the years 2021 and 2022, the limit defined by a linear trajectory», with the yearly allocations set by the Commission: «The Commission shall adopt implementing acts setting out the annual emission allocations for each Member State for the years from 2021 to 2030 in tonnes of CO 2 equivalent in accordance with the linear trajectories set out in paragraph 2 of this Article.»

Flexibilities. «1. In respect of the years 2021 to 2025, a Member State may borrow a quantity of up to 7,5 % from its annual emission allocation for the following year.» «4. A Member State may transfer up to 10 % of its annual emission allocation for a given year to other Member States in respect of the years 2021 to 2025, and up to 15 % in respect of the years 2026 to 2030.» Before a transfer: «Before any transfer of annual emission allocations pursuant to paragraphs 4 and 5, a Member State shall inform, in electronic form, the Climate Change Committee established by Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 of its intention to transfer part of its annual emission allocation for any given year.»

Allowance cancellation. «One-tenth of the total quantity of EU ETS allowances determined pursuant to Article 4(4) of this Regulation shall be cancelled pursuant to Article 12(4) of Directive 2003/87/EC for each year from 2021 to 2030 for that Member State. One-sixth of the total quantity of EU ETS allowances determined pursuant to Article 4(4) of this Regulation shall be cancelled pursuant to Article 12(4) of Directive 2003/87/EC for each year from 2025 to 2030 for Member States that have notified the Commission pursuant to paragraphs 3a and 3b of this Article.»

Land use credit. «the cumulative quantity taken into account for that Member State for the years 2021 to 2025 does not exceed half of the maximum amount of total net removals set out in Annex III to this Regulation for that Member State»

Corrective action. «If the Commission finds, in its annual assessment under Article 29 of Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 and taking into account the intended use of the flexibilities referred to in Articles 5, 6 and 7 of this Regulation, that a Member State is not making sufficient progress towards meeting its obligations under Article 4 of this Regulation, that Member State shall, within three months, submit to the Commission a corrective action plan that includes:»

Just transition. «6. When undertaking the actions to limit the greenhouse gas emissions under paragraphs 1 and 2, Member States shall consider the need to ensure a just and socially fair transition for all.»

Excess land-use emissions. «2. If the greenhouse gas emissions of a Member State in the period from 2021 to 2025 referred to in Article 4 of Regulation (EU) 2018/841 exceeded its removals, as determined in accordance with Article 12 of that Regulation, the Central Administrator shall deduct from that Member State’s annual emission allocations an amount equal to those excess greenhouse gas emissions in tonnes of CO 2 equivalent for the relevant years.»

National percentages. The Annex table gives, for each Member State, a reduction from 2005 levels, in two columns: «Column 1 Column 2 Belgium -35 % -47 % Bulgaria -0 % -10 % Czechia -14 % -26 % Denmark -39 % -50 % Germany -38 % -50 % Estonia -13 % -24 % Ireland -30 % -42 % Greece -16 % -22,7 % Spain -26 % -37,7 % France -37 % -47,5 % Croatia -7 % -16,7 % Italy -33 % -43,7 % Cyprus -24 % -32 % Latvia -6 % -17 % Lithuania -9 % -21 % Luxembourg -40 % -50 % Hungary -7 % -18,7 % Malta -19 % -19 % Netherlands -36 % -48 % Austria -36 % -48 % Poland -7 % -17,7 % Portugal -17 % -28,7 % Romania -2 % -12,7 % Slovenia -15 % -27 % Slovakia -12 % -22,7 % Finland -39 % -50 % Sweden -40 % -50 %»

*Analytical inference:* each requirement above falls on a Member State, the Commission or the Central Administrator; the text names no obligation on a business. This rests on the wording of the quoted articles. No cost, price effect or surcharge for freight is stated.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any national measure made to meet these percentages creates a duty or cost for a freight business; the Regulation itself does not.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets national emission limits for Member States, not product rules.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Member States report emissions data: «3. From 2023, Member States shall determine and report to the Commission final greenhouse gas inventory data by 15 March each year (year X) and preliminary greenhouse gas inventory data by 15 January each year» A Member State tells the Climate Change Committee before a transfer: «Before any transfer of annual emission allocations pursuant to paragraphs 4 and 5, a Member State shall inform, in electronic form, the Climate Change Committee established by Regulation (EU) 2018/1999 of its intention to transfer part of its annual emission allocation for any given year.» Public disclosure: «Each Member State shall make its corrective action plan as referred to in paragraph 1 and any justification as referred to in paragraph 3 publicly available.» Revised percentages are notified: «The Member States listed in Annex II may decide to revise the notified percentage once in 2024 and once in 2027. In such case, the Member State concerned shall notify the Commission thereof by 31 December 2024 or by 31 December 2027, respectively.»

*Analytical inference:* these reporting steps fall on Member States; the text states none on a freight business.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation requires no system from a freight business. The reporting systems sit with Member States: «3. From 2023, Member States shall determine and report to the Commission final greenhouse gas inventory data by 15 March each year (year X) and preliminary greenhouse gas inventory data by 15 January each year» An advisory board may also weigh in: «may, on its own initiative, provide scientific advice or issue reports on Union measures, climate targets, annual emission levels and flexibilities under this Regulation»

*Analytical inference:* data a Member State reports on transport emissions comes from national inventories, not from reports a freight business files under this Regulation; the text states no data request to businesses.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Malta has its own notification: «Malta shall notify the Commission by 31 December 2023 if it intends to make use of the limited cancellation of EU ETS allowances referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, up to the percentage listed in Annex II for each of the years 2025 to 2030, for its compliance under Article 9.» Its entry in the Annex reads: «Malta 7 %» Other listed Member States: «the Member States listed in Annex II which have not notified the Commission by 31 December 2019 of an intention to make use or full use of the limited cancellation of EU ETS allowances referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall notify the Commission by 31 December 2023» When a state revises its percentage the cancellation changes: «a correspondingly lower or higher quantity of EU ETS allowances shall be cancelled for that Member State in respect of each year from 2026 to 2030 or from 2028 to 2030, respectively» For shipping, the recital limits the scope: «While emissions trading will also apply to greenhouse gas emissions from maritime transport as well as from buildings, road transport and additional sectors, the scope of Regulation (EU) 2018/842 should be maintained. Regulation (EU) 2018/842 should therefore continue to apply to the greenhouse gas emissions from domestic navigation, but not to those from international navigation.»

*Analytical inference:* the Annex II states carry a limited route to cancel emission trading allowances toward their limit; the text does not say that route changes any charge to a freight business.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2024/3099 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 27 November 2024 amending Directive 2009/16/EC on port State control», the Union directive that rewrites the rules for port State control, the inspection of foreign ships that call at Union ports. Its reach is set by its last article: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» Anything it says about ships and their owners or operators therefore reaches them through the national laws the Member States adopt. What the Directive states is quoted from its text; what it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive amends an earlier directive, Directive 2009/16/EC, which «sets out rules on the system for port State control inspections, whereby eligible ships calling at Union ports are inspected to check whether the competence of the crew on board and the condition of the ship and its equipment comply with the requirements of international conventions on the safety of life at sea, on the protection of the marine environment and on living and working conditions on ships of all flags.» The amending text adds three international conventions to the list that inspectors check ships against: «(l) the International Convention for the Control and Management of Ships’ Ballast Water and Sediments, 2004 (the “BWM Convention”); (m) the Nairobi International Convention on the Removal of Wrecks, 2007 (the “Nairobi Convention”); (n) the Hong Kong International Convention for the Safe and Environmentally Sound Recycling of Ships, 2009 (the “Hong Kong Convention”).» Its recitals give the aim of the new ship risk profile: «the ship risk profile should be updated to reflect environmental issues by attaching more importance to the environmental performance of ships.»

The Directive enters into force as its Article 3 states: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* the Directive works on ships and on the authorities that inspect them. A forwarder or shipper is not named in it. A freight business meets it through the ship owners and operators that carry its cargo, and through the Member State ports those ships call at.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Directive sets no step on a freight operator within the next 30 days. Its dated duty sits on the Member States: «Member States shall adopt and publish by 6 July 2027 the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.» That date is ahead, so the refusal of access rules below reach ships through national text that is not yet due.

- A carrier-relations lead, at the next review of an ocean contract, asks the ship owner or operator for the flag State of each ship on the business's services and for any detention of those ships, because a ship that «has been detained more than twice in the course of the preceding 36 months in a port or anchorage of a Member State or of a State signatory to the Paris MoU» can be refused access under Article 16 as replaced.

- A compliance lead lists the Member States whose ports the business's ocean services call at and, on 6 July 2027, checks which of them have published the laws the Directive requires, so the refusal of access rules are read in the national text that applies.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the refusal of access rule and the transposition duty quoted above; the Directive requires neither step of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client or carrier contract gives the business a right to the detention history of a ship.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive names the Member States, their competent authorities, the owner or operator of a ship, the master, the flag State administration, the recognised organisation and the Commission. The owner or operator holds the right to challenge a measure: «The owner or operator of a ship or the owner or operator’s representative in the Member State shall have a right of appeal against any detention or refusal of access by the competent authority. An appeal shall not cause the detention or refusal of access to be suspended.» A refusal of access order is passed on to several parties: «The competent authority shall send a copy of the refusal of access order to the flag State administration, the recognised organisation concerned, the other Member States, and the other signatories to the Paris MoU, the Commission and the Paris MoU Secretariat.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder or shipper is not named. The party the Directive addresses for a refusal of access is the owner or operator of the ship, and the order is issued by a Member State's competent authority. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a business that books cargo on a ship under a refusal of access order has any duty or liability under national law.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Several later steps are set by the text. The Commission reports on the Directive: «The Commission shall, by 6 July 2032 and every 5 years thereafter, submit a report to the European Parliament and the Council on the implementation of, and compliance with, this Directive.» It also assesses a ship carbon rating as an input to the risk profile: «After the IMO has concluded the revision of its carbon intensity indicator (CII), the Commission shall assess the suitability of that CII as an environmental parameter used for the determination of a risk profile of a ship under this Directive.» The list of conventions can be changed by the Commission: «The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 30b, to amend Article 2, point (1), with regard to the list of Conventions set out therein, once such Conventions have been adopted as a relevant instrument under the Paris MoU». One convention added by the Directive had its own start date, which has passed: «will enter into force on 26 June 2025.»

*Analytical inference:* the report at the 2032 date is where the Commission decides whether to propose changes to the Directive. The text does not say what the carbon rating assessment will conclude, and it sets no date for it, so a forwarder cannot yet read a cost effect from it.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether a ship is refused access is how often it has been detained and under which flag. The text sets it: «A Member State shall refuse access to its ports and anchorages to any ship which: (a) flies the flag of a State that appears on the low performance list, adopted in accordance with the Paris MoU on the basis of information recorded in the inspection database and published annually by the Commission, and which has been detained more than twice in the course of the preceding 36 months in a port or anchorage of a Member State or of a State signatory to the Paris MoU; or (b) flies the flag of a State that appears on the high or medium performance list, adopted in accordance with the Paris MoU on the basis of information recorded in the inspection database and published annually by the Commission, and which has been detained more than twice in the course of the preceding 24 months in a port or anchorage of a Member State or of a State signatory to the Paris MoU.» The rule has one carve-out: «The first subparagraph of this paragraph shall not apply in the situations referred to in Article 21(6).» When the refusal starts: «The refusal of access shall be applicable as soon as the ship leaves the port or anchorage where it has been the subject of a third detention and where a refusal of access order has been issued.»

*Analytical inference:* the same count of detentions leads to a refusal sooner for a ship under a low performance flag (36 months window) than under a high or medium one (24 months window). *Legal Confirmation Required:* which performance list a given flag State is on at the time of a detention, which the Commission publishes each year.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Refusal of access. The first refusal order is lifted late: «The refusal of access order shall be lifted only after a period of three months has passed from the date of issue of that order and when the conditions listed in points 3 to 6 of Annex VIII are met. If the ship is subject to a second refusal of access order, that refusal of access order shall be lifted only after a period of 12 months.» A further detention leads to a wider refusal: «Any subsequent detention in a port or anchorage of a Member State or of a State signatory to the Paris MoU shall result in the ship being refused access to any port or anchorage within the Union. Such a third refusal of access order may be lifted after a period of 24 months has passed from the date of issue of that order and only if:» The last step is permanent: «Any subsequent detention after a third refusal of access order, in a port or anchorage within the Union, of a ship flying the flag of a State that appears on the medium or low performance list shall result in the ship being permanently refused access to any port or anchorage within the Union.» A second route to refusal exists for ships that avoid a detention order: «Member States shall take measures to ensure that access to any port or anchorage within the Union is refused to ships referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article and to detained ships as referred to in Article 19(2), which: (a) proceed to sea without complying with the conditions determined by the competent authority of any Member State in the port of inspection;» «The refusal of access order shall become applicable from the date of its issuing. The refusal of access order shall be lifted only after a period of 12 months has passed from the date of issue of that order and when the conditions listed in points 3 to 6 of Annex VIII are met.»

Member State quality system. «Each Member State shall develop, implement and maintain a quality management system covering the operational parts of the port State-related activities of its administration directly involved in inspections. That quality management system shall be certified in accordance with applicable international quality standards by 6 July 2032.»

*Analytical inference:* each duty above falls on a Member State's competent authority, which issues and lifts the orders, or on the Member State itself; the consequence for a ship is a refusal of access to ports. The Directive states no fine, charge or freight rate effect, so the cost to cargo of a refused ship is a gap. No phase-in is stated in Articles 16, 21 and 30 as replaced. No scope limits are stated in Articles 16, 21 and 30 as replaced.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a refusal of access order against a ship used by the business gives a client or the business any right or duty beyond the order itself.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reporting duties fall on Member States and their authorities. On the national laws: «They shall immediately inform the Commission thereof. When Member States adopt those measures, they shall contain a reference to this Directive or shall be accompanied by such reference on the occasion of their official publication.» «Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.» On orders: «The competent authority shall also update the inspection database with information on the refusal of access without delay.» On information from port bodies: «Each Member State shall ensure that its port authorities or bodies and other relevant authorities or bodies provide the competent authority with the following types of information in their possession:» information about ships that did not notify, ships that left without complying with the waste reception rules, ships denied entry on security grounds and reported anomalies.

*Analytical inference:* these are duties of Member State authorities; the text states no registration or report by a forwarder.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the owner or operator of a ship, not a forwarder, has the work of lifting a refusal order. «In order to have the refusal of access order lifted, the owner or the operator of the ship must address a formal request to the competent authority of the Member State that imposed the refusal of access order.» The timing: «Such a request including the required documents must be submitted to the banning State at least one month before the end of the ban period. If this deadline is not met, then a delay may occur of up to one month after the banning State received the request.» After a lifting: «The information system will add an overriding factor to the ship and the ship will be indicated as eligible for an expanded inspection at its next call at port/anchorage in the Paris MoU region.»

- A carrier-relations lead, when a ship on the business's services is placed under a refusal of access order, asks the ship owner or operator for the date the request to lift it is due, one month before the end of the ban period, and for the date it was sent.

- A booking desk, when a ship returns after a lifting, notes that it is indicated as eligible for an expanded inspection at its next call and asks the owner or operator whether a port call has been affected.

*Analytical inference:* the owner or operator carries the request and the documents; the Directive states no data a forwarder must keep, so both steps are questions to the ship owner or operator, not systems the Directive requires of the business.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Two carve-outs are stated. A Member State without seaports may be excused from the Directive: «By way of derogation from paragraph 1, Member States which do not have seaports and which can demonstrate that, of the total number of individual vessels calling annually over the three previous years at their river ports, less than 5 % are ships covered by this Directive, may derogate from the obligation to transpose and implement this Directive.» An inspection missed for a stated reason is not counted against a Member State: «If an inspection is not carried out due to extraordinary and unforeseen circumstances it shall not be counted as a missed inspection and the reason for not carrying out the inspection shall be recorded in the inspection database.»

*Analytical inference:* the first exemption applies to Member States with river ports only, not to ships or cargo, and the second concerns how a Member State's inspection record is counted.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2026/706 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 11 March 2026 amending Directive 2014/32/EU as regards measuring systems for electric vehicle supply equipment and compressed gas dispensers, and electricity, gas and thermal energy meters», an EU directive published in the «Official Journal of the European Union». Its jurisdiction is the Member States of the European Union: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» What the Directive says is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*. The Directive was adopted on «Done at Strasbourg, 11 March 2026.»

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive changes an existing EU law on measuring instruments. The original law's aim: «One of the objectives of Directive 2014/32/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ( 3 ) is to guarantee the functioning of the internal market with regard to measuring instruments.» The reason for the change: «new measuring instruments that do not fall within the scope of Directive 2014/32/EU have appeared on the market. That is the case, in particular, for measuring systems for electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) and measuring systems for compressed gas dispensers, which are important for the successful development of clean mobility.» It adds two new instrument rules: «(5) the text set out in Annex IV to this Directive is inserted as Annex Va;» and «(7) the text set out in Annex VI to this Directive is inserted as Annex VIIa.» The first covers meters in electric vehicle charging, the second compressed gas dispensers for vehicle fuelling.

The Directive enters into force as its text states: «Article 5 This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .» The text itself refers to the amended law from a date: «By way of derogation from Directive 2014/32/EU, conformity assessment bodies which comply with that Directive, as amended on 9 April 2026, may be notified in accordance with that Directive, as amended on 9 April 2026, before 10 October 2028.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight operator is a user, not a duty holder, of these rules. It pays for electricity or gas that a charger or dispenser measures, and the rules govern how accurate and how clearly displayed that measurement must be. The Directive is addressed to Member States and names no freight role (section 4).

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The nearest dated step binds Member States: «By 10 April 2028, Member States shall adopt and publish the measures necessary to comply with this Directive. They shall immediately inform the Commission thereof. They shall apply those measures from 10 October 2028.». That is more than a year away.

- When a depot charging site is commissioned or a charging or fuelling supply contract is renewed after 10 October 2028, a procurement lead asks the supplier which accuracy class, A, B or C, the measuring system for EVSE declares and which procedure certified it, because the manufacturer must specify a class: «The manufacturer shall specify the class index of the measuring system for EVSE. The class indices are defined as: Class A, B and C.»

*Analytical inference:* the question rests on the class rule above and on the text on pricing for these systems: «That measurement result shall serve as the basis for the price to pay, if applicable.» The Directive requires no such question of the buyer. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a buyer may rely on the declared class in a charging contract is not stated and needs counsel.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive names Member States, manufacturers and notified conformity assessment bodies. Member States: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» The putting into use rule: «Member States shall ensure that the intended use determines the foreseen and foreseeable practical working conditions, namely the rated operating conditions, so that the measuring system for EVSE is suitable for its use.» Manufacturers: «The manufacturer shall specify the class index of the measuring system for EVSE. The class indices are defined as: Class A, B and C.» Conformity assessment bodies: «By way of derogation from Directive 2014/32/EU, conformity assessment bodies which comply with that Directive, as amended on 9 April 2026, may be notified in accordance with that Directive, as amended on 9 April 2026, before 10 October 2028.»

*Analytical inference:* the source names no forwarder, carrier, shipper or fleet operator; a freight business meets these rules as a buyer of charging or compressed gas. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a fleet operator that runs its own charging or fuelling point is a manufacturer, a user or neither under national measures.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text sets dates, most still ahead. National measures: «By 10 April 2028, Member States shall adopt and publish the measures necessary to comply with this Directive. They shall immediately inform the Commission thereof. They shall apply those measures from 10 October 2028.» Existing instruments: «1. By way of derogation from Article 7(2) of Directive 2014/32/EU, Member States shall not impede the making available on the market and putting into use of measuring instruments that are in conformity with that Directive on 8 April 2026, and that have been placed on the market before 10 October 2028.» New-type instruments: «that have been placed on the market before 10 April 2030», and certificates: «shall remain valid until the expiry of their validity, and in any case no longer than 10 April 2038».

*Analytical inference:* the dates mean national rules apply from 10 October 2028 and the older stock of instruments is tolerated in stages up to 10 April 2030 for the new instrument types; the text states no later guidance date.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Whether a charger meter or a gas dispenser meter falls under the new rules turns on the definitions. For charging: «A measuring system for EVSE is a system that includes all relevant metrological functions related to the conductive transfer (either direction), at a specified transfer point, of active electrical energy between EVSE (such as charging stations for electric vehicles) and electric vehicles (such as motor vehicles, rail engines, boats, vessels and aircraft).» The same text excludes a class of meter: «Such measuring systems shall not be considered as utility measuring instruments as referred to in Annex I.» For gas: «Compressed gas dispenser A system intended for the fuelling of vehicles (such as motor vehicles, rail engines, boats, vessels and aircraft) with compressed gaseous fuel.»

*Analytical inference:* the definitions cover vehicles of several transport kinds, so a depot charger for road vehicles and a charger serving rail engines, boats, vessels or aircraft fall in the same definition. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular depot charger or dispenser is a measuring system for EVSE or a compressed gas dispenser.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

National measures. «By 10 April 2028, Member States shall adopt and publish the measures necessary to comply with this Directive. They shall immediately inform the Commission thereof. They shall apply those measures from 10 October 2028.» The measures go to the Commission, and the text also says: «Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.»

Accuracy class for charging meters. «The manufacturer shall specify the class index of the measuring system for EVSE. The class indices are defined as: Class A, B and C.»

Display of charging energy. «The electrical energy measured shall be displayed in kilowatt-hours or their decimal multiples.»

Conformity assessment for charging meters. «The conformity assessment procedures referred to in Article 17 that the manufacturer can choose between are: B + F or B + D or G or H1.»

Accuracy for gas dispensers. «Type of compressed gas measuring systems Accuracy Class (MPE [% of measured value]) Compressed hydrogen measuring systems 2,0 Other compressed gas measuring systems 1,5»

Price display on gas dispensers. «Where a measuring system is fitted with a price display, the difference between the indicated price and the price calculated from the unit price and the indicated quantity shall not exceed the smallest currency unit.»

Units on gas dispensers. «The metered quantity shall be displayed in kilograms, or their decimal multiples or submultiples, and, if applicable, in joules or watt-hours, or their decimal multiples.»

Existing instruments. «1. By way of derogation from Article 7(2) of Directive 2014/32/EU, Member States shall not impede the making available on the market and putting into use of measuring instruments that are in conformity with that Directive on 8 April 2026, and that have been placed on the market before 10 October 2028.»

*Analytical inference:* these requirements fall on Member States and manufacturers; the text names no obligation on a freight buyer. This rests on the Directive being addressed to Member States and on the manufacturer wording above. No price pass-through of testing or certification cost is stated.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a charging or fuelling supplier may pass certification cost to a customer; the text is silent on it.

No exceptions are stated in Articles 3, 5 and 6. No scope limits are stated in Articles 3, 5 and 6. No phase-in is stated in Articles 3, 5 and 6.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Member States inform and report to the Commission: «By 10 April 2028, Member States shall adopt and publish the measures necessary to comply with this Directive. They shall immediately inform the Commission thereof. They shall apply those measures from 10 October 2028.» «Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.» Notification of bodies: «By way of derogation from Directive 2014/32/EU, conformity assessment bodies which comply with that Directive, as amended on 9 April 2026, may be notified in accordance with that Directive, as amended on 9 April 2026, before 10 October 2028.» The text sets no registration or reporting duty on a business.

*Analytical inference:* the information duties fall on Member States; the source states none on a freight business.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Directive requires no system from a freight business. System design duties sit with manufacturers, for example the rule on how a charging result is used: «That measurement result shall serve as the basis for the price to pay, if applicable.» and, for charging meters, the choice of procedure: «The conformity assessment procedures referred to in Article 17 that the manufacturer can choose between are: B + F or B + D or G or H1.» The putting into use rule for charging systems is: «Member States shall ensure that the intended use determines the foreseen and foreseeable practical working conditions, namely the rated operating conditions, so that the measuring system for EVSE is suitable for its use.»

*Analytical inference:* a freight operator that owns charging points and puts them into use could meet the putting-into-use rule through its national measures; the Directive text assigns that duty to Member States. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether an owner of a charging point is subject to national measures that apply the rule.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Stock already on the market is protected for a time. «1. By way of derogation from Article 7(2) of Directive 2014/32/EU, Member States shall not impede the making available on the market and putting into use of measuring instruments that are in conformity with that Directive on 8 April 2026, and that have been placed on the market before 10 October 2028.» For the new instrument types: «2. By way of derogation from Article 7(2) of Directive 2014/32/EU, Member States shall not impede the making available on the market and putting into use of measuring instruments defined in Annexes Va and VIIa of that Directive, as amended on 9 April 2026, that are in conformity with the national law of a Member State and that have been placed on the market before 10 April 2030.» For certificates: «shall remain valid until the expiry of their validity, and in any case no longer than 10 April 2038» The recitals add that existing equipment is not to be retrofitted: «while ensuring that no retrofitting obligations are imposed as regards existing charging stations» and «while ensuring that no retrofitting obligations are imposed as regards existing compressed gas dispensers».

*Analytical inference:* an existing depot charger or dispenser is not required to be retrofitted under the recitals quoted, because they state the aim of imposing no retrofitting obligation; the operative articles are those above.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DECISION (EU) 2022/591 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 6 April 2022 on a General Union Environment Action Programme to 2030», the European Union's overall environment programme. Its subject: «This Decision sets out a general action programme in the field of the environment for the period up to 31 December 2030 (the ‘8th Environment Action programme’ or ‘8th EAP’).» Its reach: «It establishes a monitoring framework to measure the progress of the Union and its Member States towards the attainment of the priority objectives of the 8th EAP». What the Decision states comes from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Decision is a programme of aims, not a rulebook for companies. It states the long-term aim: «the long-term priority objective that by 2050 at the latest, people live well, within the planetary boundaries in a well-being economy where nothing is wasted, growth is regenerative, climate neutrality in the Union has been achieved and inequalities have been significantly reduced.» One of six priority objectives is «promoting environmental aspects of sustainability and significantly reducing key environmental and climate pressures related to the Union’s production and consumption, in particular in the areas of energy, industry, buildings and infrastructure, mobility, tourism, international trade and the food system». The Decision enters into force as its last article states: «This Decision shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .»

*Analytical inference:* mobility and international trade are named among the areas where pressure is to fall, so the programme points in the same direction as the transport and trade rules a freight business meets, but the Decision itself sets no duty, rate or deadline on a forwarder, a carrier or a shipper. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any later Union act adopted under the programme reaches the business; this Decision does not.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight business within the next 30 days, and the Decision names no duty on one. The dated steps are the Commission's: «By 31 March 2029, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of the 8th EAP.» That date is ahead, and the evaluation can lead to a proposal for the next programme.

- A regulatory-affairs lead adds the Commission evaluation due by 31 March 2029 to the business's policy calendar, and checks at that date whether a proposal for the next programme names mobility or international trade.
- A strategy lead asks, in the next annual planning round, which of the six priority objectives in Article 2(2) the business's own sustainability claims to clients refer to, so the claims use the same words as the programme.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the Commission evaluation in Article 6 and on the six objectives in Article 2(2); the Decision sets no cost, fee or rate on freight. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether client-facing sustainability claims that quote the programme are accurate, since the Decision states aims and not company duties.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Decision names the Commission, the European Environment Agency, the European Chemicals Agency, Member States, regional and local authorities and stakeholders. It assigns monitoring to the Commission: «The Commission, supported by the European Environment Agency (EEA) and the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA), without prejudice to their independence, shall monitor, assess and report on the progress of the Union and the Member States with regard to attaining the priority objectives set out in Article 2, on an annual basis». It assigns the enabling conditions broadly: «The attainment of the priority objectives set out in Article 2 shall require the following from the Commission, Member States, regional and local authorities and stakeholders, as appropriate».

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder, a carrier and a shipper are not named; the word stakeholders is the nearest the text comes, and it assigns them no specific duty. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business counts as a stakeholder under Article 3 for any purpose beyond the general wording.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Decision. Section 6 notes the Commission steps the text sets.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Commission was to present headline indicators: «the Commission shall, by 2 May 2022, present a monitoring framework, based on a limited number of headline indicators». That date has passed. A review was due: «By 31 March 2024, the Commission shall carry out a mid-term review of the progress achieved in attaining the thematic priority objectives set out in Article 2(2)». That date has passed too, and the captured text does not say what the review found. The Commission was also to set a method for other harmful subsidies: «a methodology that is set out by the Commission, in consultation with Member States, by 2023, to identify other environmentally harmful subsidies». The next step ahead is the evaluation: «By 31 March 2029, the Commission shall carry out an evaluation of the 8th EAP.» followed, «if appropriate, by a legislative proposal for the next environmental action programme by 31 December 2029».

*Analytical inference:* the evaluation due by 31 March 2029 and the proposal due by 31 December 2029 are the points where the programme's direction on mobility and international trade can change; the text states no outcome for either. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the mid-term review and the methodology on subsidies have been completed, which the captured text cannot show.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question is what the programme binds. The Decision speaks of aims and of a governance mechanism: «It lays down the priority objectives of the 8th EAP and identifies the enabling conditions necessary to attain those priority objectives.» The six objectives are stated for a period: «The 8th EAP shall have the following six interlinked thematic priority objectives for the period up to 31 December 2030».

*Analytical inference:* the text states objectives and conditions, not thresholds, quotas or limits for a company. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any objective in Article 2(2) is carried into a binding duty by another Union act that a client's cargo meets.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Objectives (Article 2). «The 8th EAP shall have the following six interlinked thematic priority objectives for the period up to 31 December 2030». The first: «swift and predictable reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and, at the same time, enhancement of removals by natural sinks in the Union to attain the 2030 greenhouse gas emission reduction target as laid down in Regulation (EU) 2021/1119».

Enabling conditions (Article 3). «ensuring effective, swift and full implementation of Union legislation and strategies on the environment and the climate». «improving guidance and recommendations, including on effective, dissuasive and proportionate penalties to reduce risks of non-compliance with Union environmental law». On subsidies: «strengthening environmentally positive incentives as well as phasing out environmentally harmful subsidies, in particular fossil fuel subsidies, at Union, national, regional and local level, without delay».

Monitoring (Article 4). «shall monitor, assess and report on the progress of the Union and the Member States with regard to attaining the priority objectives set out in Article 2, on an annual basis».

The captured text sets no penalty, fine or sanction in this Decision; Article 3 speaks of enforcing Union environmental law elsewhere.

*Analytical inference:* each item above is an aim or a Commission task; the text states no amount, no fee and no pass-through to freight customers. No phase-in is stated in Articles 2 to 4. No exceptions are stated in Articles 2 to 4. No scope limits are stated in Articles 2 to 4.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which later Union acts carry out these aims and whether any binds a freight business.

Obligations surveyed: 0; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 6.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Decision sets a programme of aims, not rules for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Reporting runs in two directions. Member States report to the Commission on subsidies, as the text states below, and the Commission reports to the Union institutions. The Commission's mid-term report goes upward: «The Commission shall submit a report on the mid-term review to the European Parliament and to the Council.» The monitoring results are public: «The information that results from that monitoring, assessment and reporting shall be made publicly available and easily accessible.» On subsidies, the text asks Member States to report: «on the basis of that methodology Member States shall identify other environmentally harmful subsidies and report them regularly to the Commission».

*Analytical inference:* the reporting duties fall on the Commission and Member States, and none on a forwarder is stated.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Decision builds a monitoring framework for the Union and states no system for a freight business to build.

- A sustainability data lead checks the Commission's public monitoring information each time it is updated, once a year, for movement on the priority objective that names mobility and international trade.
- A sales lead keeps one reference sentence for client talks that says the programme states aims to 2030 and sets no duty on a freight business, until a later act changes that.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the public monitoring in Article 4 and on the absence of a company duty in the text. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client contract allows the programme to be cited as support for a sustainability claim.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Decision names no exemption, transition period or edge case for a company. Its principles frame how it is to be read: «The 8th EAP shall be based on the precautionary principle, the principles of preventive action and of rectification of pollution at source and the polluter pays principle.» Its fairness aim reads: «whilst ensuring a just transition that leaves no one behind».

*Analytical inference:* the principles and the just transition aim guide the Union's later acts and do not exempt or burden a freight business directly. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a later act cites these principles to set a duty that reaches the business.

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 6 April 2022: Decision adopted at Strasbourg
- 2 May 2022: date by which the Commission presents the monitoring framework (passed)
- 2023: year by which the Commission sets a method to identify other environmentally harmful subsidies (passed)
- 31 March 2024: date by which the Commission carries out the mid-term review (passed)
- 31 March 2029: date by which the Commission carries out the evaluation of the programme
- 31 December 2029: date by which a proposal for the next programme follows, if appropriate
- 31 December 2030: end of the period of the programme
- 2050: long-term aim date for the programme's objective

The Decision enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal; the text states no calendar date for that day.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2024/1799 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 June 2024 on common rules promoting the repair of goods and amending Regulation (EU) 2017/2394 and Directives (EU) 2019/771 and (EU) 2020/1828», the Union directive that sets common rules for the repair of consumer goods. Its scope: «This Directive shall apply to the repair of goods purchased by consumers in the event of a defect of the goods that occurs or becomes apparent outside the liability of the seller pursuant to Article 10 of Directive (EU) 2019/771.» It is addressed to the Member States: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» Anything it says about manufacturers, repairers and sellers therefore reaches them through national law. What the Directive states is quoted from its text; what it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive states its purpose: «This Directive lays down common rules strengthening the provisions related to the repair of goods, with a view to contributing to the proper functioning of the internal market, while providing for a high level of consumer and environmental protection.» Its core duty: «Member States shall ensure that upon the consumer’s request, the manufacturer shall repair goods for which, and to the extent that, repairability requirements are provided for by Union legal acts listed in Annex II.»

The Directive enters into force as its Article 23 states: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* the Directive concerns goods bought by consumers and the manufacturers and repairers who fix them. A forwarder or shipper is not named. A freight business meets it as a carrier of goods to or from repair, as an importer or distributor if it holds that role for goods it brings into the Union, or when it supplies a repairer or manufacturer.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Directive sets no step on a freight operator within the next 30 days. The transposition date has passed: «Member States shall bring into force the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive by 31 July 2026 at the latest.» «Member States shall apply those measures from 31 July 2026.» The next live date is 31 July 2027: «Member States shall ensure that their national online platforms are operational by 31 July 2027.» The platform lists transport among the services a repairer may offer: «availability and conditions of ancillary services, including removal, installation and transportation, offered by repairers»

- A contracts lead at a business that brings consumer goods into the Union checks, at the next review of a supplier contract, whether the manufacturer is outside the Union and has an authorised representative in the Union, because the repair duty then moves as follows: «Where the manufacturer obliged to repair pursuant to paragraph 1 is established outside the Union, its authorised representative in the Union shall perform the obligation of the manufacturer. Where the manufacturer has no authorised representative in the Union, the importer of the good concerned shall perform the obligation of the manufacturer. Where there is no importer, the distributor of the good concerned shall perform the obligation of the manufacturer.»

- A product lead at a business that carries goods to or from repairers decides, before 31 July 2027, whether to ask its repairer customers to list transportation as an ancillary service on their national platform entry, because the platform search covers that service.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the repair duty chain and the platform search quoted above; the Directive requires neither step of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an importer or distributor within the Directive's meaning, which Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 defines and is not held here.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive names the consumer, the repairer, the seller, the manufacturer, the authorised representative, the importer, the distributor and Member States. A repairer is defined: «‘repairer’ means any natural or legal person who, related to that person’s trade, business, craft or profession, provides a repair service, including manufacturers and sellers that provide repair services and repair service providers whether independent or affiliated with such manufacturers or sellers;» Importer and distributor are defined by reference: «‘importer’ means ‘importer’ as defined in Article 2, point (44), of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781; (8) ‘distributor’ means ‘distributor’ as defined in Article 2, point (45), of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781;» The substitute roles may sub-contract: «The authorised representative, importer and distributor may sub-contract repair in order to fulfil their obligation to repair.» The repair form lists transport among the services: «(i) where applicable, the availability of ancillary services, such as removal, installation and transportation, offered by the repairer, and the detailed costs of those services, if any, for the consumer;»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder or shipper is not named. A carrier that moves goods to a repairer is not a repairer unless it also provides a repair service; a business is an importer or distributor only as that Regulation defines them. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business holds the importer or distributor role for any goods it brings into the Union.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance on this Directive is held.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Later steps are set by the text. Platform: «By 31 July 2027, the Commission shall develop the common online interface for the European online platform.» Measures: «By 31 July 2029, Member States shall notify to the Commission one or more measures taken under paragraph 1.» Review: «By 31 July 2031, the Commission shall submit a report on the application of this Directive.» The list of goods can change: «The Commission shall adopt such delegated acts without undue delay after publication of the respective Union legal act, and at the latest 12 months after such publication.» Power to do so runs for a set period: «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 5(9) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of six years from 31 August 2024.»

*Analytical inference:* the 2027 date is the one that opens the national repair platforms; the 2031 report is where the Commission assesses the contribution of the Directive, and the list of goods covered can grow by delegated act in between. The text does not say which goods will be added.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question that decides whether the repair duty bites is which goods are covered. The text sets it: «Articles 5 and 6 shall only apply to goods for which and to the extent that repairability requirements are provided for by Union legal acts listed in Annex II.» Annex II lists the acts by good, for example «For household washing machines and household washer-dryers, Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2023» and also «For goods incorporating light means of transport batteries, Regulation (EU) 2023/1542» The duty has an end point: «The manufacturer shall not be obliged to repair such goods where repair is impossible.»

*Analytical inference:* the repair duty applies only to goods whose own Union act sets repairability requirements; goods not listed in Annex II are outside Articles 5 and 6. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a good the business handles is within an Annex II act.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Repair information form. «Repairers may provide the consumer with the European Repair Information Form set out in Annex I.» «The repairer shall not alter the conditions of repair specified in the European Repair Information Form for a period of 30 calendar days from the date on which that form was provided to the consumer.»

Obligation to repair. «The repair pursuant to paragraph 1 shall be carried out subject to the following conditions: (a) it shall be carried out either free of charge or for a reasonable price; (b) it shall be carried out within a reasonable period of time from the moment the manufacturer has physical possession of the good, has received the good or has been given access to the good by the consumer;» «Manufacturers that make spare parts and tools available for goods covered by Union legal acts listed in Annex II shall offer these spare parts and tools at a reasonable price that does not deter repair.» «Manufacturers shall not refuse to repair goods covered by Union legal acts listed in Annex II for the sole reason that a previous repair has been performed by other repairers or by other persons.»

Information and platform. «Member States shall ensure that the manufacturer or, where applicable, the authorised representative, importer or distributor make available free of charge, at least for the entire duration of their obligation to repair pursuant to Article 5, information on their repair services in an easily accessible, clear and comprehensible manner.» «Member States may extend the scope of their national section on the European online platform or, where applicable, their national online platform to cover, not only repairers, but also sellers of goods that have been subject to refurbishment, purchasers of defective goods for refurbishment or community-led repair initiatives.»

Seller liability. «Where, in accordance with Article 13(2), repair takes place as the remedy to bring the goods into conformity, the liability period shall be extended once by 12 months.»

Penalties. «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of national provisions adopted pursuant to Articles 4, 5 and 6 and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.»

*Analytical inference:* each duty above falls on the manufacturer, or the authorised representative, importer or distributor in its place, or on the repairer for the form; the penalties are for Member States to set, and the Directive states no amount, so the cost of an infringement is a gap. The Directive states no freight rate or surcharge effect. No phase-in is stated in Articles 4, 5 and 6.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which party carries the repair duty for a good the business brings into the Union, and whether a carrier of repaired goods has any duty under national law.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reporting duties are on Member States; registration is voluntary for repairers. Contact points: «By 31 July 2026, Member States shall inform the Commission about: (a) the national contact point that they have designated for the European online platform; or (b) the national online platforms that they have established or will establish in accordance with Article 7(3).» Penalty rules: «Member States shall, by 31 July 2026 notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures and shall notify it, without delay, of any subsequent amendment affecting them.» Text of measures: «Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.» Registration: «The registration shall be voluntary for repairers and, where applicable, sellers of goods that have been subject to refurbishment and purchasers of defective goods for refurbishment or community-led repair initiatives.»

*Analytical inference:* these are duties of Member State authorities; the text states no registration or report by a forwarder, and a repairer's registration on the platform is a choice.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: manufacturers and the parties that stand in for them must publish repair prices and avoid blocking repair, which is work for those parties, not a forwarder. Prices: «Manufacturers, or, where applicable, authorised representatives, importers or distributors who have an obligation to repair pursuant to this Article shall ensure that consumers can access, via a free access website, information on the indicative prices that are charged for the typical repair of goods covered by Union legal acts listed in Annex II.» Contract terms: «Manufacturers shall not use any contractual clauses, hardware or software techniques that impede the repair of goods covered by Union legal acts listed in Annex II unless justified by legitimate and objective factors including the protection of intellectual property rights under Union and national law.»

- A contracts lead, at the next review of a supply contract with a manufacturer of Annex II goods, checks that the contract does not require the business to use terms that impede repair, because the Directive bars manufacturers from using such clauses unless a stated factor justifies them.

- A service lead at a business that carries goods for a manufacturer's repair service asks, at the next service-level review, whether the manufacturer's published repair prices and repair information include the transport cost, because the form lists the cost of transportation where the repairer offers it.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the contract-term and price-information rules above; the Directive states no data a forwarder must keep as a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is a manufacturer's authorised representative, importer or distributor.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Some limits are stated. Sales before the start date: «Article 16 of this Directive shall not apply to sales contracts concluded before 31 July 2026.» Costs of diagnosis: «By way of derogation from paragraph 2, where a diagnostic service, including a physical or remote examination, is needed to identify the nature of the defect, the type of repair and to estimate the price of repair, the repairer may request the consumer to pay the necessary costs of this service.» Help for small firms: «Where appropriate, the Commission shall adopt guidelines to support in particular micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in complying with the requirements and obligations set out in this Directive.»

*Analytical inference:* the 31 July 2026 start for seller-liability changes means contracts concluded before it keep the old rules; the diagnostic charge is stated in the Article on the repair information form.
