   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «(EU) 2024/3170 of 18 December 2024 laying down detailed provisions concerning the voluntary environmental labelling scheme for the estimation of the environmental performance of flights, established pursuant to Article 14 of Regulation (EU) 2023/2405 of the European Parliament and of the Council (Flight Emissions Label)», the European Union rule that sets how a flight's emissions are estimated and shown to buyers. Its subject: «This Regulation lays down detailed provisions to ensure the uniform implementation of and compliance with the rules on the environmental labelling scheme set out in Article 14 of Regulation (EU) 2023/2405». Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The scheme is voluntary for airlines, and detailed once an airline joins. The Regulation states that the Union's aviation safety agency issues the labels: «the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (the ‘Agency’)». It defines the figure that matters for cargo: «‘freight emissions’ means the proportion of flight emissions attributed to freight, measured in tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent». Cargo flights come in later: «from the date of entry into force of this Regulation until 1 January 2028 the Agency should issue labels for passenger air transport services or mixed passenger-freight flights only, excluding all-cargo air transport services.» The Regulation enters into force as its last article states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.»

*Analytical inference:* air freight buyers will see labels first on mixed passenger-freight flights and, from 1 January 2028, on all-cargo flights; the label is shown by the airline at its points of sale, so a forwarder meets it as a reader of labels and possibly as a seller of flights. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder's online booking or quoting platform is a point of sale under the definition quoted in section 4.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight business within the next 30 days. The date that matters for cargo is the one in Article 9: «However, it shall apply to freight aircraft operators within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2023/2405 as from 1 January 2028.» That duty is the airline's, and the scheme itself is voluntary.

- An air-freight procurement lead adds to the next air carrier tender or rate review, and in any case before 1 January 2028, the question whether the carrier will apply for labels on its all-cargo flights, so the tender data can later be compared with the labels the Agency issues.
- A client-reporting lead decides, before 1 January 2028, whether freight emissions per tonne from a label may be quoted in client emissions reports, and records the label's own comparison basis next to each figure used.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the all-cargo date in Article 9 and on the label content in Annex III (section 8). The Regulation sets no fee, surcharge or rate on air freight. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder that quotes a label figure to a client is itself bound by the rule against labels that mimic the official ones, which the text addresses to aircraft operators.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names aircraft operators, the Agency and points of sale. A point of sale is defined broadly: «‘point of sale’ means a physical location or online platform service owned by an aircraft operator, or which offers the flights of an aircraft operator, where an aircraft operator, or any person authorised to represent that aircraft operator, stores and makes information available to the public about flights operated by that aircraft operator for purchase or comparison purposes.» The duty to make points of sale show labels sits with the airline: «the points of sale do not reject the display of labels nor recalculate the flight emissions estimated by the Agency for those aircraft operators, either for comparison or purchase purposes».

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder is not named; if its platform offers an airline's flights it may be a point of sale, and the airline must see that the label is shown and not recalculated. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder's platform that offers cargo space on an airline's flights counts as a point of sale, and which party answers if a label is not shown.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no authoritative guidance is held for this Regulation. The Regulation itself is the detailed rule under Article 14 of Regulation (EU) 2023/2405.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The text names one dated change: «Labels should cover all types of air transport services only as from 1 January 2028.» It also expects benchmarks from the Agency: «a benchmark to be developed by the Agency based on observed typical performance on the route or on comparable routes». The Agency reviews each operator's labels at least on a semi-annual basis: «The Agency shall review, at least on a semi-annual basis, for each aircraft operator for which labels were issued, whether the factors on the basis of which a label was issued for each flight or set of flights operated under the same conditions have changed.»

*Analytical inference:* the date of 1 January 2028 is the point at which all-cargo flights join the scheme; the text gives no date for the benchmark. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the benchmark has been published, which the captured text cannot show.

## 7. Threshold Questions

The question is which flights are labelled. The label is for flights of an operator that applies, and for cargo the answer changes in 2028: «excluding all-cargo air transport services». The text adds why: «Passenger and freight air transport services are inherently different in the way their operations are organised, and in particular, in their relations with final customers.» The scheme is open to operators in the scope of the parent Regulation: «open to all aircraft operators falling within the scope of that Regulation».

*Analytical inference:* before 1 January 2028 an all-cargo flight is outside the labels the Agency issues; a mixed passenger-freight flight may carry a label. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given flight on a client's route is an all-cargo flight or a mixed flight.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Application and reporting (Article 3). «An aircraft operator seeking the issuance of labels for its flights shall submit an application to the Agency, by 1 February of each year, through the dedicated module of the digital reporting tool.» «By 1 May of each year, the aircraft operators mentioned in paragraph 1 shall report, through the dedicated module of the digital reporting tool, the information listed in paragraphs 3 and 4 on their scheduled flights and on the operations carried out during the previous calendar year.»

Labels (Article 4). «it shall, by 30 June of each year: (a) estimate the flight emissions of each flight or set of flights, in accordance with Article 5».

Display (Article 6). «at the latest within 15 days following their receipt from the Agency in accordance with Article 4(1), point (c)». At sales partners: «the labels are displayed without any undue delay and the latest within 30 days following their receipt from the Agency in accordance with Article 4(1), point (c)». Look-alikes are barred: «not provide customers with or display labels, markers, symbols, or any equivalent form or inscriptions that mimic the labels issued under this Regulation and which do not comply with the requirements of this Regulation».

Content (Annex III). «for all-cargo flights, having regard to Article 9, the freight emissions per tonne, in kg CO2eq/t».

Consequence (Article 7). «If the Agency concludes, after carrying out the review, that a label is no longer appropriate or is not being correctly displayed by an aircraft operator, it shall decide, after giving the aircraft operator an opportunity to be heard, to revoke the existing label, or to issue a new label.»

*Analytical inference:* each duty above sits on an aircraft operator or on the Agency; the cost to an airline of a revoked label is the loss of the label, and the text states no fine, no fee and no pass-through to freight customers. No phase-in is stated in Articles 3, 4, 6 and 7 apart from the 2028 cargo date. No exceptions are stated in Articles 3 and 4. No scope limits are stated in Articles 3 and 4.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any of these display duties reaches a forwarder acting as a point of sale.

Obligations surveyed: 4; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 9.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets rules for airlines and the Agency, not for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Airlines register for the scheme by applying to the Agency each year (Article 3, quoted in section 8). Reporting runs through a tool the Agency manages: «‘digital reporting tool’ means a digital platform developed and managed by the Agency as the unique point of contact with aircraft operators for the reporting of data and for the distribution of labels». The public sees results on a website: «The Agency shall create and maintain a flight emissions website (the ‘website’) consisting of a public part with online access for the general public and a compliance part only to be accessed by aircraft operators.»

*Analytical inference:* the registration and reporting duties fall on aircraft operators, with the Agency running the tool; none on a forwarder is stated.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks airlines to build the reporting and display systems, and states no system for a freight business to build, unless its platform is a point of sale.

- A systems lead checks, before 1 January 2028, whether the business's booking or quoting platform offers any airline's flights, and if so notes which airline contracts name the platform as a point of sale.
- An air-freight pricing lead confirms with each airline partner at the next contract review that the platform will show the label unchanged and will not recalculate the flight emissions.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the point of sale definition and on Article 6(6), quoted in section 4. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether showing the label unchanged is required of the forwarder or only of the airline.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

All-cargo services are held back to 2028 (section 2). An operator may ask to end a label: «Aircraft operators may, under exceptional circumstances, request the Agency to terminate individual labels issued for flights or a set of flights whose operations have been discontinued or where a change in operational conditions during the scheduling period render the valid labels incorrect.» A late display can be excused once: «grant the aircraft operator a one-time exemption for the delay, alongside a new deadline».

*Analytical inference:* a label can end or be excused mid-period, so a figure seen in a tender may not match the label in force for the same route later. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a client may rely on a label figure after the operator has asked to end the label.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

*No content for this section as of November 2026: no adjacent industry research or alternative is held for this Regulation.*

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 18 December 2024: Regulation adopted at Brussels
- 1 January 2028: freight aircraft operators within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2023/2405 come under the Regulation

Each year: applications by 1 February, reports by 1 May, labels issued by 30 June. The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal; the text states no calendar date for that day.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «DIRECTIVE (EU) 2023/2864 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 December 2023 amending certain Directives as regards the establishment and functioning of the European single access point», a Union directive that changes the rules of many financial and company-reporting directives so that the information they already require to be published also goes to a national collection body and appears on one Union website. Its reach is set by its last article: «This Directive is addressed to the Member States.» Anything it says about issuers, undertakings and financial firms reaches them through national law. What the Directive states is quoted from its text; what it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Directive supports a Union website, the European single access point (ESAP), set up by Regulation (EU) 2023/2859. Its aim, in its recitals: «in order to provide the public with easy centralised access to information about entities and their products that is of relevance to financial services, capital markets and sustainability, which authorities and entities are required to publish pursuant to Union legislative acts in those fields.» The way it is to work: «Such publication should be carried out in accordance with a ‘file once’ principle and without entailing any additional disclosure requirements beyond those specified by law.» The roll-out is staged: «the scaling-up of the collection and submission of information needs to be gradual.»

The Directive enters into force as its Article 18 states: «This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union».

*Analytical inference:* this is reporting plumbing, not a freight rule. It adds a filing step to rules that already exist for listed issuers, for undertakings that publish management reports and financial statements, and for financial firms. A forwarder or shipper is not named in it. A freight business meets it only if it is itself an issuer or a reporting undertaking of the kinds the Directive names, or when it reads a counterparty's filings on ESAP.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: the Directive sets no step on a freight operator within the next 30 days. Its transposition date has passed: «Member States shall adopt and publish by 10 January 2026 the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with this Directive.» The date for the changes to the transparency rules passed too: «By way of derogation from paragraph 1 of this Article, Member States shall adopt and publish by 10 July 2025 the laws, regulations and administrative provisions necessary to comply with Article 3.» The next live step for a company that publishes annual reports is the date for the accounting rules: «From 10 January 2028, Member States shall ensure that, when making public the management report, consolidated management report»

- A finance lead at a business that publishes a management report or annual financial statements checks, before 10 January 2028, whether the business is one of the undertakings that Directive 2013/34/EU names in Articles 19a, 29a and 40a, and asks the national collection body how filings are to be sent.

- A compliance lead, from 10 January 2028, looks up a customer's or supplier's filed reports on ESAP at the next counterparty review instead of asking the counterparty for a copy.

*Analytical inference:* the first step rests on the same-time submission duty in Section 8; the second rests on the aim to give the public central access to filings. The Directive requires neither step of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an undertaking referred to in Articles 19a, 29a or 40a of Directive 2013/34/EU, or an issuer under Directive 2004/109/EC.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Directive names the Member States, the issuer, the undertaking that makes reports public, the collection body, the competent authority and ESMA. For listed issuers the duty reads: «the issuer or the person who has applied for admission to trading on a regulated market without the issuer’s consent shall submit that regulated information at the same time to the collection body referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article for the purpose of making it accessible on the European single access point (ESAP)» The Member State picks the body that receives the filing: «the collection body as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 shall be the officially appointed mechanism designated under Article 21(2) of this Directive.»

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder or shipper is not named. A freight business sits in the chain only as an issuer or as a reporting undertaking, and then the Member State ensures the submission; the Directive does not state a duty on a customer or supplier of that business. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business falls in either role under national law.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Later steps are set by the text. Member States name the body that collects accounting filings: «By 9 January 2028, for the purpose of making the information referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article accessible on ESAP, Member States shall designate at least one collection body as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 and notify ESMA thereof.» Financial-sector steps follow: «By 9 January 2030, for the purpose of making the information referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article accessible on ESAP, Member States shall designate at least one collection body as defined in Article 2, point (2), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 and notify ESMA thereof.» And: «From 10 January 2030, Member States shall ensure that the information referred to in Article 15 of this Directive is made accessible on ESAP.» The Commission fills in the technical detail: «the Commission shall be empowered to adopt implementing measures to specify: (a) any other metadata to accompany the information; (b) the structuring of data in the information; (c) for which information a machine-readable format is required and, in such cases, which machine-readable format is to be used.» «Where necessary, the Commission shall adopt guidelines to ensure that the metadata submitted in accordance with paragraph 5, point (a), are correct.»

*Analytical inference:* the 2028 date is the one that touches companies that publish management reports; the 2030 dates concern financial-sector filings. The Commission's implementing measures have no date in the text, so the exact format for machine-readable filings is open.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Issuers. «From 10 July 2026, Member States shall ensure that, when disclosing regulated information referred to in Article 21(1) of this Directive, the issuer or the person who has applied for admission to trading on a regulated market without the issuer’s consent shall submit that regulated information at the same time to the collection body referred to in paragraph 3 of this Article for the purpose of making it accessible on the European single access point (ESAP)»

Undertakings with management reports and financial statements. «From 10 January 2028, Member States shall ensure that, when making public the management report, consolidated management report, including for both reports the information required in Article 8 of Regulation (EU) 2020/852, as well as the annual financial statements, consolidated financial statements, audit report, assurance report, sustainability reports concerning third-country undertakings and related assurance opinion, the statement referred to in Article 40a(2), fourth subparagraph, of this Directive, the report on payments to governments, and the consolidated report on payments to governments referred to in Article 30, Article 40d and Article 45 of this Directive, the undertakings referred to in Articles 19a, 29a and40a of this Directive submit those statements and reports at the same time to the collection body»

Form of the filing. «(a) be submitted in a data extractable format as defined in Article 2, point (3), of Regulation (EU) 2023/2859 or, where required by Union or national law, in a machine-readable format, as defined in Article 2, point (4), of that Regulation;» Each filing carries an identifier and a note on the reporting entity: «(i) all the names of the undertaking to which the information relates and, where the reporting undertaking is an exempted subsidiary undertaking as referred to in Article 29a(4), second subparagraph, the name of the parent undertaking that reports information at group level;» «For the purposes of paragraph 1, point (b)(ii), Member States shall ensure that undertakings obtain a legal entity identifier.»

Filing already made elsewhere. «Where an undertaking has submitted the information referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article to an Officially Appointed Mechanism pursuant to Article 23a of Directive 2004/109/EC in order to make that information accessible on ESAP, that undertaking shall be deemed to have fulfilled its obligations under paragraph 1 of this Article, provided that this information complies with all requirements on metadata set out in paragraph 1 of this Article.»

*No penalty: the source states no penalty, fine or enforcement consequence; enforcement sits with national law.*

*Analytical inference:* each duty falls on the Member State to ensure, and through it on the issuer or undertaking that files; the Directive states no cost, fee or freight rate effect, so any cost to a business is a gap. No scope limits are stated in Articles 23a and 33a as inserted beyond the cross-references to the undertakings and information they name.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether, and from which date, the business must send its annual report to a national collection body under the Member State's law.

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The reporting duties are on Member States, issuers and undertakings. On national law: «They shall immediately communicate the text of those measures to the Commission.» «Member States shall communicate to the Commission the text of the main measures of national law which they adopt in the field covered by this Directive.» On identifiers: «For the purposes of paragraph 1, point (b)(ii), Member States shall require issuers to obtain a legal entity identifier.» On what must go with each filing: «(v) the type of information, as classified pursuant to Article 7(4), point (c), of that Regulation; (vi) an indication of whether the information contains personal data.»

*Analytical inference:* a legal entity identifier is needed by an issuer or reporting undertaking before the first filing; the text states no registration of a forwarder as such.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Directive asks issuers and reporting undertakings to be able to file at the same time as they publish, in a data extractable format, with an identifier and metadata (Section 8). No step is due from a freight operator that is neither.

- A finance lead at a business that publishes an annual report asks, ahead of 10 January 2028, the person who prepares the report to confirm that it can be produced in a data extractable format and that the business holds a legal entity identifier.

- A data lead at a business that already files regulated information in a Member State checks, at the next filing date, whether the filing already goes to the officially appointed mechanism, because the Directive treats that as meeting the accounting-rule filing duty if the metadata is complete.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the format and identifier duties and the deemed-fulfilment rule in Section 8; the text states no data a forwarder must keep as a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an issuer or a reporting undertaking.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

The Directive also allows voluntary filing: «any entity governed by the law of a Member State should be able to submit to a collection body, on a voluntary basis, information about its economic activities that is of relevance to financial services or capital markets, or that concerns sustainability»

*Analytical inference:* voluntary submission is open to any entity governed by the law of a Member State and is an option, not a duty, for a freight business.

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2024/1679 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 June 2024 on Union guidelines for the development of the trans-European transport network», the Union rule that sets what the European rail, inland waterway, port, road, airport and terminal network must look like and by when. Its jurisdictional scope is the Union: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» The subject matter: «This Regulation establishes guidelines for the development of a trans-European transport network consisting of a comprehensive network and of a core network and extended core network, with the core network and extended core network to be established on the basis of the comprehensive network.» What the Regulation says is taken from its own text. What it may mean for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation is an infrastructure rule: it tells Member States what to build and maintain, in three nested networks. The scope: «This Regulation applies to the trans-European transport network as specified in the maps set out in Annex I and in the lists in Annex II.» The modes it covers: «The infrastructure of the trans-European transport network consists of the infrastructure for railway transport, inland waterway transport, maritime transport, road transport, air transport and multimodal transport, including in urban nodes, as laid down in the relevant sections of Chapters II, III and IV.» The three steps and their dates: «(a) the completion of a core network by 31 December 2030; (b) the completion of an extended core network by 31 December 2040; and, (c) the completion of a comprehensive network by 31 December 2050.» The corridors that matter most for freight flows are defined: «The European Transport Corridors shall consist of the parts of the core network or extended core network which are of the highest strategic importance for the development of sustainable and multimodal freight and passenger transport flows in Europe and for the development of interoperable high-quality infrastructure and operational performance.» The Regulation enters into force as Article 69 states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union.» It replaces the earlier rule: «Regulation (EU) No 1315/2013 is repealed with effect from 18 July 2024.»

*Analytical inference:* the duties sit on Member States and public bodies, but the dates tell a freight business when a line, terminal, port or road it uses is meant to reach a standard. The text states no freight rate, surcharge or cost.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step in the Regulation falls on a freight operator within the next 30 days, and the text states no cost or penalty for one. The nearest dated steps ahead fall on Member States in 2027: «By 19 July 2027, Member States shall notify the Commission of the lines concerned.» and «By 19 July 2027, Member States shall conduct a market and prospective analysis on multimodal freight terminals on their territory.»

- A rail-freight product lead lists, before 19 July 2027 and at the next annual route review, the lines on the routes the business sells that are core network lines or that match one of the three conditions for comprehensive network lines (a terminal or port link to the core freight network, a re-routing line, or more than ten freight trains a day), because those are the lines for which the 740 m train length and 22,5 tonne axle load apply and, for the comprehensive network lines only, which Member States notify under Article 15(3).
- A multimodal-terminal lead asks, before 19 July 2027, the terminal operators the business uses for the Member State's market and prospective analysis on multimodal freight terminals, and records which of its terminals are listed in Annex II.
- A rail-freight customer-service lead writes the target values for rail freight (25 minutes average dwell time at internal cross-border sections, with listed exceptions, and 75 % of trains within 30 minutes of schedule, both by 31 December 2030) into the service section of the next rail rate agreement, because the Rail Freight governance is to make all possible efforts to meet them.

*Analytical inference:* the three steps rest on the line notification, the terminal analysis and the Article 19 targets in Section 8. The Regulation requires none of them of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular line, terminal or corridor of a client's route is in the maps of Annex I and the lists of Annex II.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names Member States, the Commission, European Coordinators of each corridor, infrastructure managers, railway undertakings, the Rail Freight governance, operators of locks, local authorities and terminals open to all operators. The coordinators have a task: «Each European Coordinator of the European Transport Corridors and the two horizontal priorities shall draw up, at the latest by 19 July 2026 and every four years thereafter, a work plan». The terminal requirements are written for terminals described as «which are open to all operators and users in non-discriminatory way and apply transparent and non-discriminatory charges». A forwarder is not named.

*Analytical inference:* a freight business sits outside the named compliance chain; it is a user of the terminals, lines, ports and roads the Member States must provide, and the terminal requirements cover terminals that are open to all operators and users on non-discriminatory terms. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a terminal the business uses is open to all operators and users in the sense of the Regulation.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No content for this section: no authoritative guidance document on this Regulation is held.*

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Regulation sets dated follow-up steps for the Commission and the coordinators. The implementing act on urban mobility data: «No later than by 19 July 2025, the Commission shall adopt an implementing act:» Studies and plans: «the Commission shall carry out a study to identify possibilities for short-notice large-scale movements across the Union». Climate: «By 19 July 2026, the Commission, in close cooperation with the Member States concerned, shall carry out an assessment of the resilience and vulnerability of the core network to the consequences of climate change». The review looks ahead to the later deadlines: «the Commission shall evaluate whether the extended core network and the comprehensive network as provided for in this Regulation is likely to comply with Chapters II, III and IV by the deadlines of 31 December 2040 and 31 December 2050, as applicable» and it starts with the core network: «By 31 December 2033, the Commission, having consulted with Member States as appropriate and with the assistance of the European Coordinators, shall carry out an assessment of the implementation of the core network, evaluating in particular its compliance with the requirements of this Regulation.» The power to adopt delegated acts is time-limited: «The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 11(3) and Article 58(1) and (5) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 18 July 2024.»

*Analytical inference:* the dates in 2025 and 2026 have passed; the 2033 review is the point at which the Commission judges whether the 2040 and 2050 deadlines are likely to be met. The text states no content for these outputs beyond what is quoted. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Commission has published the 2025 study and the 2026 climate assessment.

## 7. Threshold Questions

One threshold decides which comprehensive-network rail lines carry the freight train length requirement: «The requirements set out in paragraph 2, points (b) and (c), shall apply only on those lines of the comprehensive network which: (a) connect a multimodal freight terminal or a maritime or an inland port with its closest crossing point with the core freight network or extended core freight network;» The other two conditions: «(b) constitute a re-routing line of a line that is part of the core freight network or extended core freight network; or (c) operate more than ten freight trains per day on average in both directions based on the data for the previous year prior to the notification.»

*Analytical inference:* a comprehensive-network line that none of the three conditions describes does not carry the 740 m and 22,5 tonne requirement on this wording. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a line a client uses is notified by the Member State under these conditions.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Scope. «This Regulation applies to the trans-European transport network as specified in the maps set out in Annex I and in the lists in Annex II.»

Rail. «Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December 2050, the railway infrastructure of the comprehensive network, except connections referred to in Article 14(1), point (d): (a) is fully electrified as regards line tracks and, to the extent necessary for electric train operations, as regards sidings; (b) enables, without special permission, an axle load of at least 22,5 tonnes; and (c) enables, without special permission, the operation of freight trains with a train length of at least 740 m (including the locomotive or locomotives).» «Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December 2030, the railway infrastructure of the core network, except connections referred to in Article 14(1), point (d): (a) for lines that are part of the network for freight transport: meets the requirements set out in paragraph (2), points (a), (b) and (c) of this Article;» «(i) on double track lines, at least one train path per two hours and direction and not less than 24 train paths on daily basis, can be allocated to freight trains with a length of at least 740 m if requested by a railway undertaking;» «Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December 2040, lines for freight transport that are part of the railway infrastructure of the core network or extended core network, including connections referred to in Article 14(1), point (d), allow for the circulation of freight trains carrying standard semi-trailers up to 4 m high, loaded at a height of at least 27 cm above the top of the rail track on the European Transport Corridors on their territories.» «Member States shall ensure that class B systems are decommissioned, no later than by 31 December 2040 on the core network, by 31 December 2045 on the extended core network and by 31 December 2050 on the comprehensive network, provided that an appropriate level of safety is ensured». «ERTMS is equipped on the railway infrastructure of the extended core network by 31 December 2040 and the comprehensive network by 31 December 2050».

Rail freight service. «The Rail Freight governance shall make all possible efforts to ensure by 31 December 2030, that, on the European Transport Corridors, the quality of services provided to railway undertakings and technical and operational requirements for infrastructure use do not prevent the operational performance of rail freight services along the European Transport Corridors from meeting the following target values: (a) for each internal cross-border section, the dwelling time of all freight trains crossing the border between two Member States does not exceed 25 minutes on average,» «at least 75 % of the freight trains crossing at least one border along a European Transport Corridor arrive at their destination, or at the external Union border if their destination is outside the Union, at their scheduled time or with a delay of less than 30 minutes».

Inland waterways and ports. «Member States shall by 31 December 2030 in particular ensure that: (a) rivers, canals, lakes, lagoons, inland ports and their access routes provide a navigable channel depth of at least 2,5 m and a minimum height under non-openable bridges of at least 5,25 m». «Member States shall ensure that the maritime transport infrastructure of the core network meets the requirements set out in Article 26(2) by 31 December 2030.» «Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December 2050: (a) maritime ports of the comprehensive network with a total annual cargo volume of more than 2 million tonnes are connected with the rail and road infrastructure and, where possible, inland waterways;»

Road and air. «Member States shall ensure that the road infrastructure meets the requirements set out in Article 30(3): (a) for the existing infrastructure of the core network, by 31 December 2025, and for the existing infrastructure of the extended core network, by 31 December 2030;» «Member States shall ensure that, by 31 December 2050, the roads referred in Article 29(1), point (a), of the comprehensive network meet the following requirements: (a) the road is specially designed, built or upgraded for motor traffic; (b) rest areas are available at a maximum distance of 100 km from each other, providing safe and sufficient parking space, and appropriate facilities». «Member States shall, by 31 December 2040, ensure the development of safe and secure parking areas along the roads of the core network and extended core network, or within 3 km driving distance from the nearest exit of the road of the trans-European network, with an average maximum distance of 150 km between two such areas, providing sufficient parking space for commercial vehicles». «(g) the airports of the core network and comprehensive network with a total annual passenger traffic volume of more than four million passengers provide infrastructure for pre-conditioned air supply to stationary aircraft at aircraft contact stands used for commercial transport operations by 31 December 2030 for airports of the core network and 31 December 2040 for airports of the comprehensive network.»

Multimodal freight terminals. «Member States shall make all possible efforts to ensure in a fair and non-discriminatory manner that all multimodal freight terminals, which are open to all operators and users in non-discriminatory way and apply transparent and non-discriminatory charges in maritime ports and inland ports as listed in Annex II and in all rail road terminals and terminals along inland waterways specified in the maps set out in Annex I and listed in Annex II, meet the following requirements:» «(b) they are, by 31 December 2030, equipped inside the terminal or within the 3 km distance from the terminal with at least one recharging station, as defined in Article 2, point (52), of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 dedicated to serve heavy-duty vehicles». «shall be able to accommodate 740 m long trains without manipulation or, if this is not economically viable, that adequate measures are taken to improve the operational efficiency of accommodating 740 m long trains by 31 December 2040.»

*Analytical inference:* the infrastructure requirements above are duties of the Member States; the terminal items are an obligation to make all possible efforts, and the rail freight service items are targets the Rail Freight governance is to make all possible efforts to meet, as the text words them; the Regulation states no duty, cost or price effect for a freight business. No phase-in is stated beyond the three network steps and the dated requirements above. The text of the rail and road requirements is in Articles 15, 16, 18, 19, 30 and 31.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* which Member State has notified which lines, and how each Member State has set the requirements into national law and plans.

Obligations surveyed: 30; workspace-adjacent: 20; extracted as FACT: 19.
Shortfall: the extracted obligations are the freight-facing ones; urban nodes, resilience, military mobility, accessibility and safety obligations are surveyed but not extracted.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section: the Regulation sets infrastructure requirements for Member States, not a product a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

The Regulation sets no registration obligation on a freight business. Reporting items run between Member States and the Commission, and one is public. Member States notify lines: «By 19 July 2027, Member States shall notify the Commission of the lines concerned.» Member States publish water data: «Member States shall publish on a website accessible to the public the number of days per year as referred to in point (a) during which the actual water level exceeds or does not achieve the specified reference water level for navigation channel depth, as well as the average waiting times at each lock». Delay in completion is reported on request: «In the event of significant delay in starting or completing work on the core network, extended core network and the comprehensive network compared to the initial expected timeline set out in implementing acts referred to in Article 55, the Commission may ask the Member State or Member States concerned to provide the reasons for the delay.» The Commission may then respond: «provide the Member States concerned with recommendations with a view to eliminating that delay and preventing or reducing further delays.»

*Analytical inference:* the published water and lock waiting data are the items a freight business can read; the other reporting steps run between Member States and the Commission. *Legal Confirmation Required:* where each Member State publishes the water level and lock waiting data.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks a freight business to build no system and states no cost or penalty. Two steps keep the business ready for the dated requirements. A rail-freight product lead records, at the next rate book update, whether each rail corridor in the offer allows freight trains with standard semi-trailers up to 4 m high, because Member States must allow it on the European Transport Corridors by 31 December 2040. A road-freight planning lead records, at the next review of terminal contracts, which terminals the business uses within 3 km of a recharging station for heavy-duty vehicles, because Member States are to make all possible efforts to equip terminals with such a station by 31 December 2030.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the dated rail and terminal requirements in Section 8; the Regulation requires neither of a forwarder. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a terminal contract of the business carries any term on these requirements.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Exemptions are made for places without railways and for particular parts of the network. Railways and terminals: «The provisions relating to railways, and in particular any requirement to connect airports and ports to railways, as well as the provisions related to multimodal freight terminals shall not apply to Cyprus, Malta, islands and outermost regions for as long as no railway system is established within their territory.» Parking and track gauge: «The provisions relating to safe and secure parking shall not apply to Cyprus, Malta, islands and outermost regions.» «The provisions related to European standard nominal track gauge of 1 435 mm for rail in Article 17 shall not apply to Ireland, islands and outermost regions.» Isolated rail networks: «The requirements set out in paragraphs 2 and 4 shall not apply to isolated networks.» The track gauge rule has dated steps: «That requirement is considered to be met when 1 435 mm track gauge trains can circulate on the infrastructure by 31 December 2030 for the core network and by 31 December 2040 for the extended core network.» Member States with a different gauge plan their migration: «Member States with an existing rail network, or a part thereof, with a track gauge different from that of the European standard nominal track gauge of 1 435 mm shall carry out an assessment, by 19 July 2026, identifying the existing railway lines located on the European Transport Corridors in view of their possible migration to the European standard nominal track gauge of 1 435 mm.» That date has passed.

*Analytical inference:* a route to or across Cyprus, Malta, an island or an outermost region may not carry the rail, terminal or parking requirements on this wording, and Ireland is outside the track gauge rule. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which exemptions a Member State has requested or been granted for a route a client uses.

## 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

The Regulation links the network to climate and defence aims. The recital: «sets a climate neutrality objective to be achieved by the Union by 2050, as well as a clear objective to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55 % by 2030, compared to 1990 levels». The study on defence movements is in Section 6: «the Commission shall carry out a study to identify possibilities for short-notice large-scale movements across the Union».

## 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

The Regulation is dated by its closing line: «Done at Brussels, 13 June 2024.» It is the base for every deadline below.

- 13 June 2024: Regulation adopted
- 18 July 2024: earlier network rule repealed and the five year delegation period starts (date passed)
- 19 July 2025: Commission implementing act on urban mobility indicators and a Commission study due (date passed)
- 31 December 2025: existing core network roads to meet the Article 30(3) requirement (date passed)
- 19 July 2026: coordinators' work plans, Member State track gauge assessment and Commission climate assessment due (date passed)
- 19 July 2027: Member States notify rail lines and conduct the multimodal freight terminal analysis
- 31 December 2030: core network to be completed; rail, port, waterway and road requirements fall due on Member States, while the terminal and rail freight service items are targets that Member States and the Rail Freight governance make all possible efforts to meet

   "body": "## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document covers «REGULATION (EU) 2025/14 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 19 December 2024 on the approval and market surveillance of non-road mobile machinery circulating on public roads and amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 (Text with EEA relevance)», the European Union rule that sets one approval system for work machines driven on public roads. Its subject: «This Regulation lays down technical requirements, administrative requirements and procedures for EU type-approval, EU individual approval, and placing on the market of all new non-road mobile machinery intended to circulate on public roads.» Its reach: «This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.» What the Regulation requires is stated from its own text; what it means for a freight business is marked *Analytical inference:* and each point for counsel is marked *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Regulation covers self-propelled work machines that drive on public roads: «‘non-road mobile machinery’ means self-propelled mobile machinery with a propulsion system, falling within the scope of Directive 2006/42/EC, that is designed and constructed for the purpose of performing work». Its scope reads: «This Regulation applies to non-road mobile machinery (‘U-category vehicles’) where it is placed on the market and intended to circulate, whether occasionally or regularly, with or without a driver, on a public road.» Early approvals start sooner than the full rule: «From 28 January 2025, national authorities may grant EU type-approval for a new type of non-road mobile machinery or EU individual approval for new non-road mobile machinery». The Regulation enters into force as its last article states: «This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union .» and applies later: «This Regulation shall apply from 29 January 2028.»

*Analytical inference:* machines of this kind are cargo for a freight business, and the duties fall on manufacturers, importers and distributors, not on a carrier or forwarder as such. The nearest links are the importer and distributor duties on conformity and the rule on transport conditions in section 8. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a forwarder or customs broker that brings machinery into the Union for a client counts as an importer.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

MONITORING: no step falls on a freight business within the next 30 days. The Regulation applies from «29 January 2028», and the Commission is to set the model for the statutory plate before then: «The Commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down the model for the statutory plate with marking of non-road mobile machinery.» «The first such implementing acts shall be adopted by 29 July 2027.»

- A trade-compliance lead lists, before 29 January 2028, the self-propelled work machines that the business ships to the Union or stores there for clients, and notes for each whether it is meant to be driven on public roads.
- A contracts lead asks, at the next machinery-transport or storage contract renewal and before 29 January 2028, the client or importer to state who is the importer and who holds the certificate of conformity for each machine.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on the scope in Article 2 and on the importer and distributor duties in Articles 10 to 12 (section 8). The Regulation sets no fee, surcharge or rate on freight. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the business is an importer or a distributor for any machine it handles, which depends on its own role in placing the machine on the market.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Regulation names four economic operators. «‘importer’ means a natural or legal person established in the Union who places on the market non-road mobile machinery that has been manufactured in a third country». «‘distributor’ means a dealer or any other natural or legal person in the supply chain, other than the manufacturer or the importer, who makes available on the market non-road mobile machinery». «‘economic operator’ means the manufacturer, the manufacturer’s representative for market surveillance, the importer or the distributor». Supply is defined by commercial activity: «‘making available on the market’ means any supply of non-road mobile machinery for distribution or use on the market in the course of a commercial activity, whether in return for payment or free of charge».

*Analytical inference:* a forwarder and a carrier are not named. The distributor definition reaches any person in the supply chain who supplies machinery in the course of a commercial activity, so a business that sells or hands over machinery in its own name could fall inside it, while one that only moves the machinery for the owner may not. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which of the four roles, if any, a freight business takes for a given consignment.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

The Commission must adopt implementing acts on the plate: «The Commission shall adopt implementing acts laying down the model for the statutory plate with marking of non-road mobile machinery.» «The first such implementing acts shall be adopted by 29 July 2027.» It also holds delegated powers for a term: «for a period of 5 years from 28 January 2025». It must set threshold values for machines too heavy or wide to circulate: «The Commission shall adopt implementing acts setting out those threshold values in accordance with that methodology.» Member States report to the Commission: «By 29 January 2032, Member States shall inform the Commission of the following». The Commission then reports: «By 29 January 2033, the Commission shall present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council on the implementation of this Regulation, accompanied, where appropriate, by relevant legislative proposals.»

*Analytical inference:* the implementing acts due by 29 July 2027 fix the model of the statutory plate that EU type-approved machines must carry from 29 January 2028; the threshold values decide which heavy or wide machines a Member State may keep off the road. The text states no outcome for the 2033 report. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the implementing acts due by 29 July 2027 have been adopted, which the captured text cannot show.

## 7. Threshold Questions

Several limits decide whether a machine is inside. Speed: «non-road mobile machinery with a maximum design speed exceeding 40 km/h» and «non-road mobile machinery with a maximum design speed not exceeding 6 km/h» are outside. Seats: «non-road mobile machinery equipped with more than three seating positions, including the driver’s seating position» is outside. Age: «non-road mobile machinery that was placed on the market, registered or entered into service before 29 January 2028» is outside. Carrying goods: «machinery, as defined in Article 2, point (a), of Directive 2006/42/EC, primarily intended for the transport of one or more persons, animals or goods other than instruments or auxiliaries required for the performance of work, materials resulting from or necessary for work or for intermediate storage, or materials transported on construction sites» is outside.

*Analytical inference:* a machine whose main job is to carry goods is outside the Regulation, as are slow, fast, many-seat and older machines. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a particular machine on a client's consignment meets one of these exclusions.

## 8. Substantive Requirements

Manufacturers (Article 7). «Manufacturers shall ensure that the non-road mobile machinery they place on the market either belongs to a type that has been granted an EU type-approval and is designed and manufactured in accordance with that type or has been granted an EU individual approval.»

Importers (Articles 10 and 11). «Importers shall ensure that non-road mobile machinery that they place on the market either belongs to a type that has been granted an EU type-approval and conforms to that type or has been granted an EU individual approval.» «Importers shall not make available on the market non-road mobile machinery that is not in conformity with the requirements laid down in this Regulation, until such machinery has been brought into conformity.»

Distributors (Article 12). «that the EU type-approved non-road mobile machinery bears the statutory plate with marking required by this Regulation» and «that a certificate of conformity accompanies the EU type-approved non-road mobile machinery». On handling: «Distributors shall ensure that, while EU type-approved or EU individually approved non-road mobile machinery is under their responsibility, storage or transport conditions do not jeopardise its conformity with this Regulation.»

Traceability (Article 15). «Economic operators shall, on request, identify to the approval authorities and market surveillance authorities, for a period of 10 years after the placing on the market of non-road mobile machinery, the following: (a) any economic operator who has supplied them with non-road mobile machinery; (b) any economic operator to whom they have supplied non-road mobile machinery.»

Member States (Article 5). «Member States shall only permit the making available on the market, registration, entry into service or circulation on public roads of non-road mobile machinery that complies with this Regulation.»

Penalties (Article 53). «Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation and shall take all measures necessary to ensure that they are implemented. The penalties provided for shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.» The infringements include «economic operators making available on the market or entering into service non-road mobile machinery subject to approval without such approval or falsifying documents or markings with that intention».

*Analytical inference:* the duties on importers and distributors are the ones that can reach the freight chain, and the transport-conditions duty in Article 12(3) is addressed to distributors for machinery under their responsibility. The text states no amount of fine, no rate and no pass-through to freight customers. No phase-in is stated in Articles 7, 10, 11, 12 and 15 beyond the application date of 29 January 2028. No exceptions are stated in Articles 10, 11 and 15. No scope limits are stated in Articles 10, 11 and 15.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight business that stores or moves machinery for a client is a distributor under Article 12, and whether Article 12(3) then reaches its handling.

## 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*No content for this section as of November 2026: the Regulation sets approval rules for machinery, not rules for products a freight business sells.*

## 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

Approval rests on documents that travel with the machine. «The manufacturer shall issue a certificate of conformity to accompany each non-road mobile machinery that is manufactured in conformity with the EU type-approved non-road mobile machinery.» «The certificate of conformity shall be delivered free of charge to the user together with the non-road mobile machinery.» For makers outside the Union: «manufacturers established outside the Union shall appoint a single representative established within the Union». Member States set up the authorities: «Member States shall establish or appoint the authorities competent in matters concerning approval and market surveillance in accordance with this Regulation.» They report their penalty rules: «Member States shall, by 28 January 2028, notify the Commission of those rules and of those measures».

*Analytical inference:* the certificate of conformity and the statutory plate are the documents a customs or storage desk would see with an approved machine; the registration and reporting duties fall on manufacturers, importers, distributors and Member States, and none on a forwarder as such is stated.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

MONITORING: the Regulation asks manufacturers, importers and distributors to build the document and traceability systems, and states no system for a freight business to build unless it takes one of those roles.

- A documentation lead adds a field for the statutory plate and the certificate of conformity to the machine intake record, before 29 January 2028, so a missing document is caught when the machine arrives.
- A trade-compliance lead records, for each machine the business supplies in its own name after 29 January 2028, the party that supplied it and the party it was supplied to, since economic operators must identify both on request for 10 years.

*Analytical inference:* both steps rest on Article 12(2) and Article 15, quoted in section 8. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the record-keeping step applies to the business at all, which depends on whether it is an economic operator.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

Some machines may skip EU approval. «For the following non-road mobile machinery, the manufacturer may decide to apply for the EU type-approval, to apply for the EU individual approval or to comply with the relevant national law, where appropriate:» includes «non-road mobile machinery where the number of units per type does not exceed 70 per year and in each Member State» and «non-road mobile machinery designed and constructed for use principally in quarries, ports or airport facilities». A transition runs for years: «By way of derogation from this Regulation, until 29 January 2036, Member States may apply any national law on national type-approval of non-road mobile machinery for circulation on public roads to non-road mobile machinery that is placed on the market between 29 January 2028 and 29 January 2036.» A Member State may keep a machine off the road: «due to its excessive dimensions, the machinery would not allow for sufficient manoeuvrability on public roads».

*Analytical inference:* machines made for ports or airport facilities follow the manufacturer's choice of EU approval or national law, and the national route runs to 29 January 2036. *Legal Confirmation Required:* which route a given machine takes, since it depends on the manufacturer's choice.
